# Codebase Memory — Knowledge Graph Tools

Graph tools return precise structural results in ~500 tokens vs ~80K for grep.

## Quick Decision Matrix

| Question | Tool call |
|----------|----------|
| Who calls X? | `trace_path(direction="inbound")` |
| What does X call? | `trace_path(direction="outbound")` |
| Full call context | `trace_path(direction="both")` |
| Find by name pattern | `search_graph(name_pattern="...")` |
| Dead code | `search_graph(max_degree=0, exclude_entry_points=true)` |
| Cross-service edges | `query_graph` with Cypher |
| Impact of local changes | `detect_changes()` |
| Risk-classified trace | `trace_path(risk_labels=true)` |
| Text search | `search_code` or Grep |

## Exploration Workflow
1. `list_projects` — check if project is indexed
2. `get_graph_schema` — understand node/edge types
3. `search_graph(label="Function", name_pattern=".*Pattern.*")` — find code
4. `get_code_snippet(qualified_name="project.path.FuncName")` — read source

## Tracing Workflow
1. `search_graph(name_pattern=".*FuncName.*")` — discover exact name
2. `trace_path(function_name="FuncName", direction="both", depth=3)` — trace
3. `detect_changes()` — map git diff to affected symbols

## Evidence Tiers
- **Scout (Tier 1):** fast positive lookup with few graph calls and targeted source checks. Treat results as provisional; never make absence, exhaustive, dead-code, or complete-impact claims.
- **Verify (Tier 2, default):** task-directed searches, relevant trace directions, exact snippets for material claims, and all relevant result pages.
- **Auditor (Tier 3):** bounded-scope full verification with a current graph generation, complete relevant pagination, both call directions and broader relationships when material, plus explicit unresolved limitations.
- **Every tier:** after candidate paths are known, call `check_index_coverage` once with every evidence path. For negative or exhaustive claims also include the relevant scopes. A clean result means no recorded gap, not proof of completeness. For partial, skipped, excluded, stale, pending, or unknown coverage, read/grep the reported ranges or scope before relying on the graph.

## Sessions and Subagents
- At session start or after compaction, call `list_projects`/`index_status` before structural exploration, then choose Scout, Verify, or Auditor for the task.
- Before delegating, query the graph and coverage in the parent. Pass the tier, exact project, generation/freshness, bounded scope, queries and pagination state, qualified symbols, paths, call-chain findings, coverage ranges/reasons, source fallback already performed, and unresolved questions to the child.
- Runtimes such as Hermes isolate child context: put those graph findings in the `context` argument to `delegate_task`; do not assume the child inherits MCP access or the parent's conversation.
- A child without MCP tools must not call or claim MCP access. It should work from the supplied evidence and use read/grep on exact source, especially every reported missed-coverage range.

## Quality Analysis
- Dead code: `search_graph(max_degree=0, exclude_entry_points=true)`
- High fan-out: `search_graph(min_degree=10, relationship="CALLS", direction="outbound")`
- High fan-in: `search_graph(min_degree=10, relationship="CALLS", direction="inbound")`

## 15 MCP Tools
`index_repository`, `index_status`, `list_projects`, `delete_project`,
`search_graph`, `search_code`, `trace_path`, `detect_changes`,
`query_graph`, `get_graph_schema`, `get_code_snippet`, `get_architecture`,
`check_index_coverage`, `manage_adr`, `ingest_traces`

## Edge Types
CALLS, HTTP_CALLS, ASYNC_CALLS, DATA_FLOWS, IMPORTS, DEFINES, DEFINES_METHOD,
HANDLES, IMPLEMENTS, OVERRIDE, USAGE, CALL_REFERENCE, CONFIGURES, FILE_CHANGES_WITH,
SIMILAR_TO, SEMANTICALLY_RELATED, CONTAINS_FILE, CONTAINS_FOLDER,
CONTAINS_PACKAGE

## Cypher Examples (for query_graph)
```
MATCH (a)-[r:HTTP_CALLS]->(b) RETURN a.name, b.name, r.url_path, r.confidence LIMIT 20
MATCH (f:Function) WHERE f.name =~ '.*Handler.*' RETURN f.name, f.file_path
MATCH (a)-[r:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name = 'main' RETURN b.name
```

## Gotchas
1. `search_graph(relationship="HTTP_CALLS")` filters nodes by degree — use `query_graph` with Cypher to see actual edges.
2. `query_graph` has a 100k row ceiling — add a Cypher `LIMIT` for broad queries or use `search_graph` pagination.
3. `trace_path` needs exact names — use `search_graph(name_pattern=...)` first.
4. `direction="outbound"` misses cross-service callers — use `direction="both"`.
5. `search_graph` results default to 50 per page — check `has_more` and use `offset`.

   246	class TurnDiagnostics:
   247	    """Samples a running turn so a timeout can be attributed to a cause.
   248	
   249	    Usage mirrors the shims' existing shape::
   250	
   251	        diag = TurnDiagnostics(worktree=run_cwd)
   252	        diag.start()
   253	        try:
   254	            subprocess.run(..., timeout=turn_timeout)
   255	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
   256	            bounded_rc = 7
   257	        finally:
   258	            diag.stop()
   259	        if bounded_rc == 7:
   260	            reason, detail = diag.classify()
   261	    """
   262	
   263	    def __init__(self, worktree: str | None = None, interval: float = DEFAULT_INTERVAL_S,
   264	                 root_pid: int | None = None):
   265	        self.worktree = worktree
   266	        self.interval = interval
   267	        # GH-492: a turn shim IS the process tree it measures, so its own pid is the right default.
   268	        # A consult is not: it launches every advisor as a sibling under one parent, so measuring
   269	        # `os.getpid()` there sums ALL advisors and one busy model masks another's hang. Passing the
   270	        # advisor's own pid scopes the CPU reading to that advisor's subtree.
   271	        self.root_pid = root_pid if root_pid is not None else os.getpid()
   272	        self._stop = threading.Event()
   273	        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None
   274	        # Sticky once CONFIRMED: a dialog that blocked the turn and was then
   275	        # dismissed still explains the stall, so this is never cleared. It is
   276	        # only set after DIALOG_CONFIRM_SAMPLES consecutive positives, so a
   277	        # momentary auth elsewhere on the machine cannot set it.
   278	        self.security_dialog_seen = False
   279	        self._dialog_streak = 0
   280	        self.samples: list[tuple[float, float, int]] = []   # (wall, cpu_seconds, nproc)
   281	        self.mtime_start = 0.0
   282	        self.mtime_last = 0.0
   283	        # GH-492: monotonic timestamp of the last sample that showed the tree doing
   284	        # SOMETHING — CPU growth past the jitter epsilon, or a file newer than the
   285	        # one we last saw. `idle_seconds()` measures forward from here.
   286	        self._last_progress_t: float | None = None
   287	
   288	    def _sample(self) -> None:
   289	        cpu, nproc = _descendant_cpu_seconds(self.root_pid)
   290	        now = time.monotonic()
   291	        prev_cpu = self.samples[-1][1] if self.samples else None
   292	        self.samples.append((now, cpu, nproc))
   293	        if _security_dialog_present():
   294	            self._dialog_streak += 1
   295	            if self._dialog_streak >= DIALOG_CONFIRM_SAMPLES:
   296	                self.security_dialog_seen = True
   297	        else:
   298	            self._dialog_streak = 0
   299	        mtime_now = _newest_mtime(self.worktree)
   300	        # GH-492: "progress" is deliberately the SAME two signals classify() already
   301	        # reasons about, so an early idle kill can never disagree with the verdict
   302	        # printed for it. A first sample counts as progress: it establishes the
   303	        # baseline rather than starting the clock in the past.
   304	        if (
   305	            prev_cpu is None
   306	            or cpu > prev_cpu + CPU_PROGRESS_EPSILON_S
   307	            or mtime_now > self.mtime_last
   308	        ):
   309	            self._last_progress_t = now
   310	        self.mtime_last = mtime_now
   311	
   312	    def _loop(self) -> None:
   313	        while not self._stop.is_set():
   314	            try:
   315	                self._sample()
   316	            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — never fail the turn being measured
   317	                pass
   318	            self._stop.wait(self.interval)
   319	
   320	    def start(self) -> None:
   321	        self.mtime_start = _newest_mtime(self.worktree)
   322	        self.mtime_last = self.mtime_start
   323	        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, name="turn-diagnostics", daemon=True)
   324	        self._thread.start()
   325	
   326	    def stop(self) -> None:
   327	        self._stop.set()
   328	        if self._thread is not None:
   329	            self._thread.join(timeout=2.0)
   330	
   331	    def cpu_ratio(self) -> float | None:
   332	        """CPU seconds per wall second over the sampled window, or None.
   333	
   334	        Anchored on the PEAK observed cumulative CPU, not the last sample. A
   335	        process's accounting disappears from ``ps`` the moment it exits, and the
   336	        final sample is taken *after* the timeout kill — so reading the last
   337	        sample scores a dead runaway as 0.00s/s and reports it as idle, which is
   338	        exactly backwards. Cumulative CPU only rises while a process lives, so
   339	        the peak is the true total for the tree.
   340	        """
   341	        if len(self.samples) < 2:
   342	            return None
   343	        t0, c0, _ = self.samples[0]
   344	        t_peak, c_peak = t0, c0
   345	        for t, c, _ in self.samples:
   346	            if c > c_peak:
   347	                t_peak, c_peak = t, c
   348	        # A process that never accumulates CPU leaves the peak at sample 0, so
   349	        # the peak window is zero-length. That is the BLOCKED case — the one this
   350	        # module exists to name — and returning None there would file it as
   351	        # `unclassified` instead of `idle-no-progress`. Measure a flat trace over
   352	        # the full observed window so it scores a real 0.0, and reserve the peak
   353	        # window for traces that actually grew.
   354	        span = (t_peak - t0) if c_peak > c0 else (self.samples[-1][0] - t0)
   355	        if span <= 0:
   356	            return None
   357	        return max(0.0, (c_peak - c0)) / span
   358	
   359	    def idle_seconds(self) -> float | None:
   360	        """Wall seconds since the tree last showed CPU growth or file progress.
   361	
   362	        ``None`` means "not enough evidence to say" — fewer than
   363	        ``IDLE_MIN_SAMPLES`` readings, or no sample taken yet. Callers MUST treat
   364	        ``None`` as "do not kill"; it is the not-yet-measured state, not zero.
   365	
   366	        GH-492: this exists so a hang can be contained on a short idle threshold
   367	        instead of only at the full wall cap. The observed incident produced 90
   368	        consecutive samples reading ``cpu=0.02s/s, worktree-progress=no`` and they
   369	        were unanimous from the start — the run learned nothing between sample 3

CHANGELOG.md-7-- **GH-624 / GH-629: merge-cleanup Phase 5 lands more than one ledger-touching PR per run.** The `pr_merged` work emit moved from before the fast-forward to after reconciliation; Phase 5 now runs merge → fast-forward → reconcile → emit → commit → push and asserts the primary is clean at `origin/<integration>` before the next PR (`commit_and_push_phase5_writes`). Reconciliation first looks for the hosted `wave-reconcile.yml` run for the exact merged head (`gh run list --commit`), polls it to completion (`MERGE_CLEANUP_HOSTED_WAIT_S`, `MERGE_CLEANUP_HOSTED_POLL_S`, `MERGE_CLEANUP_HOSTED_GRACE_S`), fast-forwards onto its commit on success, and runs the local `wave_reconcile.py` only when the hosted run is absent or completed red — never while it is queued or in progress. Tests: a two-PR `Closes #N` landing in `test/gh534_phase_c_tests.py` (red under the old order), a hosted-wait test against a fake `gh run list`, and an AST order pin in `test/gh549-work-events.sh`. Landed by marathon `marathon/10days-2026-09-15` (builder codex, reviewer agy).
CHANGELOG.md-8-- **GH-625: agent-chorus bridge binds without a reverse DNS lookup.** `ThreadingHTTPServer.server_bind` now calls `socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind` and takes `server_name`/`server_port` from the bound socket instead of `HTTPServer`'s `socket.getfqdn()`, which hung past the 4 s probe window on the GitHub-hosted macOS runner and kept `test/agent-chorus-bridge.sh` (and therefore hosted `wave-reconcile.yml`) red. One new check runs the bridge with `socket.getfqdn` patched to raise. Same marathon.
CHANGELOG.md-9-- **GH-630: `agy-turn.py` model validation accepts the id, the display name, or the whole `agy models` line.** #607 narrowed the match to the first token (right for the CLI's `id<TAB>Display` rows) and turned `test/agy-turn.sh` red on `development`, which blocked every full-validation push; the check now accepts all three forms. Found by this branch's pre-push gate.

CHANGELOG.md-13-- **GH-626: skills(workhorse, unstuck): close the autonomous re-entry loop.** Establishes an explicit orchestrator re-entry drive loop (`drive → repair/park → --resume → loop`) in `skills/workhorse/SKILL.md`, mandating that sub-item repairs (such as resolving PR merge conflicts) are treated as intermediate steps requiring immediate re-invocation of the batch runner with `--resume` rather than prompting the operator. Adds an anti-downgrade rail forbidding "Done" claims when batch deliverables were bypassed. Equips `skills/unstuck/SKILL.md` with 4 autonomous self-trigger tripwires (two-turn no-milestone, tool exit code inertia, passive waiting narration, false completion) and hardens Rung 5 to require re-driving the primary execution engine before exiting. Reversibility: **Easy** — revert the two SKILL.md edits and re-deploy via Skills Army HQ. Verification: `test/test_deploy_skills.py` 25/25 passing; live deployment via `intake.py --apply update` to all enabled IDE targets; `utils/pdda/pdda.sh run` clean.

CHANGELOG.md:15:- **GH-623: merge-cleanup survives transient network failures; collision edges no longer cascade handoffs.** File-collision toposort edges are now SOFT (`_soft_deps`): they order the sequence but never produce "NOT attempted" — only explicit `depends on #N` edges (`_hard_deps`) block on a failed predecessor, so one handoff no longer removes most of the queue (the incident's S3; PR #601-style MERGEABLE dependents are attempted and their own landing simulation decides). Every retry-site network call is bounded in time (`run_git` gains an additive timeout, default unbounded; `fetch_open_prs` bounded + raises `FetchError` instead of silently returning `[]`), transient failures (DNS/refused/timed-out/TLS/rate-limit) are retried 3× (2s, 4s), and a pre-decision failure that survives the retries DEFERS that PR while the queue continues (the incident's S4). A failed `gh pr list` now exits 2 before teardown instead of reading as "No open PRs found". New `--resume` consults attempt records only after the live refresh: a PR whose repair resolved and now merges cleanly lands; a still-conflicting exhausted PR skips as parked (the incident's S5). SKILL.md gains a Drive loop with a Done rule ("do not report Done unless Phase 5 ran — or the operator asked for teardown/scan") and a retry-once rule for permission-classifier blocks of `--execute` (S1/S2). Reversibility: **Easy** — revert the PR; no schema or data changes; `_deps` remains in the standalone JSON output as the sorted union. Verification: 13 witnessed red controls failing on pre-change code (soft-edge, retry+defer, discovery, bounded calls, both resume pins), then the merge-cleanup unit suite 156/156 green including the parity guard; full qualifying gate in a disposable clone recorded in the PR.
CHANGELOG.md-16-- **GH-605: preserve JSON-native unresolved identities across saved preview/apply.** Normalize planner output once so unchanged unknown evidence survives JSON round-tripping; retain exact drift refusal. Existing real integration fixtures now include a missing-ledger issue, assert it stays untouched, and reject tampered unresolved evidence. Reversibility: Easy, revert the output normalization. Verification: witnessed failing regression before correction and 51/51 focused board tests after.

CHANGELOG.md-23-- **GH-605: make work-state projection evidence-driven and policy-safe.** Roadmap updates now emit section-first lifecycle transitions only when section/marker state actually changes; terminal sweeps append all per-row events with one receipt and rollback boundary. `releases work status` diagnoses schema/cursor/activity age read-only without treating stale, malformed, future, backfill, identity-mismatched or superseded observations as current work, binds evidence and emitted events to each roadmap row's actual repo, retains independently trusted source identity when an issue URL is invalid, refuses ambiguous number-only updates, returns structured unready diagnostics for unsupported roots, and rejects WAL-format databases before opening even when sidecars are absent. Jog add/lease/status/drop/skip/retry lifecycle writes resolve one exact queue row across all repositories inside the receipt transaction and refuse ambiguous cross-repository numbers; queue clear and orphan recovery emit owned batched transitions atomically, same-state metadata writes do not manufacture lifecycle events, and active queue positions compact only when a row actually leaves `pending`/`running`. Forced rerating replaces the complete old score/override token, and repoint mutates one resolved global row. The existing board writer gains a deterministic saved-policy planner, RepositoryOwner-based project resolution, balanced bounded queries, complete issue/PR identities, preview/apply/conditional-restore commands, durable per-request intent/result audit, status clear support, destination validation before add, and a raw-replay guard for policy-managed boards. Explicit OPEN closing PR links can place genuinely absent ledger issues while contradictory, invalid, or duplicate ledger evidence remains preserved on every issue selection path, including CLOSED issues. The legacy raw connector retains its configured single-repository replay payload; policy preview/apply is the complete repo-qualified multi-repository projection. Reopened/duplicate linked issues, unset and unknown Ready cards, malformed/future terminal data, unknown PR state, and duplicate/opaque/foreign cards are preserved or explicitly reported. Apply holds the same-ledger connector lock across fresh preflight and writes, compares item ID plus status before every request, validates add/set/clear response item IDs before recording success, and requires both preview creation and evidence clocks to be coherently ordered and no older than 15 minutes; restore requires its own audit artifact and keeps both prior and new lost/indeterminate responses explicit. The stateful GitHub mock preserves issue versus PR identity and refuses unknown content IDs. No scheduler, dependency, deletion, schema, or personal board default was added. Reversibility: **Costly** for an interrupted remote apply—disable the connector, retain its result journal, read back GitHub, and use conditional restore; code rollback is otherwise straightforward. Verification: the two direct focused fixtures pass 78/78 in this bounded turn, including real preview/apply/failure/restore, invalid-URL identity preservation through the real loader/planner boundary, cross-repository lease ownership, idempotent queue compaction, actual jog command/batch lifecycle and rollback, coherent-clock, CLOSED-identity, PR-mock, mutation-response, rerating and repoint controls; legacy shell/full gate and live Rev. 2 application remain for the parent in a disposable full clone.

CHANGELOG.md:185:- **GH-299: Gen 4 ATE & True Evolutionary Fuzzing — all five phases, on `feat/gh299-gen4-ate`.** Gen 3/3.5 established deterministic oracles and sandbox safety but stayed at enumerated variation; Gen 4 adds generative fuzzing and $0 triage on top of them without forking any of them. One shared contract, `utils/py/telemetry_schema.py` (`TelemetryEvent` schema 1.0, stderr normalizer + 16-hex digest, duration buckets, line-level JSONL validation), is the interchange record for every pillar. **Phase 1** `utils/py/domain_oracles.py`: zero-state (SHA-256 tree digest + bounded `lsof` leak sweep), host containment (`.git/config` bytes, `core.bare`, remotes, HEAD ref/tip, host tree digest — refuses a work root that is not disjoint from the host), idempotence + receipt monotonicity, and crash/stale-lock recovery (SIGKILL the holder in its own process group, prove the recover command succeeds and every JSONL stays line-valid); reuses `metamorphic_oracle` primitives. **Phase 2** `utils/py/adaptive_ate.py` + `utils/py/calibrate_tier1.py`: a YAML/JSON flag-grid grammar with `conflicts`/`requires`, an AETG-style all-pairs generator (reference 12-flag grid: 13 cases vs 13,824 Cartesian, 100% valid 2-way coverage confirmed by an independent brute-force walk in the suite), a <5 ms Tier-1 classifier over the feedback vector, a Tier-2 escalation hook that is invoked only on anomalies, and a shipped calibration (`utils/ate/tier1-calibration.json`) produced from a 50 known-pass / 20 known-fail benchmark under a hard 0% false-negative floor. **Phase 3** `utils/py/fuzz_engine.py`: four seeded mutator families, byte-identical plan replay from `--seed`, a `.fuzz_corpus/` (gitignored) capped at 500 with `0.7×novelty + 0.3×recency` eviction where a smaller mutant wins a signature collision and keeps the slot id, per-mutant timeouts that kill the whole process group, and a cross-twin parity oracle (`--parity-env XYZ_PYTHON=0`) — its first real run recorded 6/12 divergences on `codex-turn.sh`, filed as a finding for the soak, not fixed here. **Phase 4** `utils/py/repro_synth.py` (and `repro_builder.py --mode synth`): counterexamples are clustered by `stderr_digest` before ddmin, so 50 mutations of one root cause emit exactly one hermetic, fixture-guarded `test/gh<N>-gen4-*.sh` that passes while the defect reproduces and goes red once it is fixed. **Phase 5** `utils/py/gen4_campaign.py`: the unattended runner — disposable full clone as `cwd`, nine real harness targets round-robined, sandbox zero-state + host identity checked after every batch with reset-on-contamination, replay-verified clusters (false positives reported, never synthesized), `campaign-report.json` + `campaign-summary.md`, opt-in `self_healer.py` handoff. `validate.sh` is deliberately not a target: the first campaign run showed a mutant slipping past `--print-mode` and running the full gate inside the sandbox. Pinned by five suites, `test/gh-gen4-phase{1..5}-*.sh` (17/18/20/17/17 assertions, every oracle and classifier with a positive **and** a negative control), all registered in `validate.sh` and the `ate` tier-2 subsystem. The GH-299 doc was promoted 1-INBOX → 2-WORKING through the DB verbs. **Owed, not claimed:** the Phase 5 bar (>10,000 mutations, 0 host contamination, 0 false positives over a multi-hour soak) — a 400-mutation evidence run lives in `TESTS-RESULTS/2026-09-04+GH-299/campaign/`, and the 3-hour soak prompt for Agy is `relay-system/2026-09-04/gh299-gen4-soak-agy-PROMPT.md`. Reversibility: **Easy** — six new modules, one delegating `--mode` in `repro_builder.py`, one `.gitignore` line, registry entries; revert the branch. Verification: the five phase suites green plus `gh155` 6/6 (Gen 3 minimizers untouched), `gh35` 71/71 and `gh139` after their fixture updates, full pre-push gate green on every phase push.

CHANGELOG.md-717-- **The `releases-skill` gate is unregistered until its file lands — `development`'s suite was red in every clone but one.** The registration reached `development` while the gate file it names did not, so `validate.sh` exited 127 for everyone whose working tree did not happen to hold the author's uncommitted copy — and green for the one session that could not see the breakage. That is #461's defect in mirror image: there, a gate that exists but is unregistered is invisible; here, a registration with no gate is a permanent red that says nothing about the code, and since GH-544 put the suite on the push boundary it was refusing every push from every session. **The test is not at fault and was not deleted** — it passes **26/0** in the tree where its inputs exist. It needs the whole consolidation (the plural skill directory, removal of the legacy singular one, and the router / PDDA-contract routing updates), which is in flight and uncommitted elsewhere; landing that change re-enables the line in the same commit. Deliberately not completed here: pulling ~7 files of another session's uncommitted work across — including its own CHANGELOG prose — to satisfy a one-line registration would be a much larger intervention than the breakage warrants. Suite goes from 3 failures to 1. **RESOLVED the same day** — the consolidation landed and the line was re-registered in the commit that brought the gate file with it, which is exactly the condition recorded here. Kept rather than deleted because a ~2h window in which the shared branch refused every session's push is a real event, and the rule it produced is worth stating once: **register a gate and its file together, or neither.** → [#461](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/461)
CHANGELOG.md-718-- **GH-561: the marathon branch guard was protecting the one branch marathons never touch, and the 2026-08-15 Meter run landed four commits straight on `development` with no branch and no PR.** `refuse_trunk_commit` (GH-402) keyed on `origin/HEAD`, which here resolves to `origin/main`, so `development` read as an ordinary feature branch and the guard returned without firing — while `marathon-closeout.sh:18` has hardcoded `BASE_BRANCH="development"` all along. **The two halves of one ceremony disagreed about what `development` is**: closeout treats it as the branch you PR *into*, the guard treated it as one you may commit *on*, and AGENTS.md is with closeout. The harm the guard's own message names — turns commit continuously, so a run that lands on a shared branch can only be un-landed by rewriting history someone else may have pulled — applies to `development` exactly as to `main`. **The remedy changed too, and this is the consequential half:** GH-402 shipped a hard refusal, and the refusal was right about the harm and wrong about the response, because the operator's only correct next action was always the same `checkout -b` and an unattended marathon has nobody there to take it. The guard now **cuts the lane branch and continues** (`SP_SUGGESTED_BRANCH`, else `marathon/<phase>-<date>`; an existing branch is switched to so a re-fire resumes its own work rather than stranding each attempt), and a green phase calls `marathon-closeout.sh --open-only --no-commit` so a finished lane leaves an open PR into `development`. **`--no-commit` is new and load-bearing** — closeout's default `git add -A` swept 20 unrelated files into a lane PR once already (2026-08-10), and an automated caller must not re-arm that. GH-402's invariant is unchanged and now measured directly rather than inferred from a refusal: the shared branch receives nothing. **Bet:** redirecting beats refusing because the refusal had exactly one correct response; if auto-cut ever produces a branch the operator did not want, the cost is a stray branch, not lost work. **Failure signal:** a lane branch that carries no commits, or a PR opened against the wrong base. **Rollback:** `MARATHON_INTEGRATION_BRANCH=` restores GH-402 scope; a failed auto-cut already falls back to the original hard refusal. **Contributing cause recorded rather than smoothed over:** the run cited AGENTS.md's "do not create new git branches automatically" as its justification, ignoring the marathon carve-out in the very next bullet — that bullet is amended, but the guard is what actually stops it, same lesson as GH-551. `test/gh402-branch-enforcement.sh` **20/0** (was 13, and cases 1/2/6 were rewritten from refusal semantics to redirect semantics), `test/marathon-closeout.sh` **25/0**. → [#561](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/561) · [#402](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/402)
CHANGELOG.md-719-- **GH-557: an acceptance verdict of `unknown` no longer reads as `ready` on a frozen manifest entry.** `check_acceptance_fidelity` blocked only on `diverged`, so `unknown` fell through to `ready (exit 0)`. Caught live against Meter manifest member **#382** with `gh` authenticated and the network healthy: `inlined-acc : 6 criterion(a)`, `acceptance : unknown — issue #382 has no '## Acceptance' section`, `verdict : ready (exit 0)`. Six criteria in the capture doc, none on the issue, lane dispatchable — which is exactly the GH-400 failure arriving through GH-400's own pass-through case, since neither builder nor reviewer ever sees the issue. **One status was hiding two situations that need opposite handling**, and that collapse cost a real diagnosis: during the 2026-08-14 DNS outage every Meter packet read `unknown` and it was attributed to DNS; when DNS was restored the same entries still read `unknown` for the second reason entirely, and nothing in the output distinguished them. A `cause` field now separates **`fetch-failed`** (transient — advisory on *every* path, including manifest members, because an outage is not a contract violation and making it one would have halted the whole repo on 2026-08-14) from **`no-issue-section`** (structural — the issue states no criteria, so no retry will ever verify the doc's list). **Only the structural cause blocks, and only on a frozen manifest member**: everywhere else it stays advisory, because refusing every acceptance-less issue would be a hard stop on ordinary exploratory and externally-reported work. Membership is read from each `test/*-release.sh` goalpost's `MANIFEST=(...)` array — already cross-checked against `RELEASES.md` by the goalpost itself — and **not** by parsing `RELEASES.md`'s `Manifest:` prose, which names #509 (retired), #358 Phase 2 (moved to Lantern) and #551's nine root-cause siblings; a regex over that line would have read every one as a member and blocked unrelated lanes, a worse failure than the one being fixed. The packet's provenance line for the structural case also stops telling the reader to "read the issue before building" — there is nothing there to read, which is the whole problem. **16/0**, hermetic; control in `test/baselines/GH-557-negative-control.md` is **5 pass / 11 fail** pre-fix with the pin observed as `expected exit 5, got 0` — and the three assertions that *pass* pre-fix are the load-bearing ones, since a detector that simply refused every acceptance-less issue would satisfy the pin and fail all three. **Deliberately not admitted to Meter**, which stays frozen at seven: it was found while re-running that manifest, which is provenance, not membership. → [GH-557-UNKNOWN-BLOCKS-MANIFEST.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-557-UNKNOWN-BLOCKS-MANIFEST.md) · [#557](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/557) · [#400](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/400) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)

CHANGELOG.md:770:- **`validate.sh --parallel N` — the GH-528 spike's one "go" lever, shipped as explicitly experimental.** The spike measured the full gate before touching it (190 shell suites, 950.3s sequential on M-series macOS) and returned three no-gos the suite keeps: **zero redundant suites** (full read of the GH-375/385/390/407/419 family — the thrice-repeated red-gate→`pre-advance-failed` assertion is a load-bearing anti-overcorrection control in each of its three homes, confirmed independently by a Codex+agy consult), **no sleep surgery** (hypothesis falsified: the top-10 wall-clock owners contain essentially zero executed sleep; the load-bearing timeout proofs were already env-injected to 1–5s), and **no cuts** (no incident-backed suite is touched, so the #419 observed-red standard is not in play). The go: every suite is already self-isolated in its own mktemp dir, and the only load-bearing shared resource is this clone's `.git/relay-driver.lock` — the GH-42 exclusion, held by the **13 suites that execute the real `relay-drive.sh`** ("--target-root moves the build, not the lock", `test/gh331-cost-summary.sh`). `--parallel N` pools the other 177 and serializes those 13 in one lane; the sequential no-arg path is unchanged, malformed flags refuse with exit 2, per-suite output goes to per-run logs with a failed suite's tail printed and named. **A/B on one commit: sequential 946.0s rc=1 vs `--parallel 8` 184.3s rc=1 — 5.1×, with byte-identical pass/fail sets** (the two fails were a genuinely stale ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md, which failing the parallel run is the attribution QA gate demonstrating itself, and the pytest lane missing pytest in that shell). No driver lock leaked, no worktree leaked. **Deliberately NOT the default and NOT promotion evidence:** the consult set the bar — multi-width repeated runs (~N=50 for the timing-sensitive suites under CPU load), clean-tree/leak checks, pytest+npm steps included — recorded as Phase 2 in the doc; the driver-lock-scope question (`relay_drive.py:67,403` locks the harness root regardless of `RELAY_TARGET_ROOT`) is parked as Phase 3 for its own issue rather than a drive-by change to a safety mechanism with incident history (#331/#376/#448). → [GH-528-TEST-SUITE-RECALIBRATION.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-528-TEST-SUITE-RECALIBRATION.md) · [#528](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/528)

CHANGELOG.md-773-- **The gamma-poison qualification fixture was re-derived after rotting unnoticed, and `validate.sh` now probes for the rot it could not see (GH-428).** `git apply --check test/fixtures/gamma-poison/poison.patch` had been failing at `src/paths.js:9` since GH-71 refactored that file — and because the fixture is deliberately *not* wired into `validate.sh` (its own `verify-fixture.sh` runs the whole suite, so nesting recurses), **nothing detected it**; the fixture's own README warned about exactly this staleness mode and the warning came true in silence. Since this is Phase 1 of the GH-40 double-blind Reviewer qualification gate — the only fixture covering a Reviewer rubber-stamping a change that silently drops the suite — no Reviewer could be qualified while it was broken. **The fix is a context regeneration, not a semantic change:** the poisoned line is byte-identical, GH-71 merely inserted a JSDoc block above it and shifted the hunk from `@@ -9,7` to `@@ -15,7`, so the poison remains exactly `*` dropped from the negated class in `literalPrefix()`. `verify-fixture.sh` ran end-to-end — **FIXTURE OK, 171/172, exactly one failing check and it is `path-overlap`** — with the trap leaving a clean tree and `src/paths.js` untouched. The new probe in `validate.sh` is a plain non-recursive `git apply --check` that never invokes `verify-fixture.sh`. **The control caveat is recorded rather than glossed, because the first attempt at it failed:** corrupting only the hunk header's line numbers still applies, since `git apply` matches on context and tolerates line drift — the falsifying control has to corrupt a *context line*, which both the builder lane and the orchestrator discovered independently. So the probe catches content drift (and the GH-71 context drift that actually caused this rot) but is deliberately tolerant of pure line movement. → [GH-428-GAMMA-POISON-FIXTURE-ROT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-428-GAMMA-POISON-FIXTURE-ROT.md) · [#428](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/428)
CHANGELOG.md-774-- **`improve-loop.sh` stopped writing its only audit trail somewhere that evaporates (GH-430).** The state dir defaulted to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/improve-loop.$$`, and `provenance.jsonl` — every accept/reject, the metric trace, the spend — went with it: a full-tree search found **zero** `provenance*.jsonl` in the repo, including for the 2026-06-30 live-agent run cited in `ROADMAP.md` and in the GH-50 close as "proven … provenance logged". The default is now `$HERE/state/improve-loop.$$` → `relay-automation/state/`, **verified by `git check-ignore` to match no ignore rule**, which is the whole point: the GH-396 constraint is that `.tick/` is gitignored and `rtl_enforce` does not inspect ignored files, so a gitignored state dir inherits zero containment protection. An explicit `--state-dir` still wins. `test/gh430-state-dir-tracked-default.sh` is registered and reports **8/0 inside the full gate**, asserting the default resolves in-repo, is not under `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR`, is not gitignored, writes a non-empty `provenance.jsonl`, and is still overridable; the lane observed it red against the reverted line 70. `AGENTS.md` carries the process half — an uncommitted `provenance.jsonl` is treated as no claim. **One choice is the operator's to invert:** the issue offered "refuse to start without `--state-dir`" as the alternative, and this took the in-repo-default branch because refusing would break every existing caller. → [GH-430-IMPROVE-LOOP-STATE-DIR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-430-IMPROVE-LOOP-STATE-DIR.md) · [#430](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/430)

It matters more than a doc nit because three lines below, the same table concludes that `xyz-vendor.sh` (not `install.sh`) **is** the path to concurrent per-repo relay isolation — so the documented entry point failed on first use. **One instance of the same wrong form remains and is deliberately not fixed here:** `skills/relay-xyz/find-harness.sh:255` prints it inside a hint string, outside this lane's artifact allowlist; it is recorded on the capture doc rather than swept in silently. → [GH-421-RELAY-XYZ-VENDOR-DOC.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-421-RELAY-XYZ-VENDOR-DOC.md) · [#421](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/421)
CHANGELOG.md-776-- **`--parallel` reported a failure the sequential gate does not have, on its very first reuse — the driver-lock lane list was built on the wrong rule, and a hand-maintained list that fails silently was the real defect.** Merging `development` into the GH-528 branch and re-running produced one red suite: `gh322-unknown-arg-rejection.sh`, `exit codes diverge — Python 2, Bash 1`. Not a flake and not a product bug. **`relay-drive.sh` takes the driver lock at line ~142, before `usage()` and before it parses a single argument**, so under contention the Bash twin exits 1 (lock refusal) while the Python twin, which parses first, still exits 2 — and the suite, which never drives anything and only asserts that a bogus flag is rejected identically by both twins, reports a parity mismatch that is plausible, on-topic and completely false. Reproduced deterministically by holding the lock with a live pid, and green the instant it is released. **The lane rule was wrong, not merely the membership**: it is not "suites that drive", it is **suites that invoke a driver at all** — and the spike derived the original 13 from observed lock *refusals*, so a suite whose contention surfaces as a *parity assertion* was invisible to that method. Fixing only the list would have left the trap armed for the next suite, so two things changed: `gh322` joins the lane (13 → 14), and **every pooled failure is now re-run alone** with the lane finished and the lock free before it is believed — fails alone too → real failure with the serial log printed; passes alone → counted **passed** (sequential is the source of truth, and returning sequential's answer is the flag's entire promise) and **named in a warning** as a lane-list gap. An incomplete list can no longer produce a false red, and can no longer be silent about itself either. **A third defect surfaced while proving the second:** the lane iterated the literal `DRIVER_LOCK_LANE` string rather than intersecting it with `TESTS`, so lane suites ran even when `TESTS` did not contain them — `--parallel` executed suites the sequential path skipped, and the summary printed `passed: 16 / 3`; both lists are now derived from `TESTS`. `test/gh528-parallel-contention-retry.sh` pins all of it (4/0, registered), and its control is a **mutation rather than a race**: the contention failure is timing-dependent and did *not* reproduce on a later run with the same broken list, which is exactly why it could not be caught by re-running — so the probe suite reproduces the shape (red first, green alone) against a copy of `validate.sh` with only the `TESTS` array swapped, keeping every line of the shipped parallel implementation under test. With the re-run block deleted — the state this branch shipped in its first build — 3 of 4 assertions go red and the probe is reported as failed exactly as `gh322` was. **The honest read: the flag's original A/B was not sufficient evidence.** One green parallel run on one commit cannot distinguish "correct" from "did not happen to collide this time", which is the gap GH-528 Phase 2's stress bar exists to close — this argues for that bar, not against it. → [GH-528-TEST-SUITE-RECALIBRATION.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-528-TEST-SUITE-RECALIBRATION.md) · [#528](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/528)

CHANGELOG.md-780-- **The command rail now names both gate forms, because a faster gate nobody knows about does not get run — and the reason it exists is on the invoice.** `ROUTER.md` previously listed `./validate.sh` alone; it now lists the sequential run as the canonical gate (**the only one that qualifies a claim**) alongside `./validate.sh --parallel 8` as the experimental fast self-check, with the ordering and the labels doing the work — an operator who reads only the first line still gets the correct default. The motivation is measured, not asserted: the org's actual August usage (`gh api orgs/.../settings/billing/usage`; the per-run billable-timing API reports 0min here and is unusable) is **$9.09 net of a $10 budget — Ubuntu 2,740 min at $4.44 net after the 2,000 included minutes, plus macOS 3-core 75 min at $4.65 net with no discount at all.** **75 macOS minutes cost as much as 2,740 Linux minutes**, so each `boundary-macos` dispatch is ≈$1.25–1.50 and the job's `workflow_dispatch`-or-push-to-`main` gating is doing real work — but nothing brakes repeated dispatches, and three landed on `feat/gh509-ci-macos-strategy` on 2026-08-13 alone. The Linux side is over quota on *volume*: every push to `development` and every PR into `development`/`main` starts a run (route-tiered, so not every run is the full gate), while a feature-branch push with no open PR costs $0. That is what makes the local gate's 946s → 184s the cost-relevant number rather than merely a convenience: the local run is the substitute for a hosted one, and it is now cheap enough to be used that way. Recorded on #509, which owns CI spend; #528 owns only the runner. → [#528](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/528) · [#509](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/509)

CHANGELOG.md-785-- **Local evidence became a thing the machine can read, not a claim in a chat message.** Three pieces. `utils/gate-record.sh` writes `.gate-evidence/<sha>.txt` after a full green and **refuses on a dirty tree** — a record keyed to a commit while uncommitted edits sit in the tree attests to a state that was never tested, which is worse than no record because it reads as evidence; untracked files count, since that is the common case (a new test beside the code it covers). It was **extracted from `ci-local.sh` specifically so the refusal is testable**: inlined, the only way to exercise it was a ~15-minute suite run, so it would have shipped asserted-by-comment — the exact thing this repo keeps paying for. `ci-local.sh --probe` strips `codex`/`agy`/`aider` from PATH to simulate a fresh Mac where XYZ was just installed, which is #380's actual audience and the class that produced all three of #520's failures; it **aborts if the binaries survive the strip**, because a probe that silently ran with them present reports green and means nothing. `utils/gate-status.sh` is the reading surface — local record, hosted macOS boundary with **distance**, and the canary line — because with no branch protection available CI here is a detector, and a correct detector nobody reads buys nothing. **Two real bugs surfaced by the new tests and recorded rather than quietly fixed:** the status tool's first filter matched any successful push/dispatch and therefore reported a push to `development` — an ubuntu canary run that never touches macOS — as **boundary evidence**, meaning the tool built to prevent false promotion evidence was manufacturing it; the filter now mirrors the boundary job's own `if:` and a test pins them together. And `git rev-parse HEAD` prints the literal string `HEAD` on stdout in a repo with no commits, so both scripts would have written `.gate-evidence/HEAD.txt` — now `--verify`. The record states **on its own face** that it is not promotion evidence, and a test fails if that line is removed, because the file is what a future reader will find and reason from. `test/gh509-gate-evidence.sh` 17/0, registered in `validate.sh` (191/191). → [#509](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/509)
CHANGELOG.md-786-- **Pushes to `development` are classified instead of blanket-full — the 72% of the bill GH-509 identified and then exempted.** Measured over 60 runs in ~24h: **37 pushes to `development`, every one on the full route, ~396 of ~551 billed minutes.** Phase 1 routed pull requests and cut their average from ~16 min to 6.1 — it worked, on the other 28%. `utils/ci-route.sh` now classifies `push` from its pushed range exactly as it classifies a PR from its diff; `workflow_dispatch` and `schedule` stay unconditionally full, because a manual dispatch is someone asking for the whole gate and answering with a routed subset answers a different question. **Three ways a range can be unusable all fail closed** — an all-zeros `before` on a new branch, an unreachable `before` after a force-push, and no range concept at all — each by handing the classifier an empty path list, reusing the zero-path branch that already had its own test rather than inventing a second fail-closed rule needing its own proof. **The rename loophole is closed, and the fix is a flag, not logic:** with git's default rename detection `--name-only` prints only a rename's *destination*, so a renamed regression test read as an ordinary changed file that still exists and never reached `ci-route.sh`'s fail-closed branch — while that branch's own comment claims to cover "deleted/renamed". Deletion reached it; rename never did. The collection command now passes `--no-renames`. **The control drives a real `git mv` through the workflow's own command** rather than asserting on the classifier, because the classifier was never wrong — it behaves correctly for whatever paths it is handed, and the defect was in which paths it was handed. Both directions are pinned: a renamed test selects full, and the same file merely *edited* does not, so the rule is not a blanket that would pass the rename case for the wrong reason. A first assertion records the premise itself (`plain --name-only reports ONE path for a rename`) so a future git change makes the guard say its premise is stale instead of silently becoming decoration. `ci-route` 15 → 23, `ci-workflow` 37 → 40, every new guard witnessed red (`test/baselines/GH-509-phase3-negative-control.md`). One pre-existing assertion was **updated rather than deleted** — it pinned the literal `utils/ci-route.sh pull_request`, which legitimately changed to `"$EVENT_NAME"`; the invariant it protects (routing is delegated to the tested classifier, never reimplemented inline in YAML where it would have no test) is unchanged and still asserted. → [#509](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/509)
CHANGELOG.md-787-- **A macOS promotion boundary — the first CI job whose green says anything about what XYZ actually ships.** `boundary-macos` runs on `macos-latest` and invokes `RELAY_SELF_SUFFICIENCY_SKIP=1 ./validate.sh` **directly, with no skip list**. That single choice closes the defect where the hosted "full" route scraped `TESTS` out of `validate.sh` with a `.sh`-only expression and therefore could never see `test/test_python_layer.py` — **20 tests over the authoritative implementation since GH-264, which had never run in CI at all**. There is no second list to keep honest, and an assertion fails if one appears. **Triggers are `push` to `main` plus `workflow_dispatch`, and never `pull_request`** — hosted macOS bills roughly 10× Linux, so putting it on routine traffic would restore the original spend at ten times the rate, which is the failure GH-509 exists to prevent; the boundary is affordable *because* it is rare. `workflow_dispatch` is the trigger that will actually get used: work lands on `development` and `main` sees almost nothing, so a main-only boundary would always arrive *after* the promotion decision rather than before it. **A precision limit is encoded in the job rather than discovered later** — `workflow_dispatch` targets a *ref*, not an arbitrary commit, so the job qualifies whatever that ref points at when dispatched; it therefore prints `MACOS-BOUNDARY: green|red <sha>` into the job summary, because the promotion rule compares against a recorded commit, not a remembered run. Bounded at 45 minutes, since an unbounded hang on a 10× runner is the failure discovered on an invoice. `test/ci-workflow.sh` 30 → 37, with **four mutations producing exactly one failure each** and restoring clean — one-failure-each being the property that separates a precise assertion from a blunt one (`test/baselines/GH-509-phase4-negative-control.md`). Still open and deliberately not claimed: no hosted macOS run has happened yet, and the entire promotion rule rests on that witness. → [#509](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/509)
CHANGELOG.md:788:- **Agent2Agent documents Doorbell mode — `watch` as a wake mechanism, not a poll, for bridging two live interactive sessions hands-free.** On a host that re-invokes the session when a background command exits (Claude Code's background Bash tasks), each seat launches `watch --timeout 0` as a background task after its one pasted join; the session sleeps until it owns `NEXT:`, wakes with the exit, composes its turn with the session's full accumulated context, sends, and re-arms in the same turn. This is docs-only — no helper change; `watch` already blocks, never writes, and never locks, which is exactly what makes it usable as a doorbell. The section makes re-arming part of the send step rather than optional hygiene, because an un-re-armed doorbell downgrades the seat to manual with no error, indistinguishable from the other participant still thinking. Seats degrade independently: doorbell, foreground `watch`, `drive`, and manual turns coexist in one roster. Where `drive` runs a fresh headless command per turn under one-hour/six-turn caps, doorbell turns are answered by the ongoing live session, so no subprocess caps apply — ownership enforcement in `send`/`close` is unchanged and remains the only write path. Hardened by a 3-round driven agy relay review (`relay-system/2026-08-12/agent2agent-doorbell-agy-review.md`, Approved r3 with every claim re-verified against the script): a `take-turn` join routes straight to send-and-re-arm, dead-watch recovery keys on the missing `DECISION:` line rather than exit code (a timeout also exits non-zero but still prints its `DECISION`), no re-arm after `close`, and `watch`-granted turns are admitted to the send gate, which had been `join`-only. **Contributor feedback on PR #524 then converted re-arming from documented discipline into tool-enforced protocol**: a `watch` that exits `take-turn` now also prints a `REARM:` line — the exact, self-contained relaunch argv (absolute script path + `--root`, shell-quoted for paths with spaces) — so the waking session has the command in front of it at the moment it needs it instead of recalling a doc; a `closed` or `timeout` exit deliberately prints none, so a dead discussion cannot invite a reflex re-arm. `test/agent2agent.sh` asserts both directions (REARM present and self-contained on take-turn, absent on closed), observed **2 red** against the pre-fix source. → [#510](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/510)

CHANGELOG.md-790-### Changed
CHANGELOG.md-791-- **CI stopped treating a Linux runner's opinion as breakage, and the local runner stopped imitating a platform we don't ship to.** XYZ is a developer toolkit for **macOS**; Linux and Windows are on the roadmap and are not here yet. Two consequences, both shipped. **(1)** `jobs.tier1` → `jobs.canary-ubuntu`, `continue-on-error: true`, renamed to *"portability canary (ubuntu — advisory, never breakage)"*, with an `if: always()` verdict step emitting `PORTABILITY-CANARY: green|drift`. `always()` is the load-bearing half — without it the step is skipped in exactly the case it exists for, so the canary goes silent when it has something to say and every run that reaches the verdict is green by construction. The wording deliberately avoids "failed"/"broken" and states *NOT breakage* inline, because on a platform with no users those words are wrong and the wording **is** the mechanism. **(2)** `ci-local.sh` now runs a **superset** of the hosted job: it previously mirrored CI's skip list and therefore skipped `registry-lock-concurrency.sh`, a suite the workflow's own comment says *"passes locally"* — discarding real macOS signal to stay faithful to a contended Linux runner. Only `acorn-extract.sh` is still skipped, as duplicate work rather than dropped coverage. `test/ci-workflow.sh` had **pinned the two skip lists together**, so that assertion was inverted with it: local skipping that suite is now a failure, witnessed red. Both files' honesty notices were re-pointed — the useful caveat is no longer "a green local run isn't a green ubuntu run" but "a local run is **self-reported** and does not qualify a promotion", which is precisely what the hosted macOS boundary buys. **Advisory is not the same as read**, and the code says so instead of pretending: that critique came from the agy review and was accepted, with the mechanism deferred to a named acceptance criterion (the canary's status appears in the promotion output) plus a deletion trigger if two consecutive promotions ship with drift unresolved. `test/ci-workflow.sh` 26 → 30, every new assertion **witnessed red on its own mutation** (one failure each, restoring clean) — `test/baselines/GH-509-phase2-negative-control.md`. Honest limit recorded in the workflow itself: these assert the workflow *declares* the contract and cannot prove GitHub's runtime semantics; that needs a witnessed hosted run and is still open. One defect in the new test code was caught by this repo's own guard and is recorded rather than quietly fixed — the `if: always()` assertion was first written as `awk … | grep -q ok` in a `pipefail` script, the GH-472 SIGPIPE shape; the pipe was deleted and **the control re-run against the rewritten assertion**, since a witnessed red for code that no longer exists proves nothing about the code that ships. → [#509](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/509)

CHANGELOG.md-794-- **Three suites shipped green on a developer machine and were red on every ubuntu CI run, because their fixtures stubbed the builder binary and not the reviewer's — the GH-232 trap, walked into a third time.** `utils/py/marathon_drive.py:334` probes `CODEX_BIN` (default `codex`) before the guards, the preflight or any dispatch, so `gh402-branch-enforcement.sh`, `gh514-write-set-trackable.sh` and `gh388-run-log-durability.sh` never reached the code they were written to test — every assertion read `marathon-drive: reviewer binary 'codex' not found on PATH` instead. They passed locally only because a real `codex` is installed there. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already describes this failure mode in its own words from GH-232 ("stubbed `CLAUDE_BIN`/`AGY_BIN` but not `CODEX_BIN` … only 'passed' locally because a real `codex` binary happened to be on the developer's own PATH"); the comment did not prevent the recurrence, which is the real finding and is why **#520** is filed rather than the fix being treated as the whole story. Each suite now creates a no-op reviewer stub and exports `CODEX_BIN`, deliberately **not** reusing the builder stub — in `gh402` that stub appends to the dispatch log the cases count. **This was material to a release claim, not just to a test:** #388 and #514 are two of the five lifecycle cases `test/nightwatch-release.sh` *executes*, so Nightwatch's recorded `GOALPOST MET` was true on macOS and false on ubuntu at the moment it was written; the 0.3.0 block now says so and records the CI-verified re-run. The control is recorded in **four** directions and reproduces the CI condition locally by stripping `codex` from `PATH` rather than waiting on a hosted run — pre-fix red (byte-identical to Actions run 31565898558), post-fix green, post-fix green *with* `codex` present, and the release gate itself green under the stripped PATH. The uncovered direction is stated rather than glossed: `gh514` asserts on the **absence** of a traceback, which a run that dies at the probe also produces, so this class can fail *open* — these three failed closed, and nothing in the design guarantees the next one will. → [#520](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/520) · [#232](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/232) · `test/baselines/GH-520-negative-control.md`

CHANGELOG.md-799-- **Meter (0.6.0) opens as a frozen release rather than as Nightwatch leftovers, at operator instruction, with a scope boundary against Lantern written at creation.** The items Nightwatch finished without — #378, #379, #380, #382, #491 — are now a release with a theme, a manifest frozen on the day it was created, and a target date of 2027-01-16, instead of unmilestoned backlog that a session can drift into building. The theme is the one thing all five field reports share: **a run accounts for what it spends and checks what it requires before spending it** — ten ready lanes blocked by two unrelated pre-existing failures, a $0.50 budget kill misattributed to a pre-advance gate, 108 permission grants silently dropped on an untrusted directory, a kernel panic under memory pressure with no memory in the telemetry, and three builds plus three reviews re-spent on results the driver already held. Every member came from the same real unattended marathon against `rebalance-OS`. **The boundary against Lantern is stated because two members straddle it**: route by whether the issue names a *resource or precondition* (dollars, turns, memory, a trusted directory, a green suite) or *the wording of a verdict whose handling was already correct* — #379 is explicitly split by that rule, #491 is recorded as the marginal call and placed by the invariant it violates rather than by the shape of its fix. **#358 Phase 2 went to Lantern (0.5.0), not Meter, by operator decision the same day** — and the round trip is recorded in both blocks rather than tidied away, because a frozen manifest whose membership changes without a trace is not frozen. Lantern is the right home on Meter's own boundary rule: Phase 2 produces a failure that states its own reason, which is Lantern's subject, not a resource or a precondition. **Lantern is therefore RE-FROZEN at two entries** (#499 plus #358 Phase 2) and gains the exit criterion it had been missing — a frozen manifest with no testable exit command is exactly the half-built state `RELEASES.md` warns about, and its criterion is written around the fact that **#358 Phase 2 has no executable half**: it is satisfied by a recorded transcript of a real CI failure and must NOT be satisfiable by a disposition written in advance, since that issue's capture doc forbids pre-committing one and a criterion accepting a pre-written verdict would launder the exact thing #419 exists to prevent. **The issue keeps its Nightwatch milestone** — it is a frozen entry counted in that release's RC evidence, so only the scope moved; Nightwatch's block gains a `Post RC update:` line saying so in one sentence. Nightwatch's manifest is amended in place — the manifest and RC evidence are untouched; only its description of the non-gating remainder changed. `test/meter-release.sh` is **not built**, and the block says so: writing it before fixing any member is the Litmus/Nightwatch ordering, and it is the reason both releases could tell a finished entry from a claimed one. → [#378](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/378) · [#379](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/379) · [#380](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/380) · [#382](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/382) · [#491](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/491)
CHANGELOG.md-800-- **GH-509 / PR #511 replaces the one-size-fits-all Actions gate with deterministic docs, fast, and full routes while keeping PDDA at the boundaries it owns.** Documentation changes run the PDDA gate; ordinary code-only PRs run a fixed containment/worktree smoke set plus a directly matching changed-area test; Tick, relay, worktree, frozen-twin, PDDA, and CI surfaces fail closed into the complete pre-merge suite, as does deletion or renaming of a regression test. Integration pushes and manual dispatch also run the full gate, while an automatic daily full-suite schedule was deliberately omitted because it would add minute burn without a new release boundary. Superseded runs cancel only within their event/PR-or-branch lane, so a push cannot cancel an operator-requested integration run. The previous skip list incorrectly removed PDDA fixture/negative-control tests; those are restored, leaving only the exact duplicate `pdda-repo-contract.sh` out of the aggregate. The routing table is an **Easy-to-reverse but assumption-heavy coordination bet**: review it after 30 hosted runs and widen any path that proves under-classified. Local proof before the conflict-free current-base replay: `ci-route` 15/15, `ci-workflow` 22/22, full `validate.sh` 185/185 plus Python 20/20; current-base targeted checks are green. → [#509](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/509) · [PR #511](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/511)
