CHANGELOG.md-983-- **GH-349 + GH-346: marathon-plan accepted a typo'd flag as success, and stamped every generated plan with a hardcoded trunk.** Two front-door defects found while merge-reviewing #341, fixed together because they touch the same entry point. **(a) An unknown flag exited 0 on the lane that runs.** `utils/py/marathon_plan.py`'s `usage()` ended in an unconditional `sys.exit(0)`, which made the `die(f"unknown argument: {arg}")` on the very next line **unreachable** — so `utils/marathon-plan.sh --bogus` returned **0** on the default Python lane while the Bash twin returned 2. The practical bite is the drift gate: `utils/marathon-plan.sh --check --requre-gh || alert "plan drifted"` printed usage, compared nothing, and reported **success**. Same class as #322. Fixed by splitting printing from exiting — `print_usage()` prints and returns, `--help` calls it then exits 0, the unknown-argument branch calls it then `die()`s — which is exactly the Bash shape (`:102` prints only; `:139` is `usage; die "unknown argument: $1"`), so usage lands on stdout and the error on stderr on both lanes. **(b) `branch:` was the string literal `"main"`.** Reported against `rebalance-OS`, whose trunk is `development`, so every generated plan asserted a branch that exists but is not the trunk and is not where any lane would land — and of 41 docs in that repo's `PROJECT/2-WORKING`, only the two *generated* plans said `main`, so a reader had good reason to trust the field. **#346's own fix note was already stale when filed:** it said the Python lane had no `branch:` string of its own so fixing `:945` covered both, which was true only while `marathon_plan.py` shelled out to the copied JS — GH-340 (merged `1d06862`) replaced that with a native engine carrying its own `o.append("branch: main")` at `_marathon_plan.py:1151`. Both engines now derive it, and #348's newly-working parity gate is what makes "both" verifiable rather than hopeful. Deliberately the **trunk, not the current branch**: deriving `HEAD` would make `--check` report drift merely because someone cut a feature branch. Order is `QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCH` (override + hermetic test seam, since the suite's fixture roots are plain directories) → `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` with the prefix stripped (the same source `release-lanes.sh` uses) → `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` → `unknown`. The floor is `unknown` rather than `main` because PDDA does not require this key (`pdda.sh:39`) and no consumer was found — a wrong value is worse than an absent one, which is the whole complaint. New Scenarios **U** and **V** in `test/marathon-plan.sh`: **72 passed / 0 failed**, observed **65/7 against pre-fix sources**. The three pre-fix passes are each a thing that was already correct — usage already went to stdout, `--help` already exited 0, and the Bash lane already exited 2, that last being the entire premise of #349. V asserts neither engine still holds the literal, that a non-git root renders `branch: unknown`, that `QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCH` overrides on both lanes, and that **the whole rendered doc stays byte-identical across the two engines** — a derived value computed independently in two places is precisely the drift class #348 exists to catch. Checked by hand on the live 160-item ROADMAP too: both lanes emit the same 233-line doc. **Also corrected:** three `UPGRADE.md` spots (`:164`, the `:246` interpreter matrix, and `:251`'s "the 10 non-marathon-plan twins") still described `_marathon_plan_node.js`, which GH-340 deleted. Low severity — Node remains a baseline requirement via `bin/tick`, so the document's operative conclusion was never wrong — but two pointed at a path that no longer exists, and the carve-out had inverted: marathon-plan's Python lane is now the one entry point that does *not* need Node for its own work. → [GH-349-346-MARATHON-PLAN-CLEANUP.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-349-346-MARATHON-PLAN-CLEANUP.md) · [#349](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/349) · [#346](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/346)
CHANGELOG.md-984-- **GH-348: the repo's only Bash↔Python parity assertion compared the Python lane to the Python lane, and so could not fail.** `test/marathon-plan.sh`'s `run_qp()` invoked `bash "$QP"` and never set `XYZ_PYTHON`, while `utils/marathon-plan.sh:6` reads `${XYZ_PYTHON-1}` — **default 1**. So Scenario T, labelled *"matches between shell and `XYZ_PYTHON=1`"*, compared Python against Python. Proven by mutation, not by argument: corrupting the Bash engine's rendered banner at `utils/marathon-plan.sh:956` left the file at **60 passed / 0 failed**, both T assertions green. **Why this one mattered more than a generic coverage gap:** `marathon-plan` is the *deliberate* exception to GH-308's Python-authoritative policy — `utils/marathon-plan.sh` stays dual-maintained — so cross-lane drift here is a live risk that has already materialised twice, in **GH-154** (the copy missing the GH-48 zone model) and **GH-255** (two further gaps papered over by pre/post-processing *around* the copied program). Scenario T was added by GH-154 to prevent the third instance and never could. Surfaced while merge-reviewing #341, which cited Scenario T as its parity evidence; the port itself was still genuinely proven, by a live-ROADMAP comparison that sets `XYZ_PYTHON=0` explicitly. Fixed with three things, not one: a new **`run_qp_sh()`** forcing `XYZ_PYTHON=0` for T's left side (the other 58 cases deliberately keep `run_qp` — unset is what production runs, so they are correctly exercising the live lane); a **loud counted `SKIP`** when `node` is absent, since the Bash engine hard-requires it at `:146` and falling back to `run_qp` there would restore the exact tautology while looking like a pass; and an **in-run mutation self-check** that renders with a mutated copy of the Bash engine and asserts the difference *is* detected, so a future refactor cannot quietly point both sides at one lane again — with a failure message that names both possible causes instead of guessing one. **61/0** on a clean tree, and the mutation that previously left 60/0 now yields **59 passed / 2 failed**, which is the acceptance criterion the issue set. The dry-run half of T still passes under that particular mutation, correctly: the banner appears only in the rendered doc, which is why the self-check compares the doc. On a no-node PATH: 57/1/**2 skipped**, the one failure (`F: json lines not all valid`) reproducing identically pre-fix and left alone — Node is a hard baseline requirement (UPGRADE.md §2), so a no-node run is not a supported configuration. **Third instance this week of one shape:** an assertion comparing a thing to a freshly-derived copy of itself — this, #342 (GH-281's test `sed`-extracted the helpers from the *Bash* file, passing for a year while the shipped lane had zero references), and #351 (the dashboard test regenerates the artifact it then validates). In all three the output reads as coverage and the gap is invisible from the pass line. → [GH-348-MARATHON-PLAN-PARITY-GATE.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-348-MARATHON-PLAN-PARITY-GATE.md) · [#348](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/348)
CHANGELOG.md-985-- **GH-342: arming `XYZ_DEBUG_LOG=1` captured nothing, because the Sentinel Tier-1 hooks existed only on the lane that stopped running.** GH-281 shipped the Tier-1 debug capture into `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh`; that file `exec`s `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` near the top and Python is the default lane since GH-264, so `grep -c 'XYZ_DEBUG_LOG' utils/py/marathon_drive.py` was **0** and an operator arming the capture to diagnose a bad marathon got an empty `debug.log` — reasonably concluding there was nothing to capture. The last known item in the Bash-only class (#322 `--log-github`, #331 cost summary, #289 build-turn guard, and the 16 ported in #338); deliberately deferred by that audit and filed so the deferral would not evaporate. **Why it hid is the sharper finding:** GH-281's own acceptance test, `test/sentinel-driver-hooks.sh`, `sed`-extracts the helper functions out of the **Bash** file and sources them into a controlled shell — so it has always passed while asserting a lane nobody runs. A feature that is off by default and silently does nothing when switched on emits no signal in either state, and its test was pointed at the wrong lane. All six Bash sites are now ported into `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` at **module scope** (the GH-322 `runlog_find_comment_id` precedent — a helper reachable only through a full driven run has its format contract asserted by nothing): `xyz_debug_log_append` + `_json_esc`, the escalation hook, the lane-park hook (moved *inside* `lane_attempt_gate` before its `sys.exit(8)`, since the Python gate exits directly where the Bash caller emits on `rc==8`), the inline stale-lock record (emitted **before** the reclaim, so the finding survives a failed reclaim), and both `harvest-findings.sh` spawns in `escalate()` / `save_transcript()`. Preserved exactly: opt-in **default OFF** (only the literal `1` arms it), `DEBUG_LOG_FILE` honored including the empty-value fallback, the JSONL field order with its empty `line`, C0/DEL normalisation, and best-effort appends that can never change the driven run's exit code. **Two things reproduced rather than improved:** the stale-lock record's *shorter* 6-field shape with an unescaped `repo` (an artifact of the Bash helper not being defined that early in the file) is carried as-is — fixing it on one lane only would manufacture the very divergence this issue removes — and `json.dumps` was avoided because it is free to differ on separators and key order while the two lanes must emit identical bytes. New `test/gh342-sentinel-debug-log-python.sh` **29/0**, observed **2 pass / 11 fail against pre-fix code**, registered in `validate.sh`. Every case drives the **default** lane (`XYZ_PYTHON` unset) or the module directly; a case pinned to `XYZ_PYTHON=0` would have passed on day one for the wrong reason. Coverage includes default-off asserting the file's **absence** rather than its emptiness, cross-lane byte parity against the real extracted Bash helper (3 cases, incl. tab/quote/backslash/newline/NUL/DEL input and a `--target-root` run), **end-to-end** on the default lane via a real `--dry-run` over a stale driver lock, and a cross-lane end-to-end comparison — the case that would have caught this on day one. The read-only-directory case **skips loudly under root** instead of reporting a pass it did not earn. What is *not* claimed: the escalation and lane-park hooks sit past the `--dry-run` exit, so they carry an **AST assertion** that they are called from their real call sites plus record-level parity, and the test says so in place rather than implying end-to-end coverage. The Bash twin is untouched — **no `Frozen-twin-exception` spent.** One defect was caught in the test before it shipped: its Python block's tallies were not folded into the file's counters, so an in-heredoc failure would have printed in red and still left the file reporting `0 fail` — the same green-signal shape the test exists to close. → [GH-342-SENTINEL-DEBUG-LOG-PYTHON-LANE.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-342-SENTINEL-DEBUG-LOG-PYTHON-LANE.md) · [#342](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/342)
CHANGELOG.md-986-- **GH-332: the Phase 4 rollup reported a release as finished when it had barely started — it fetched each issue's open/closed state and threw it away.** The tool's very first real output was `Quicksilver: 1/1 landed`, off a milestone whose single issue is **#308, an OPEN multi-phase epic**, whose only claiming commit was `GH-308: re-scope Phase 0/1 after #278 was fixed dual-lane` — planning, not delivery. The scope matcher was doing exactly what it was designed to do; the bug was in what that answer was taken to mean. *"Has any commit claimed this issue?"* is a different question from *"is this issue finished?"*, and the second one already had an authoritative answer sitting unused in the JSON: **a human closed the issue.** Landing now requires both a claiming commit **and** a closed issue. A fourth bucket, `claimed-but-open` (rendered `IN FLIGHT`), carries the rest and is excluded from the `N/M landed` headline — Quicksilver now reads `0/1 landed` with one in flight, which is true. **Commit type is deliberately still not filtered:** #332 raised whether `docs(GH-N):`/`chore(GH-N):` should count as delivery at all, and the answer is no-change — it adds false negatives for genuinely doc-only issues and is the weaker signal, since a human closing an issue outranks a commit-message prefix; the type stays visible anyway because the evidence line prints the whole subject. `test/gh284-p4-release-lanes.sh` **34 pass / 4 fail against the shipped code → 38 / 0**, on a fixture carrying #308's real subject shape. Two of the new assertions exist only to stop the *tally* from lying: the `IN FLIGHT` count must be named in the summary, and the four buckets must sum to the total, so no state can silently vanish from the denominator. A bug in the test itself surfaced the same way — `state_of()` read the label with `awk '{print $1}'`, which the new two-word `IN FLIGHT` would have truncated to `IN`, and the `grep` feeding it would not have matched the row at all. → [GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md) · [#332](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/332)
CHANGELOG.md-987-- **GH-333: the run log's `driver still running` field could only ever say `running` — dropped, and the surviving exit code now says what it means.** The exit hook asked `driver_heartbeat_status()` *before* clearing the heartbeat, and the PID it tested belonged to the process doing the asking, which is alive by definition. The field was a constant wearing the clothes of a measurement — the exact shape this program keeps finding (#315, #319, #320, #322, #331). It was also in the wrong place: the comment is posted *at exit*, so it can never tell a reader whether a driver is alive now. The thing that answers that is the heartbeat **file**, which works and is untouched — this lane still writes and clears it, and the reader observers actually use (`rtl_driver_heartbeat_status`) lives in `relay-turn-lib.sh`, a shared runtime dependency rather than a frozen twin. Writer here, reader there, so removing the Python-side status function cost nothing. **Nothing was lost, because nothing was ever posted:** `--log-github` was Bash-only and inert on the default lane until #322's port landed the day before, and a scan of the likely lane issues found **zero** run-log comments in existence — so no reader breaks and no history is invalidated. The half worth keeping was folded into the neighbouring line, which was already carrying the useful signal as a bare number: `- driver exit: \`3\` (no-progress escalation)`. `_exit_meaning()` is at module scope, total (an unmapped code renders `unrecognised exit code` rather than an empty parenthetical that would read like a meaning), and maps 1/2/8 defensively even though lock contention, `die()` and the lane-attempt cap all exit before the run log arms and so can never appear in one. **Python only — the Bash twin keeps the old field, on purpose.** GH-308 froze the eleven Tier-A twins and AGENTS.md directs behavior fixes to the Python twin; editing `marathon-drive.sh` would have required a `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer, which #321 just narrowed to per-file declarations and which exists for *safety* defects (the GH-319 precedent), not cosmetic ones. Divergence in a frozen fallback slated for deletion is the intended outcome of that policy, not a new parity defect. `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh` 26/0 → **29/0**, asserting the gloss, the field's **absence** (re-adding it fails), and that the heartbeat writer survived the removal. `test/gh308-frozen-twin-guard.sh --check` confirms no frozen twin was touched. → [#333](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/333)
CHANGELOG.md-988-- **GH-322 (the port): GH-284 Phase 2 shipped in July and had never once executed — *both* halves lived only in the Bash twin.** #324 stopped `--log-github` being silently discarded; this makes it do something. `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh` `exec`s `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` at its own **line 18**, while the `EXIT` trap that runs the run log and stops the heartbeat is installed at **line 244** — so under the default lane (`XYZ_PYTHON` unset since GH-264) the process was replaced before either could ever be wired up. Every marathon since Phase 2 merged ran, exited 0, reported success, and observed nothing. **#322's own scope statement was wrong, and the correction is the substantive finding here:** it deferred only the run log on the grounds that "the driver heartbeat *is* already in the Python twin (12 references)" — those 12 matches are `xyz_marathon_heartbeat_*`, the **GH-75 `XYZ.heartbeat.json` session record**, an unrelated file and feature; `grep -c driver_heartbeat utils/py/marathon_drive.py` returned **0**. Two different features named "heartbeat" in one file, told apart only by prefix, is what let a grep agree with the wrong conclusion. Both halves are now ported: the heartbeat (write, refresh thread, clear, `RTL_DRIVER_HEARTBEAT_FILE` honored) writes a record byte-compatible with `rtl_driver_heartbeat_write` — same six fields, same atomic `mkstemp`+`os.replace` — so the Bash reader and the Python writer agree; and `--log-github` is a real flag with `run_gate_result` tracking behind it. Exit handling mirrors the Bash trap's contract exactly (code resolved first, hooks in a `finally`, original code re-exited), so reporting can never change the driven run's result. `runlog_find_comment_id` sits at **module scope**: in Bash the same parser could only be reached through a `python3` subprocess, and the invocation shape itself (SC2259) silently broke it for a release — in-process kills the failure class, and importable means the test drives the real function instead of a copy of its logic. New `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh` (**5 pass / 19 fail against pre-change code, 26 / 0 after**) is the counterpart to `test/gh284-runlog-heartbeat.sh`, every driver invocation in which is pinned to `XYZ_PYTHON=0` — which is exactly why that suite could not see any of this; the new file `unset XYZ_PYTHON`s deliberately. `test/gh322-unknown-arg-rejection.sh`'s `--log-github` block was **inverted**: "refuse loudly and name the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` workaround" was an interim contract, and a lane that still refused a flag it now implements would be the bug. **Deliberately left as-is:** the run log's `driver still running` field can only ever read `running` — the hook asks for status *before* clearing the heartbeat, and the PID it checks is the process asking. The Bash twin has the identical ordering (`:238` then `:239`), so it is inherited, not introduced, and porting it faithfully beats opening a silent twin divergence — the exact disease #320 and #322 are. → [GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md) · [#322](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/322)
CHANGELOG.md:989:- **GH-320: the executing Python lane capped turns at a third of the documented budget.** An agy review turn died with `agy -p exceeded 300s wall-clock cap` on a shim whose header *and* code both read 900. XYZ has been Python-default since GH-264, so `relay-automation/agy-turn.sh` `exec`s `utils/py/agy-turn.py` — which defaulted to **300**. Same split in `codex-turn` (900↔300) and `claude-turn` (600↔300); `aider-turn` and `pi-turn` were consistent. Because Python is the lane that runs, 300 s was the **real** ceiling for three of five turn-takers while every operator-facing document said otherwise, and the failure surfaces as `exit 7` — *turn timeout / hang* — which reads as a hung model rather than a misconfigured ceiling. The natural response to that, retrying, burns another turn at the same wrong cap. **GH-308's freeze does not cover this class:** freezing the Bash twins stops them drifting *forward* and says nothing about values that had already diverged before the banners landed; nothing in the suite compared the two numbers. Fixed by aligning the three Python defaults with their twins. New `test/gh320-twin-timeout-parity.sh` reads the default out of **both** files for all five shims and compares them — **no expected value is hardcoded**, since a third copy of the number would just be a third thing to drift — and separately asserts that each Bash header's documented `(default: N)` matches that file's own code, because the header is what misled. 10 pass / 0 fail. **Deliberately still open:** nothing establishes the turn timeout was the only constant that diverged pre-freeze; a general Bash↔Python constant-parity sweep belongs to GH-308 Phase 2. → [GH-320-TWIN-TURN-TIMEOUT-DRIFT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-320-TWIN-TURN-TIMEOUT-DRIFT.md) · [#320](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/320)
CHANGELOG.md-990-- **GH-321: the frozen-twin escape hatch was range-scoped — one trailer excused every twin edit in the PR.** The `Frozen-twin-exception:` hatch shipped in PR #318 passed the guard for **every** frozen twin touched in `BASE..HEAD` as soon as *any* commit in the range carried the trailer — including files nobody reasoned about, in commits that declared nothing, possibly by a different author. CI then printed `1 commit(s) declare Frozen-twin-exception — allowing:` and listed the **declaring** commit, so the log read like a narrow reviewed exception while the undeclared edit was **never named**. The trailer's whole value is making an exception auditable, and range scoping broke exactly that property in the case where it counts. Marathon PRs are the common case and the worst shape for it: 4+ autonomous lanes on one branch make an undeclared twin edit riding behind someone else's declared exception the expected accident, not an exotic one. Same class as #319 and #315 — *a green signal that means less than it appears, with nothing in the output revealing the gap* — and it was disclosed at merge time rather than found later. A trailer must now **name the twin(s) it covers** (`Frozen-twin-exception: relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh — <reason>`), and every changed twin in the range must be named by some trailer; failures name the uncovered file. **The rule moved out of inline `ci.yml` shell and into the guard script as `--allow-exceptions`** — inline YAML is unreachable from the suite, which is part of why the looseness shipped at all; `ci.yml` is now a single call. Per-file *across the range*, deliberately not "the trailer must be on the same commit as the edit": a later fixup correcting an earlier commit is ordinary and should not need re-declaration, and what the looseness actually cost was attribution, which naming the file recovers. A typo'd path fails loudly rather than silently covering nothing; the bare path-less form no longer covers anything (that form *is* the looseness); reason text is not scanned for paths, so a reason may cite `validate.sh` without being read as a coverage claim; strict mode (what `validate.sh` and `--staged` use) is unchanged. `test/gh308-frozen-twin-guard.sh` **15/0 → 27/0**, with a fixture built on **two** frozen twins because with one the range-scoped and file-scoped rules are indistinguishable — which is how this shipped. One case **reproduces** the defect rather than only asserting its absence: it evaluates #318's exact predicate on the same fixture and asserts it *would* have allowed the PR, so the suite says so if the fixture ever stops exercising the bug. The single historical trailer (`07ae1e7`) is the bare form and would fail this rule; it is already merged and CI only judges an open PR's own range, so no existing history is re-evaluated. → [#321](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/321)
CHANGELOG.md-991-- **PR #318 agy review: two Blockers closed, one Should implemented differently, one declined.** The review of the marathon PR was itself driven through the harness (`--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`, exit 5 = changes requested). Both Blockers were re-verified against source before being acted on. **(1)** `AGENTS.md` asserted that "CI supplies `GH308_FROZEN_TWIN_BASE`" — `grep -rn GH308_FROZEN_TWIN_BASE .github/` returned **0 matches**, so the frozen-twin guard had no enforcement anywhere. Added the `Frozen Bash twin guard (GH-308)` step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, with a `Frozen-twin-exception: <reason>` commit trailer as the documented escape hatch so a legitimate exception is auditable in `git log` rather than invisible. **(2)** The reviewer argued a silently-fake safety gate outranks the freeze policy, so `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh:493` is patched too — but the obvious shape was wrong: `printf '%q'` is eval-safe yet backslash-escapes the space rather than removing it, so the preflight regex at `:511` still captured `.../GH\` and would have `die`d "script file does not exist", trading a false pass for a hard failure. Single-quoting is eval-safe *and* regex-tractable, and is byte-identical to `shlex.quote()`'s output for the same path; the preflight regex now matches a fully quoted token. `test/gh319-gate-path-with-space.sh` drives **both** lanes — the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` cases fail against pre-fix Bash (7/2) and pass after (9/0). **(3)** The proposed fix for the GH-293 guard-marker fragility required editing `relay-drive.sh`, a frozen twin, to satisfy a `[Should]` — the wrong trade; the manifest now matches the guard's user-facing **diagnostic** (`turn cannot report: relay file`), which does not get reflowed. The underlying point was sharper than the example: `test/gh293-vendored-guard-drift.sh` was itself restating the old literal, so a manifest change would have left the test green while the guard check was dead — the fixture now **derives** the pattern from `SAFETY_GUARD_PATTERNS` and asserts it stripped something (15/0). **(4)** Declined the suggestion to isolate `test/pdda-repo-contract.sh` from `validate.sh`: CI already fails the PR on those errors, so the coupling predates the change — what changed is finding out locally in 8 minutes instead of after a push, which is precisely what GH-311 exists to fix.
CHANGELOG.md-992-- **GH-319: every marathon phase reported "gate passed" without the gate ever running — the default gate word-split on the space in the repo's own path and executed an unrelated 0-byte file.** `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` built its default gate as an unquoted string (`f"bash {root}/validate.sh"`) and handed it to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. At a clone under `.../Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm` the shell split on the space and ran `bash $HOME/Documents/GH`, passing `Repos/.../validate.sh` as a positional argument. **`$HOME/Documents/GH` exists on this machine as a 0-byte file**, so bash executed an empty script: exit 0, no output, 0.0 s. Reproduced in isolation before anything was changed. **All four lanes of the 2026-07-27 gate-and-fleet-integrity marathon were approved with no gate**, while `bash validate.sh` on that exact tree was RED with two genuine failures (`relay-pkg-freshness`, `skill-extract` — GH-308's freeze banners had drifted `relay-pkg.tar.gz`). It was caught by timing, not by any signal the harness emits: `.tick/events/` showed **6.6 s and 7.5 s** between `agy-done` and `marathon.phase.approved` against a **483 s** real suite. **GH-238's gate-runnable preflight — which exists for exactly this — did not fire**, because its `^\s*(bash|/\S*/bash)\s+(\S+)` regex captured the same wrong fragment and `os.path.isfile()` on the decoy returned `True`; the guard and the gate agreed on the wrong file, and the preflight even carried quote-stripping logic for a quoted argument the default never produced. This is the third instance of one failure class in this program, after GH-315 (a stale relay token let a build-nothing run report success) and the sandboxed-`Monitor` liveness gap folded into GH-284 Phase 2: **a broken observation layer where failure is invisible and every available signal agrees.** Fixed with `shlex.quote` on the default path and `shlex.split` in the preflight, so the runnability check inspects the file the shell would actually execute. **Regression coverage was written to demonstrate the bug, not merely assert the fix** — `test/gh319-gate-path-with-space.sh` builds its fixture at a spaced path *and plants the same 0-byte decoy at the split point*, so a regression cannot hide behind a split prefix that happens not to exist; against pre-fix code the driver prints `phase p1 complete — STATUS: Approved, gate passed` and exits 0 while the fixture's gate exits 1 (4 pass / 2 fail), and post-fix it is 6/0 with the driver exiting 5. Registered in `validate.sh`. **Deliberately not fixed:** `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh:493` has the identical construction, but GH-308 froze that file in this same PR and AGENTS.md now directs behavior fixes to the Python twin — so an `XYZ_PYTHON=0` run at a spaced path still has a fake gate until GH-308 Phase 2 retires the twin. Historical marathon runs on this machine that reported "gate passed" are retroactively unverified; no audit of them is planned. Full `./validate.sh` 131/131, 0 FAIL lines, exit 0. → [GH-319-MARATHON-GATE-PATH-WORD-SPLIT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-319-MARATHON-GATE-PATH-WORD-SPLIT.md) · [#319](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/319)
CHANGELOG.md-993-- **MARATHON-2026-07-27 (gate + fleet integrity) fired: 4 sequential lanes, all approved, PR #318.** `gh311 → gh289 → gh293 → gh308`, builder codex / reviewer agy throughout, 2 turns per lane (4 for gh293). Each deliverable was verified by direct inspection of the diff against its brief rather than by the runner's summary line — which is how GH-319 surfaced. **GH-311** adds `test/pdda-repo-contract.sh`, running `utils/pdda/pdda.sh run` against the repo's real docs so `validate.sh` becomes a superset of tier1's PDDA contract; it immediately earned its place by catching two real errors in this changelog's own capture doc (a hardcoded `$HOME` path and a missing ROADMAP pointer). **GH-289** widens GH-245's fast-refusal from `--review-once` to every `--target-root` turn, so a BUILD turn refuses at startup instead of completing and discarding its Log; the `--review-once` diagnostic is preserved verbatim. **GH-293** adds a behavior-marker safety-guard manifest to `xyz-sync check` (a missing guard is now distinguishable from ordinary provenance drift, inspected in the installed copy rather than inferred from `source_commit`) and makes `update --all` refuse a dirty or non-canonical harness source without `XYZ_SYNC_ALLOW_UNSAFE_SOURCE=1`. **GH-308 Phase 1** stamps FROZEN banners on the 11 Tier-A Bash twins and records the policy in AGENTS.md/UPGRADE.md — no deletions, `XYZ_PYTHON=0` still reversible, with `utils/marathon-plan.sh` and `relay-turn-lib.sh` explicitly exempt. `relay-pkg.tar.gz` rebuilt (the freeze banners drift it). → [MARATHON.yaml](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-2026-07-27-GATE-AND-FLEET-INTEGRITY/MARATHON.yaml) · [#318](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/318)
CHANGELOG.md-994-- **GH-312: `xyz-sync update` / `xyz-vendor.sh` silently destroyed the target repo's live runtime state — fixed by preserving it across the vendor swap, with three more at-risk paths than the report identified.** `materialize_vendor()` builds a staged mirror of the harness and swaps it in over an unconditional `rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR"`. The stage is mirrored purely from `$HARNESS_ROOT`, so everything the *target* accumulated at runtime was deleted unread — and since `ensure_gitignore` keeps `.xyz/` out of git, nothing under it was ever hashed into a git object, leaving **no reflog, stash, or `git fsck --lost-found` recovery**. It exited 0 and printed success. A real incident on 2026-07-27 destroyed a completed two-round Codex relay thread plus its full `.tick/` event log; the findings survived only because the Codex CLI transcripts happen to live in `$TMPDIR`, outside the harness. **The intake report's requested fix was incomplete:** it named `relay-system/`, `.tick/`, and `.relay-driver.lock`, but auditing what `.xyz/` actually accumulates (repo `.gitignore` + GH-75) turned up the completion-telemetry family — `XYZ.json` (the locked record array, 1.8 MB and actively written on the reporting machine), `XYZ.json.lock/` (its `mkdir` advisory lock), and `XYZ.heartbeat.json` — with **identical exposure**: none are in `VENDOR_DIRS`, so the stage never recreated them either. Implementing the report literally would have left the bug half-fixed; the shipped preserve list carries **six** paths, and a failed copy now `die`s *before* the destructive swap rather than proceeding. Preservation was chosen over a warning or a refusal because both still depend on an operator reading output at the right moment, and the docs frame `update` as deliberate (pinned + manual) but never as destructive. **Regression coverage was written first and observed failing** — new `test/gh312-vendor-preserves-state.sh` produced 6 failures against the pre-fix code and passes 14/14 post-fix — and it pins the *other* half of the contract too: VERSION must still restamp to live HEAD and `bin/tick` must survive, so a "fix" that preserved state by skipping the update cannot pass. It also covers the direct `xyz-vendor.sh` re-run over an existing `.xyz/`, which the capture flagged as an unverified open question and which had the same destructive swap (**answered: yes**). Docs: `xyz-sync.sh`'s header and `skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md` now state what `update` does to runtime state and that a new `.xyz/` artifact must join the preserve list. Reviewed by **agy** through a driven relay (`--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`): Approved with 4 `[Pass]` findings and no defects raised — disclosed as a clean but shallow signal, not independent corroboration. `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` rebuilt via `make-pkg.sh` (the fix touches `relay-automation/`, which drifts the vendored tarball); `relay-pkg-freshness.sh` 3/3 and full `./validate.sh` green (10 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped). **Deliberately still open:** whether durable runtime state belongs under a disposable, gitignored `.xyz/` at all — the capture's own sharper question, listed in its `non_goals`, and **not** closed by this fix. → [GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md) · [#312](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/312)
CHANGELOG.md-995-- **GH-304: relay-drive turn-taker prompt + worktree seeding used a CWD-relative relay-file path — broke same-repo vendored `.xyz/` installs for Codex.** Scaffolding/driving a relay from CWD=`.xyz` (the relay-xyz skill's documented `cd "$HARNESS"`) with a CWD-relative `--relay-file` embedded that raw string in the turn-taker's prompt and used it for worktree seeding. Since a same-repo vendored `.xyz/` has no `.git` of its own, the turn-taker's worktree roots at the *outer* repo top-level, where `relay-system/…` doesn't exist (the file is at `.xyz/relay-system/…`) — a 100% failure for Codex, masked for agy (which absolutizes the path itself). Fix: `relay-drive.sh` and `utils/py/relay_drive.py` now **absolutize `$RELAY_FILE` before exporting it** to the turn-taker (mirrors the existing `--artifact-file` handling), so it resolves identically from any CWD; `rtl_turn_prompt` (`relay-turn-lib.sh`) derives the repo-root-relative EDIT path robustly (physical-path strip, matching `rtl_init`'s allowlist normalization) so the embedded path and the seeded path stay in lockstep at the true `.xyz/relay-system/…`. **Secondary:** when the relay file is gitignored (this repo gitignores parts of `relay-system/`), `rtl_enforce`'s empty-commit case now prints a distinct "relay file is gitignored, changes are NOT git-tracked (expected, not a stall)" message instead of the ambiguous "no tracked changes (token-only move?)" that a passing and a failing run printed byte-identically. Proof: new `test/gh304-vendored-relay-path.sh` (11/11) unit-tests the allowlist normalization, prompt path, worktree seeding, and both empty-commit messages; related relay/worktree tests green locally. → [#304](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/304)
CHANGELOG.md-996-- **GH-295: PR #302 tier1 CI — two real gaps found and fixed.** `test/pi-turn.sh`'s fake `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` test fixtures ("test-key"/"test-key-not-real") were never added to `security-scan-baseline.txt`, tripping the GH-64 active gate (same pattern already baselined for `aider-turn.sh`/`deep-research.sh`). Separately, `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` had drifted from an earlier README edit on this branch and was never rebuilt, tripping `test/relay-pkg-freshness.sh`. Both fixed; `security-scan.sh`/`relay-pkg-freshness.sh` green locally.
CHANGELOG.md-997-- **GH-300: swe-diagram search input no longer touches/overflows the font-picker when typing — two distinct bugs found and fixed, same symptom family.** **(1)** `.swe-search-input` uses `type="search"` but never reset `-webkit-appearance`, so WebKit's native searchfield cancel-button decoration could override the field's explicit 180px width once it had text — the renderer already ships its own custom `.swe-search-clear` button, making the native chrome pure downside. Fixed via `-webkit-appearance: none` + explicit `::-webkit-search-cancel-button`/`::-webkit-search-decoration` resets in `utils/swe-diagram/assets/template.html`. Not independently re-verified in Safari (no automation available in this environment) — a headless-Chrome regression check confirms no change there, since Chrome doesn't exhibit the underlying bug in the first place. **(2) Found on operator re-report** (the box still visibly touched the picker on the very first keystroke, no resize needed — but resizing afterward fixed it, the key clue): `positionPicker()` only ran on page load, font-picker change, and window resize — never on the search box's own `input` event — so when the custom clear button appeared (growing the right-anchored `.swe-search` row leftward), the picker never got told to move; a resize masked the bug by incidentally recomputing from the now-grown width. Fixed by having `renderer.js`'s search `input`/clear handlers dispatch a `swe-search-resize` event on the persistent `#diagram` node, which `template.html` listens for alongside its existing triggers. **Verified quantitatively, not just visually**: headless-Chrome bounding-rect measurement showed a healthy 8px gap before typing collapsing to a -22px overlap after typing (fix 1 alone), now a constant 8px with no resize needed — and since this is plain DOM sizing/event logic rather than a WebKit quirk, the Chrome verification here is directly conclusive. `test/swe-diagram.sh` 42/42 throughout; every `ARCHITECTURE/*.html` output rebuilt after each fix. → [GH-300-SWE-DIAGRAM-SEARCH-INPUT-OVERFLOW.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-300-SWE-DIAGRAM-SEARCH-INPUT-OVERFLOW.md) · [#300](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/300)

CHANGELOG.md-1000-- **GH-299: new `trust-clustered` swe-diagram layout — the only one of 4 supported modes that clears all 5 readability acceptance criteria on the real architecture spec.** Baselined the real spec (`ARCHITECTURE/system-diagram.json`) under all 3 existing layouts first (layered/top-down/hub-ring — the latter two regenerated since they were stale, predating the 2026-07-09 trust-boundary additions): none cleared all criteria — hub-ring is structurally disqualified since group swimlanes are unsupported in that mode, and both hub-ring and top-down failed hub-dominance and label clarity. Per the plan's own escalation path, added `trustClusteredLayout()` to `utils/swe-diagram/assets/renderer.js`: bands nodes into 5 fixed columns derived from each node's existing `trust` field (Orchestration Spine / Turn-Shim Cluster / Untrusted Periphery / Shared State / Off-Live-Path Governance & Audit) rather than graph rank or author-chosen `group`, floats the containment core to the top of the spine column next to its dispatcher, wraps tiers past 6 members into sub-columns, and gives the containment-core node an emphasized border so it reads as a hub at a glance. Also added a generic edge-label-overlap avoidance pass (`placeLabelRect` in `drawEdges()`) after the baseline inspection found real label-on-label collisions in the busy periphery/shared-state boundary — a greedy vertical nudge against node rects + already-placed label rects, applied to all layouts, not just this one; re-screenshotted the other 3 layouts to confirm no regression. New sibling artifact `ARCHITECTURE/system-diagram-trust-clustered.json`/`.html` (additive; the default `system-diagram.html` is untouched). `test/swe-diagram.sh` 42/42 (10 new cases for `trustTierOf`/`trustClusteredLayout`). `./validate.sh` clean except 2 pre-existing, unrelated environmental reds (`acorn-extract.sh` missing the `acorn` npm module, `python:test_python_layer.py` 2/121 — neither touched by this change). → [GH-299-DIAGRAM-TRUST-LAYOUT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-299-DIAGRAM-TRUST-LAYOUT.md) · [#299](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/299)

CHANGELOG.md-1003-- **GH-296: `relay-drive.sh`/turn-shim EPERM on the tick lock in a same-repo vendored `.xyz/` install — root-caused as a regression via incomplete Python port, not a fresh instance of #263.** Captured via `/file-xyz-bug` from `pdda`; a Codex review turn driven against an artifact outside the vendored `.xyz/` failed to claim the tick token under both worktree-isolation settings. **#263's fix genuinely landed** in the Bash `relay-automation/codex-turn.sh` (commit `8c361a0`) — but this repo later flipped its default turn-shim runtime from Bash to Python (GH-264, `af7bb4d`), *after* #263 shipped, and `utils/py/codex-turn.py` — the file that actually executes by default now — never received the #263/GH-36 fix at all, and separately defaulted its own `root` variable to the harness's own directory (`XYZ_ROOT`) instead of falling back to the CWD's git toplevel the way the Bash version does. Confirmed via `git stash`/rerun: pre-fix, the new regression test reproduced the exact bogus `--add-dir <wrong>/.tick` sandbox path from the original bug report. Fixed: new `resolve_turn_root()` helper in `utils/py/rtl.py` (explicit override → CWD git toplevel → `XYZ_ROOT` fallback, mirroring Bash) used by `codex-turn.py`'s `root`; its `--add-dir` sandbox flag now builds off `tick_repo_root` unconditionally (both isolation states), porting #263's actual intent. **Follow-up folded into the same fix (not filed as a separate issue — same root cause, found while reviewing this one):** `agy-turn.py`/`claude-turn.py` shared the identical `root` defect, manifesting as their own pre-launch `tick claim --paths` call computing an escaping `../../../relay.md`-style path instead of a clean repo-relative one (the shared bridge into `relay-turn-lib.sh`'s worktree/containment logic already self-corrects a subdirectory root via the existing GH-160 fix, so this only bit the native, unbridged Python computation, `rtl.claim_paths_for_turn`). A second, independent bug surfaced while building the regression test for this: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns the *physical* path (macOS resolves `/var`/`/tmp` symlinks to `/private/var`/`/private/tmp`), which could mismatch a caller-supplied `relay_file` still in unresolved logical form — the same GH-51 physical/logical-path class of bug `relay-turn-lib.sh` already guards against on the bridged side, ported natively into `claim_paths_for_turn` via `os.path.realpath()` on both sides of the comparison. 5 new/extended regression cases across `test/{codex,agy,claude}-turn.sh` — each independently verified to **fail against the pre-fix code and pass post-fix** via a `git stash`/rerun/`stash pop` cycle, not just written and trusted. Also caught and fixed along the way: editing `test/*.sh` drifted the bundled `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz`, caught by `relay-pkg-freshness.sh` — rebuilt via `make-pkg.sh`. Full `validate.sh`: only the two long-standing, unrelated environmental reds remain (`acorn-extract.sh` missing the `acorn` npm module, `python:test_python_layer.py` missing `pytest`, neither installed in this local clone) — confirmed neither test file references any of the touched files. **Related, not verified:** the fix may also resolve the open #272 (same `TICK_REPO_ROOT`-in-vendored-lane root-cause family, a different symptom — a successful turn whose `tick release` lands in the wrong namespace) — flagged in the doc for a human to confirm separately. → [GH-296-RELAY-DRIVE-TICK-EPERM.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-296-RELAY-DRIVE-TICK-EPERM.md) · [#296](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/296) · [#263](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/263)

Only two real gaps remained. **(4)** `artifacts_exist_for_timeout()` (`marathon-drive.sh`) / `artifacts_exist()` (`marathon_drive.py`) checked file existence only, so a killed/no-op builder turn's 0-byte pre-created stub passed as "artifact appeared" — fixed by generalizing the existing `requires_test_delta()` non-empty+git-delta pattern (`path_has_nonempty_phase_delta()`) to the artifact-appeared check too, in both runtimes, preserving `--requires-test`'s existing contract byte-for-byte. **(6a)** `aider-turn.sh`/`aider-turn.py`'s `AIDER_OPENAI_API_BASE` seam passed the API key as a literal `--openai-api-key` CLI argument, visible to any local `ps` call — fixed by passing it via the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable instead (which Aider/LiteLLM reads natively), dropping the CLI flag. Fired via `swarm-preflight → marathon-drive` (Codex builder, agy reviewer). **Process note:** the first turn implemented both fixes correctly and added solid regression coverage (verified: key absent from captured argv AND present in the subprocess env; zero-byte and unchanged-artifact cases both correctly classified as no-progress), but also made two off-allowlist edits — a `CHANGELOG.md` entry and a rewrite of an unrelated, concurrently-open `utils/swe-diagram/NEW.md` scratch file — both correctly caught and reverted by containment (exit 6). CHANGELOG.md:1007:- **GH-280: Aider+Qwen reliability investigation concluded — root cause found and fix confirmed.** A live GH-268 Wave-1 exercise against the real production repo and the real `qwen3.8-max-preview` endpoint caught the first real failure transcript of the whole investigation: Aider auto-selects `whole` edit format for unlisted/custom model ids, but Qwen emits standard unified diffs regardless, which Aider silently discards as "no tracked changes" — the actual explanation for the historical ~86% aider-qwen failure rate, not general model unreliability. Re-running with `AIDER_FLAGS="--edit-format diff"` forced took the same task from 0/3 real edits to a 90%-complete, correct implementation landing in round 1, confirming the fix. Getting to this transcript required first closing a real observability gap: `aider-turn.sh` (and, since `XYZ_PYTHON` defaults on, the actually-executing `utils/py/aider-turn.py` and `utils/py/agy-turn.py`) were never using the GH-161 persistent-log helper, so every prior investigation round genuinely could not have captured a failure log — fixed in [#288](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/288)/[#290](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/290). Also found and fixed along the way, independent of Qwen: a fully-retired OpenRouter default model id (`openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`) that silently broke any plain `aider`/`consult` call omitting both `AIDER_MODEL` and `AIDER_OPENAI_API_BASE` — [#291](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/291), no separate issue filed. **Recommendation:** codex+agy remains the default builder pairing; Aider+Qwen is usable as a fallback with `--edit-format diff` and a generous timeout set explicitly. A separate, genuinely new gap was surfaced by the same session and filed on its own: `swarm-preflight.sh`'s suggested marathon invocations never default to `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=1` — [#294](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/294) (filed, not yet fired). → [GH-280 findings](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-280-AIDER-QWEN-VS-SONNET-INVESTIGATION.md) · [marathon plan](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-2026-07-23-GH279-GH280-AIDER-QWEN-FOLLOWUP.md) · [#280](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/280)

CHANGELOG.md-1027-- **GH-255: `UPGRADE.md` hardened by a SECOND independent `/relay-xyz` review — Codex, 5 rounds to Approved, 9 real blockers + 6 shoulds fixed that the agy pass missed.** Ran Codex as a different-model reviewer over the already-agy-Approved doc; it found substantially more, all verified against the repo before fixing. **Blockers:** the `python3 --version` "gate" didn't enforce the >=3.8 floor (3.7 passed) → executable predicate; `git fetch origin <branch>` could leave `origin/<branch>` stale → bare `git fetch origin`; the locator was referenced by a non-existent root path → concrete `skills/relay-xyz/find-harness.sh` (+ `.xyz/` variant); **Codex caught a bug in one of my own fixes** — a `python3 -c … || { echo; }` guard whose `||` swallowed the failure and continued → rewrote §2 as a real accumulator `preconditions.sh` that fails closed (behaviorally proven); per-copy permanent rollback that `git -C <root> revert`ed the *shared* live root → isolated `git worktree add <flip-sha>^` re-vendor; the §2(c) parity gate pointed at GH-255 instead of being runnable → embedded a `comm -13` Python-attributable-failure computation; the gate could **false-pass** if `validate.sh` aborted before its summary (empty set looks clean) → footer-completion guard; the Phase-2 shim guard checked python3 *presence* but not the *>=3.8 version* → version-enforcing guard; and the Type-B (vendored leaf) path was internally non-executable (told to skip only Phases 1 & 3 while Phases 2 & 4 are also root-only) → leaf now runs **none** of Phases 1–4, receive-and-verify only. **The deepest correction:** the interpreter matrix claimed the 10 non-marathon-plan twins were "python3 only" — but `bin/tick` is a Node program (`bin/tick:1`) that **both** the Bash drivers (`relay-drive.sh:42`) and the Python twins shell to, so Node was always a whole-harness baseline and the "flip 10 without Node" escape hatch was incoherent; removed it. **Shoulds** covered the honest external-tool deps (`date`/`sed`/`bash`/`consult.sh`), the `xyz-sync check` semantics (metadata-only drift, so don't hand-edit `.xyz/` because the next `update` overwrites it — not because `check` catches it), and propagating the Node/marathon-plan/Type-B corrections consistently across §0/§9/§10. Final Codex verdict: 4× `[Pass]`, 0 open. **Process note:** the closing turn hit driver exit 6 (GH-141) because I hand-edited the tree mid-review; the containment guard reverted it and the orphan-backup mechanism preserved the content — re-applied in the close commit. Thread: `relay-system/2026-07-20/upgrade-doc-review-codex.md`. → [#255](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/255)

CHANGELOG.md-1034-- **GH-258: `vendor-stack` skill — one-step XYZ harness + PDDA governance install into a target repo.** New `skills/vendor-stack/` (SKILL.md + `find-pdda.sh` + `install.sh`) orchestrates the two independent installers rather than reimplementing either: it vendors the XYZ harness into `<target>/.xyz/` via `relay-automation/xyz-vendor.sh`, then **asks** the operator whether to also install the PDDA doc-governance runtime and, if yes, runs the pdda clone's `install.sh` in observe mode. **Design fork the operator raised — prompt + PDDA path resolution live at the skill layer, not baked into `xyz-vendor.sh`:** that script is copied verbatim into every vendored `.xyz/` and runs headlessly from marathon/relay automation, so teaching it to find and run PDDA would ship dead cross-repo resolution logic to machines with no pdda clone and put an interactive prompt inside a must-stay-non-interactive script. Each tool keeps its own installer and its own per-user upgrade registry (`~/.config/xyz/registry.tsv`, `~/.config/pdda/registry.tsv`), so `xyz-sync check/update` and `pdda-sync status/push` carry updates forward independently — the skill just runs them in sequence. `find-pdda.sh` is a device-agnostic resolver mirroring `relay-xyz/find-harness.sh` (env override → harness sibling `<harness-parent>/pdda` → conventional `~/…/pdda` paths; no hardcoded machine path), and an unresolved pdda clone downgrades to XYZ-only with a note, never a hard error. **Verification:** `find-pdda.sh --check` resolves the pdda clone both via the harness-sibling rule and via `PDDA_REPO` override; `bash -n` clean on both scripts; XYZ was vendored into `hyper-pandas-python-stack` (`.xyz/` present, `bin/tick` runs, `.xyz/` gitignored, registry row written) as the original driving task. Retroactive intake: the skill was authored first, then issue #258 + the `1-INBOX` capture were filed to bring the work into PDDA compliance per the issue-first SOP. → [#258](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/258) · [GH-258-VENDOR-STACK-SKILL.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-258-VENDOR-STACK-SKILL.md)

Three findings shaped the decision. (1) **Asymmetry:** GH-211 reworked *only* consult's summary (`skills/consult/SKILL.md`); relay's operator report lives in the external `giant-brains-claude-skills` repo and was never touched — so there is nothing to coordinate against there yet, which is why that repo boundary is deferred, not opened. (2) **The Q3 target signal already exists:** `consult.sh` already computes `FIRSTHAND_COUNT` + a prompt-echoed classifier into a `*.PROVENANCE.txt` sidecar (GH-235), surfaced only as a `warn()`, never rendered into the report — so the next pass is *surface + placement*, not a new classifier. (3) **Dual bash+Python surface:** every provenance mechanic exists in both `relay-automation/*.sh` and the `utils/py/*.py` parity ports, so any stamp change lands in two places. **Contract locked** per Jedi's thread answers (2026-07-20): firsthand-read-vs-operator-asserted is the primary key (prompt-only conclusions flagged `conditional`), cited-vs-uncited demoted to a secondary affordance; provenance renders in the Disagree/adjudication body + inline `Sorted categories` notes, **never the TLDR**; consult (advisor grounding) and relay (reviewer citation discipline) keep separate stamp contracts on a shared surface — a split the inventory confirms already holds in code. **Q4 decided one issue, two disjoint lanes** — Lane C (`skills/consult/SKILL.md`, `relay-automation/consult.sh`, `utils/py/consult.py`) and Lane R (`relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh` + `new-relay.sh`), only shared dependency the single-sourced `rtl_has_uncited_claim` predicate (Wave-1 deliverable Lane C consumes). Planning marathon Plan I closed (both phases done); fireable Plan M drafted and **held — not promoted, not fired**. **Honest caveat carried into Plan M:** the "signal already exists, just needs surfacing" premise is read from the code and its GH-235 comments, *not* confirmed by a live consult run — flagged for a quick live check before Wave 2. Docs: [GH-226 capture doc](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-226-PROVENANCE-SUMMARY-SURFACE-COORDINATION.md) (§ Inventory / § Decision), [Plan I](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-2026-07-17-I-PROVENANCE-SUMMARY-COORDINATION.md), [Plan M](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-2026-07-20-M-GH226-PROVENANCE-IMPL.md). Coordinates with #178/#211/#235. → [#226](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/226)
CHANGELOG.md-1036-- **GH-255: `TEST_SOFT_FAIL=1` — first complete `XYZ_PYTHON=1` run of `validate.sh`; 10 test files fail *only* under Python, where the tracked blocker list held one.** The suite had never run to completion in Python mode. Two layers of fail-fast were conflated: `validate.sh`'s top level was *already* not fail-fast (it collects `FAILED`), but `test/_setup.sh`'s `fail()` called `exit 1` on the first failed assertion — the exact mechanism that hid [#223](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/223) behind [#215](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/215). Added opt-in `TEST_SOFT_FAIL=1` (default-off; fail-fast byte-identical when unset). **Second, non-obvious half:** most tests end in a bare `exit 0` — correct under fail-fast, a *false green* under soft-fail — so the `_setup.sh` EXIT trap now re-asserts non-zero when `FAIL > 0`, preserving `$?` verbatim when the flag is unset. Verified all three paths: passing test → 0, flag-unset failing test → exit 1 with one FAIL line, flag-on → exit 1 with all of them. **A same-commit Bash baseline was run and subtracted**, without which pre-existing failures get misattributed to the port: baseline 114/116 (2 files, 9 assertions) vs. Python 104/116 (12 files, 62), at HEAD `607dd7c`. Three findings outrank the rest. (1) **`agy-turn.py` fails open on containment** — `genuine breach should exit 5, got 0`; Bash fails the turn, Python silently accepts. A safety regression, since containment is what stops the GH-177-class incidents. (2) **Bash and Python `marathon-drive` fail in *disjoint* sets** — Bash fails GH-171/GH-172 (vendored chain, exit 6), Python passes those and instead fails GH-207/GH-238/`--require-clean`-in-a-linked-worktree; neither is a superset, so "port the remaining fixes forward" is the wrong model and the **union** needs reconciling. (3) **Fixing one gap reliably unmasks the next** — GH-215 → GH-223 → now #235: `consult.sh` is still red *after* GH-223 shipped, with 7 assertions covering the whole untported provenance surface (`FIRSTHAND_COUNT`/`ECHOED_COUNT`, `t.PROMPT.txt`). Four failing files (`debug-mantra.sh`, `marathon.sh`, `relay-artifact-file.sh`, `relay-turn-trace.sh`) have no Python twin at all — they fail because they drive `marathon-drive.sh`/`relay-drive.sh`, so the blast radius exceeds `utils/py/`. **Process note, recorded because it nearly shipped bad data:** the first sweep ran against a local `development` 31 commits behind origin that predated the GH-223 fix, and its results were filed before the staleness was caught; the issue body was invalidated and re-measured at merged HEAD. A clean `git status` says nothing about whether the branch is *current*. **Side finding:** the local baseline does not reproduce [#170](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/170)'s 9 pre-existing failures or [#232](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/232)'s ~12 — only `marathon-drive.sh` and a stale `relay-pkg.tar.gz` — so both look stale or ubuntu-specific. Supersedes the cutover criterion in [GH-172-CUTOVER-RECOMMENDATION.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-172-CUTOVER-RECOMMENDATION.md), which assumed a single blocker; proposed replacement is *no Python-attributable failures against a same-commit Bash baseline*. No production code changed — test harness only. → [#255](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/255)

CHANGELOG.md:1055:- **GH-241: `MARATHON.example.yaml` now states that phases run strictly one at a time and that `depends_on` is scalar-only — docs-only; the report's first claim was partially falsified before the fix was scoped.** First bug filed *through* the new `/file-xyz-bug` skill (from `rebalance-OS`, vendored `.xyz/`), and the first to exercise the "verify the report, don't apply it" gate. **Claim (1) as filed — "nothing signals sequential execution", evidenced by a 0-match grep — does not hold:** line 3 already read "runs … **in depends_on order**; the chain **HALTS** on the first phase that fails". The grep was a false negative, searching the literal `"in order"` against the string `"in depends_on order"`. The DX complaint survives in a narrower form, which is what got fixed: the line documented *ordering* but not *exclusivity*, and "in depends_on order" is precisely how a dependency-ordered **parallel** scheduler (`make -j`) describes itself — so the new text states execution is strictly one-at-a-time and that `depends_on` **constrains** ordering rather than **creating** it, since restating "runs in order" would not move a reader who read that line and still concluded concurrency. **Claim (2) reproduced exactly** against a local two-phase fixture: `depends_on: [p1]` → `depends_on unknown phase '[p1]'`, scalar parses fine; root cause is the hand-rolled YAML reader not implementing flow sequences, so `[p1]` survives as a literal scalar into the phase-id lookup (`bin/marathon-yaml:102-105`). The field table now marks the field scalar-and-single with the exact failure text, and the header recommends `--dry-run` as the standard pre-fire step. **Consistency finding the issue didn't call out:** `depends_on` (scalar, single) and `artifact` (comma-separated, multi) are adjacent rows of the same field table carrying two different multiplicity conventions — `artifact` documented its own, `depends_on` did not, leaving the reader to infer from the neighbour. **Deliberately NOT taken: suggested fix (3)**, a `^\[.*\]$` guard in `bin/marathon-yaml` — that is a code change plus a regression test, not doc-only, and stays open as defence-in-depth (the docs fix stops the author writing the list form; the guard would catch the one who writes it anyway). Verified no runtime change: `node bin/marathon-yaml relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` emits a byte-identical phase table before and after; `relay-pkg-freshness` 3/3 (the example is not a vendored path). → [#241](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/241)

Locator verified from a foreign repo, a spaces-in-path repo, a non-git dir, and a bogus `XYZ_REPO` override; slug regex verified across all six GitHub URL forms.

The code-level default was already correct (GH-212: `--builder` defaults to `codex`), but the only existing doc caveat was cost-framed ("don't assume it's free"), never role-framed — nothing stated that Claude Code is the orchestrator/reviewer, Agy/Codex CLI are the builders, and Claude CLI is an explicit user opt-in only. Fixed both: added the explicit role statement to `AGENTS.md`'s "Repo-specific rails" and to `skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md` (this file IS in `xyz-vendor.sh`'s `VENDOR_DIRS`, so it reaches every vendored `.xyz/` install on its next re-vendor — existing already-vendored copies need a manual re-vendor to pick it up immediately). CHANGELOG.md-1099-- **New `/10days` skill, dogfooded live on its first run — 11-14-day issue sweep, 5 of 6 candidates shipped.** Built `skills/10days/` (SKILL.md + `scan-issues.sh`/`find-doc.sh` deterministic helpers) to automate: scan a GH issue age window → verify each is still valid/reproducible/not-already-fixed via subagent fan-out → build + preflight a marathon → cut a branch and execute, unattended. Statically reviewed via `/consult --models agy` before running (caught and fixed: unsafe hand-rolled JSON in `find-doc.sh`, a `swarm-preflight.sh` multi-`--gh-issue` bundling misunderstanding, missing concurrent-marathon/behind-origin checks, no worktree isolation for parallel lanes). First live run (11-14 day window, chosen to not overlap the concurrent `#208/#154/#149/#198` sweep) scanned 16 issues, excluded 7 with commit/PR evidence (already-landed: #109, #111, #144, #96; gated-on-another-issue: #153; stale/paused: #97, #156, #157) and 2 more (#149, #154) for being actively claimed by that concurrent marathon — a collision the skill's own logic didn't catch on its own; caught by cross-referencing the other marathon's branch name live. Surfaced a real design gap along the way: `marathon-plan.sh` ranks the *entire* ROADMAP ledger, not just a sweep's own candidates, so its generated waves silently included the 2 already-claimed issues — fixed `SKILL.md` to require filtering to the sweep's own candidate set before firing anything. 6 issues survived triage; **5 shipped**: [#110](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/110) P2b (`test/roadmap-dashboard.sh` skip-guard + new top-level `run-tests.sh` entry point, `49c7b8d`), [#147](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/147) P2 (LM Studio lane threaded through the production Aider relay turn shim, byte-identical default OpenRouter path, 55/55 tests, `160c0fe`), [#151](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/151) P4 (cost-observability coverage-truth spike: Codex usage surface feasible, agy confirmed structurally cost-blind, Gemini relay-lane recommended for retirement, `7c77e4f`), [#152](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/152) P6 (`relay-drive.sh` now auto-surfaces the `tick analyze` cost block at end-of-run behind an env toggle, wired through the existing `EXIT` trap without touching the real exit code, `89d823a`), [#155](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/155) (3 new agy hardening regression cases — S2/S5/S8 — 54/54 own tests, `5f37954`). **[#141](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/141) deliberately shipped no fix** — investigated and correctly declined: no code-only signal can distinguish a peer session's concurrent edit from the agent's own off-lane self-escape (both produce identical porcelain diffs), and `rtl_enforce`'s revert is the documented backstop for a real, already-exploited self-escape vector (GH-22) — "fixing" this without an attribution signal would silently disable that protection. Recorded two non-detection follow-ups (recoverable backup-before-revert; document the don't-hand-edit-a-live-clone constraint) for an operator decision instead. Consolidated Wave 1 gate surfaced two real (non-flaky) cross-lane issues only visible once all 5 lanes merged together: a new unbaselined `credential-literal` finding from `#147`'s test fixture (`test/aider-turn.sh:322`, a dummy key — baselined, same class as the existing `test/deep-research.sh` entry) and a stale `relay-pkg.tar.gz` (two lanes each regenerated it for their own change via `make-pkg.sh`, but neither reflected the other's — refreshed once against the fully-merged tree). `worktree-isolation.sh` and `acorn-extract.sh` also failed in the gate; independently verified both fail identically against the pre-merge base commit in a scratch worktree (pre-existing GH-208 flaky race; missing `acorn` npm module) before ruling them out as unrelated. Live incident along the way: worktree directories (including the sweep's own and multiple lane worktrees) were deleted out from under running agents mid-`validate.sh` by an external, unrelated process — no committed work was lost (all recoverable from the branch), but it forced a switch to faster, targeted per-lane gates instead of the full suite to reduce the exposure window.

CHANGELOG.md-1103-- **[GH-198](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/198) Bug 1 — `rtl_enforce`'s "file-scoped" commit had no pathspec, so pre-existing staged content silently rode along into the relay's commit.** `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh`'s commit step staged each allowlisted path independently (`git add -A -- <path>`, tolerant of a non-matching entry) but then committed with a bare `git commit` — no trailing pathspec — which commits the ENTIRE staged index, not just what the turn just staged. Reproduced live twice (2026-07-10/11) driving `relay-drive.sh --target-root` against a repo with pre-existing staged WIP: it rode into the relay's auto-commit under a message that only named the relay file. Fixed by scoping the commit to the allowlist — but a naive `git commit -- "${RTL_ALLOW[@]}"` reintroduces the GH-29 class of bug (unlike `git add -A --`, `git commit --` is NOT per-path independent: one pathspec entry that matches nothing aborts the WHOLE commit), caught by `test/relay-target-root-newfile.sh` regressing during my own fix. Corrected: cross-check each allowlist entry against what's actually staged (`git diff --cached --name-only`) before including it in the commit pathspec, and treat an empty result (only pre-existing unrelated content was staged, the turn changed nothing) as the existing "no tracked changes" no-op rather than either an aborted commit or a commit-everything fallback. Kernel-path change (`relay-turn-lib.sh` is orchestrator-only per this repo's own zone model) — implemented directly, not via a headless marathon builder turn. New `test/relay-commit-pathspec.sh` (9/9): proves pre-existing staged content is excluded and remains staged/untouched, plus a control case confirming a real allowlisted artifact still commits normally. Full regression sweep across every test touching `rtl_enforce` (`archive-commit.sh`, `relay-self-sufficiency.sh`, `relay-concurrent-commit.sh`, `relay-turn-trace.sh`, `relay-dep-drift.sh`, `shim-worktree.sh`, `relay-turn-handoff.sh`, `relay-target-root-newfile.sh`) green. Rebuilt `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz`. Full `validate.sh` green except the pre-existing, tracked [#208](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/208) environment red. GH-198's Bug 2 (doc/UX gap around reviewing an uncommitted same-repo artifact) remains open.

CHANGELOG.md-1105-- **[GH-212](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/212) — marathon builder-default (no billed CLI) and plan-location (`PROJECT/2-WORKING`) are now explicit, enforced defaults in the vendored harness.** Two previously-implicit conventions, made first-class: (1) `marathon.sh`/`marathon-drive.sh` (and the `XYZ_PYTHON=1` port, `utils/py/marathon_drive.py`) now default `--builder` to `codex` instead of `claude` — `codex`/`agy` bill via subscription, not a per-call Anthropic API charge like the headless `claude` CLI subprocess; `--builder claude` remains fully supported as a documented, cost-acknowledged opt-in (`--help`/usage text on both scripts, plus `MARATHON.example.yaml`'s header). This also reconciles `marathon.sh`'s default with what `swarm-preflight.sh` already suggested (`--builder codex`). (2) `marathon.sh --plan PATH` now refuses (exit 2) a plan that resolves outside `PROJECT/2-WORKING/` in the target repo — exempt: paths under the harness's own home (`MARATHON_HOME`, e.g. shipped examples) or an explicit `MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING=1` override — so an agent authoring a new marathon from only the vendored bundle can't drift into a standalone top-level folder (a real, tracked instance of exactly this drift already exists in this repo at `marathon-plans/2026-07-15-gh205-207/`, left as historical/out of scope here). Both conventions documented in `GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md` → Conventions. Operator chose the simple builder-default swap over a more invasive `--builder self`/orchestrator-hands-back-the-turn design (recorded in the capture doc as a non-goal, revisitable later). Fixed two macOS `/var`→`/private/var` symlink canonicization gaps in the new plan-location guard (surfaced by `test/marathon.sh`'s vendored-install case) by resolving both the plan path and `ROOT`/`MARATHON_HOME` with `pwd -P` before comparing, mirroring `swarm-preflight.sh`'s existing pattern. Updated `test/marathon.sh` (fixtures moved under `PROJECT/2-WORKING/`, 3 new guard cases: refuse-by-default, override, harness-home-exempt), `test/marathon-drive.sh` (pinned `--builder claude` in its shared `run_driver` helper so existing claude-identity assertions keep testing what they always tested, plus a new dedicated case proving the unset default is now `codex`), and `test/xyz-harness-hooks.sh` (moved its two real-marathon.sh fixtures under `PROJECT/2-WORKING/`, changed a `reviewer: codex` phase to `reviewer: agy` to avoid a builder==reviewer collision now that the default builder is `codex`, added a `CODEX_BIN` stub alongside the existing `CLAUDE_BIN`/`AGY_BIN` ones). CHANGELOG.md:1111:- **ATE (Automated Testing Environment) skill built and hardened, `utils/ate/`**: renamed from `gemma-aider-variation-tester` (frontmatter `name: ate`, install destination, all doc paths). A local Gemma worker (via LM Studio) fuzzes Aider CLI-flag combinations against an OpenRouter/GLM-5.2 target for hours unattended while a frontier model supervises via `checkin.py`; the full cycle — run Aider, capture the error, document it, file it — is now chained end to end, verified with real subprocess execution (a stub failing `aider` + a stub `gh`), not just read: `run_variations.py` auto-invokes `compile_issue.py` when it stops (time limit/abort/safety cap), which files **one** GitHub issue titled `ATE - [test-name] yyyy-mm-dd` containing every finding from that run as a single severity-ranked checklist — no manual second step. A `/consult` with Codex + agy (agy's transcript flagged `FAIL` by the isolation-grounding guard for citing real-repo paths, but its findings still cross-checked cleanly) surfaced and fixed ~10 unattended-run robustness bugs beyond the three found solo: crash-on-malformed-LM-Studio-response, `compile_issue.py` `IndexError` on empty stderr, `AttributeError` on a JSON-`null` classification, stale `control.json` abort persisting into a fresh run, non-process-tree-safe subprocess timeouts (orphaned `aider` children), `UnicodeDecodeError` on non-UTF8 subprocess output, an `install.sh` self-deletion risk, and a `dict | None` (PEP 604) annotation that crashed every script outright on this machine's Python 3.9 — found only by actually executing the scripts, not `py_compile`. Confirmed via direct code trace + `grep` that the implementation is hardcoded to Aider specifically (binary name, `--edit-format`/`--map-tokens`/`--no-auto-commits` flags, the variation-grid schema, the classifier prompt's pipeline framing) despite the skill's generic description; generalizing it to other harnesses is deliberately deferred, not urgent — captured as [#191](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/191), parked in `ROADMAP.md`'s queue, and given a `ROUTER.md` routing hint.

CHANGELOG.md-1117-- **PR #184 code-review follow-up (B3/A4 rigor)**: a review of PR #184 flagged that B3's mechanical backstop only recognized a 3-word trigger list (`[Pass]`/verified/confirmed), and that A4's citeless check asked "is there a citation ANYWHERE in the whole transcript" rather than "is THIS claim cited" — letting one incidental citation excuse every later uncited claim. Fixed both: `relay-turn-lib.sh` gained `RTL_CLAIM_WORD_RE` (widened vocabulary — LGTM/looks good/checks out/all good/works as expected/no issues, alongside verified/confirmed) and a new read-only predicate `rtl_has_uncited_claim()`, shared by B3's per-line downgrade and a rewritten `consult.sh` A4 check that now flags a transcript with any uncited claim near itself, not just a transcript with zero citations anywhere. **Caught mid-fix, by the same review pass**: passing `\[Pass\]` through `awk -v` (rather than an inline `/regex/` literal) silently corrupts it under macOS's default `/usr/bin/awk` — the -v value's backslash gets stripped before the string is compiled as a regex, turning the literal tag into the bracket expression `[Pass]` ("any single P, a, or s character"), matching almost every line. Fixed by keeping the `[Pass]` tag check as an inline literal in both awk scripts and only passing the backslash-free prose-word list through `-v`; pinned with a dedicated regression test (a P/a/s-heavy non-claim line asserted byte-for-byte untouched) in both `test/relay-uncited-findings.sh` and via `rtl_has_uncited_claim`. New/extended tests: `test/relay-uncited-findings.sh` (+6 assertions, 16 total), `test/consult.sh` (+2 assertions, updated the A4 non-regression fixture to cite each claim individually rather than once anywhere). Full `./validate.sh` run (item 4 of the follow-up): also rebuilt `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` via `make-pkg.sh` — it had already drifted from `new-relay.sh`/`agy-turn.sh`/`README.md`/`relay-turn-lib.sh` since the original PR #184 landed without a rebuild, failing `relay-pkg-freshness.sh`; now green. The only remaining `./validate.sh` reds are two confirmed pre-existing environment gaps unrelated to this change — `acorn-extract.sh` (missing the `acorn` npm module) and `python:test_python_layer.py` (missing `pytest`) — both reproduced identically on the PR's original head commit via `git stash`.

CHANGELOG.md-1194-### GH-165 Codex shim now owns the relay token before launch
CHANGELOG.md-1195-Captured [GH-165](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-165-CODEX-TOKEN-OWNERSHIP.md) on the repo's PDDA rails and fixed the narrowed root cause in both implementations: Bash [relay-automation/codex-turn.sh](relay-automation/codex-turn.sh) and Python [utils/py/codex-turn.py](utils/py/codex-turn.py) no longer rely entirely on prompt-following for the **claim** half of the relay protocol. Before launching Codex they now build the exact `claim --paths` set, best-effort claim the handed-off task, prove `claimer == codex`, and ping the token; if ownership is missing they fail fast with exit 5 before any mutation, rather than allowing a commit with the token still open under the old owner. This complements GH-67's post-commit `release/done` backstop: GH-67 handled "Codex forgot to release", while GH-165 closes "Codex never owned the token in the first place." Added two regressions in [test/codex-turn.sh](test/codex-turn.sh): a **no-tick** Codex stub that edits the relay file but runs zero token commands (the shim must still hand off to the peer), and an **unowned-token refusal** case that proves no edit/commit happens when another agent still owns the task. Verification: `bash test/codex-turn.sh` **37/0** green, `XYZ_PYTHON=1 bash test/codex-turn.sh` **37/0** green, `python3 -m py_compile utils/py/codex-turn.py` green, and `bash test/relay-pkg-freshness.sh` green after rebuilding `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz`.
