CHANGELOG.md-1251-### GH-96 Seam #1 shipped + GH-140 containment-kernel fix (dogfood found a real repo-wiping bug)
CHANGELOG.md-1252-Shipped Seam #1 of the XYZ⇄Rebalance integration (`XYZ.json` schema/cadence doc + a `XYZ.heartbeat.json` companion so a hung/dead run goes stale instead of presenting the last completed record as current) — but getting there surfaced a serious containment-kernel bug. The first marathon attempt (codex build → agy Approved, 2 turns, clean relay lifecycle) crashed `marathon-drive.sh` itself immediately after approval with a garbled `syntax error`, then wiped this repo's local working tree and `.git` internals down to a handful of surviving dot-directories (`origin/main` was completely unaffected — confirmed via `git ls-remote`, recovered by re-cloning). Root cause, found by reading `rtl_worktree_end()`: it copies a turn's allowlisted artifacts back from the isolated worktree via a **non-atomic in-place `cp -R`**, which truncates-and-rewrites an existing destination at the same inode; since this lane's own artifacts included the *actively-executing* `marathon-drive.sh` and its `relay-drive.sh` subprocess, the live bash interpreter — which reads a script incrementally, not fully buffered upfront — read a half-old/half-new file mid-parse. Filed and fixed as its own kernel patch, **[#140](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/140)** (`f64a051`): copy to a temp path beside the destination, then atomically rename into place — the same `os.replace()` pattern `append-xyz-completion.sh` already uses, so an fd already open on the old file keeps reading the old inode until it closes, never observing a half-written script. Regression: `test/worktree-isolation.sh` 31/31, `test/shim-worktree.sh` 32/32, `test/agy-turn.sh` 27/27, full `validate.sh` green. Re-fired the identical GH-96 lane on a temp branch (`marathon/gh-96-xyz-json-emit-contract-heartbeat-2026-07-06`) with close, active monitoring this time — completed cleanly end-to-end (gate `test/xyz-completion.sh` 44/0, agy Approved after 1 round), confirming the fix; verified independently (gate re-run 44/0, full `validate.sh` green — the one flake was `test/relay-self-sufficiency.sh`, a live-agy-API test that reproduced clean 4/4 in isolation, pre-existing and unrelated), fast-forward merged to `main` (`f1e5223`), pushed. Marked [GH-96-XYZ-JSON-EMIT-CONTRACT-HEARTBEAT.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-96-XYZ-JSON-EMIT-CONTRACT-HEARTBEAT.md) shipped and moved to `3-COMPLETED`; issue #96 stays open for Seam #3 (tick-lane consume), still explicitly gated behind Seam #1 proving out per its own text.

CHANGELOG.md-1370-### deep-research.mjs (GH-87) had shipped un-run against real `agy` — 2 hangs fixed + grounded #111 research
CHANGELOG.md-1371-Dogfooding the merged grounded-search adapter to research #111 (Python cutover lessons) revealed it **hung on every real `agy` call** — it had been merged with stub-only tests, so it was never actually run against the real backend. Two independent bugs, both fixed + regression-tested:
CHANGELOG.md:1372:- **Missing `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** (`91f17f2`): `agy -p` blocked on a tool-permission prompt for its web-search tool until `--print-timeout`.
CHANGELOG.md:1373:- **`execFile` silently ignores the `stdio` option** (`74cd553`): `stdio:['ignore',…]` did nothing, so `agy`'s stdin was left an open pipe it blocked reading — every wrapper call hung. Switched `runAgy` to `spawn` (which honors `stdio`). Measured: `execFile` 75s→timeout/0-bytes vs `spawn` 10s→ok; the stub missed it because it never reads stdin.
CHANGELOG.md:1374:Now returns in ~27–52s with real citations; `test/deep-research.sh` **23/23** (added a `--dangerously-skip-permissions` assertion + a stdin-reading `needstdin` stub that hangs unless stdin is EOF'd). **Lesson: a stub can't prove a CLI adapter works against its real backend** — filed **#124** for hardening (opt-in real-`agy` smoke test + a runaway-grounding guard: `--search-context-size high` over-searches and can approach the timeout). First real use: ran 4 grounded searches (reframed for the XYZ→Python port, drawing applicable lessons from #111) and posted them to **#111**.

CHANGELOG.md:1423:`relay-automation/deep-research.mjs` is a zero-dep Node adapter wrapping the `agy` CLI as the first grounded-search backend (Agy Gemini Search), normalizing output to `{answer, citations, query, provider, model, raw}` so a second backend (Perplexity) can be added later without reworking the contract. Runs `agy -p` in a throwaway tmpdir (side-effect free) under a hard timeout; fail-closed typed errors (`binary_missing`/`timeout`/`empty_output`/`backend_error`) on stderr, never a silent fallback to the default model provider. `test/deep-research.sh` (21 assertions) covers request construction, CITATIONS-heading normalization, bare-URL fallback extraction, side-effect-free isolation, and all four failure modes. Reviewed via an automated agy relay (Approved, 0 Blockers/Shoulds) + an operator code review (Opus 4.8). Known Phase-1 limitation: `--temperature`/`--max-tokens` are recorded in `raw.config` for the future Perplexity backend but not yet passed to the `agy` invocation. Merged into main by resolving a ledger-file conflict against the same-day GH-30 commits; `validate.sh` green post-merge. Doc promoted `PROJECT/1-INBOX` → `PROJECT/2-WORKING`.

CHANGELOG.md-1427-### GH-30 Phases 3–5 SHIPPED (Plan A lane 5, complete) — Model A off-tree transcript commit
CHANGELOG.md-1428-Phase 2 redirected the transcript *writers*; the containment kernel still committed the relay file into the target repo. Phase 3 closes that: when `XYZ_ARCHIVE_ROOT` places the relay file in a **separate archive git repo**, the kernel commits the **transcript into the archive** while the **code artifact + the `.tick` token stay anchored to the target**. Built and reviewed operator-direct under Opus 4.8 (kernel lane — not headless).
CHANGELOG.md-1429-- **The bet (Costly, reversible — containment-kernel touch):** `rtl_enforce` now performs a second, **isolated** `git -C "$RTL_RELAY_REPO"` pathspec commit for the transcript. Because that commit can never move the target repo's HEAD, it **cannot orphan a concurrent peer commit** in the target tree — the documented `rtl_enforce` reset hazard (GH-13) is guarded on `RTL_ROOT` only, and now holds even when token-tree ≠ transcript-tree. The archive commit is best-effort: a failure **warns** (the transcript file is still written) and never fails the turn, since the file-scoped code commit already stood. Reversibility: unset the var → byte-for-byte the prior single-repo behavior; the archive is a plain committed git repo the operator owns. Revisit trigger: if a turn ever needs the transcript and token in the *same* off-tree repo (not this split), or if worktree isolation must seed the archive relay file (today the agent edits it at its real absolute path, outside the target worktree).
CHANGELOG.md-1430-- **`rtl_init` archive detection (one place):** when the relay file's git toplevel differs from `RTL_ROOT`'s, it flags `RTL_ARCHIVE_MODE` + records `RTL_RELAY_REPO`/`RTL_RELAY_ARCHIVE_REL`. An out-of-root relay file survives the repo-root-relative strip as an **absolute** path, so it is already inert to the `RTL_ROOT` status/commit loop; the worktree seed/copyback now **skip absolute allowlist entries** in lockstep (seed + seedsig + copyback) so the seedsig index stays aligned. Same-repo relay file / unset var → `RTL_ARCHIVE_MODE=0`, byte-for-byte every existing path.
CHANGELOG.md-1431-- **`.tick` stays on the target:** the token handoff (GH-67) already uses `TICK_REPO_ROOT`; archive mode never touches it. So the coordination token lives with the target repo and the transcript lives in the archive — the two trees differ safely.

CHANGELOG.md-1456-### GH-5 SHIPPED (Plan A lane 4, PR #103) — contract-seam warning for coupled lanes
CHANGELOG.md-1457-The one thing that made two lanes *actually* independent in the real run was a coordinator-pinned shared contract (both coded TO the contract, not to each other's source) — but nothing detected coupling, so operators found it only when an agent stalled waiting on another lane. `marathon-plan.sh`'s wave-packer defers only on an **exact** write-set collision, so two lanes writing disjoint files under a common directory (e.g. `src/schema/producer.js` ‖ `src/schema/consumer.js`) co-wave and *look* independent while the consumer stalls on the producer.
CHANGELOG.md-1458-- **`sharedSpine`** detects the seam: the deepest directory of ≥2 segments shared by two same-wave lanes' write-sets (top-level-only sharing — both under `src/` — is intentionally not a seam). Every coupled pair becomes a `warn`/`coupled-lanes` finding.
CHANGELOG.md-1459-- New **"## Contract seams — pin a contract before launching (GH-5)"** plan section names each pair + the shared dir + the fix (pin a short `CONTRACT.md`, point each lane prompt at it) — making the "pin the contract" step first-class (fix 1) alongside the coupled-lane warning (fix 2). Deferred-coupled-work (fix 3) is the existing Held/flagged section. **Advisory** — never re-waves the lanes (they parallelize fine once a contract is pinned); exit code unchanged.
CHANGELOG.md-1460-- Only lanes with a proven write-set (from a contract) are judged. Pairs with GH-4 work-stealing: a stolen task that's actually coupled would stall — this surfaces the seam first. `test/marathon-plan.sh` scenario K (+3: `src/schema` pair flagged; a `utils/` lane not flagged; pin-a-contract stated); `marathon-plan` 39/39. Deferred: auto-scaffolding the CONTRACT.md + source-level import-graph inference.

CHANGELOG.md-1462-### GH-4 SHIPPED (Plan A lane 3, PR #101) — lane-count-independent verdict + work-stealing unblocked
CHANGELOG.md:1463:The run success bar was `concurrency% AND each agent ≥2 done` — but a clean 2-lane/2-agent split gives 1 done each *by construction*, so a flawless run failed the bar, and the manual `handoff-exclusive` rule *blocked* a fast agent from crossing lanes precisely to protect that (broken) per-agent bar — leaving idle tail-time on the table. Fixed all three ways (events-only):
CHANGELOG.md-1464-- **(1) `tick analyze` emits a VERDICT** (`pass`/`fail`/`incomplete`) gating on concurrency% + zero-parked + **all-lanes-done** + **zero-collisions**, and explicitly **not** on per-agent done count (`computeVerdict`; target `TICK_CONCURRENCY_TARGET_PCT`, finite-tunable, default 50). A `circuit_broken` or still-open lane counts as not-done → FAIL.
CHANGELOG.md-1465-- **(2) Work-stealing** needed no new mechanism: `src/take.js` already selects the highest-priority `open` task whose paths don't overlap *any* active claim, so a free agent that `take`s after finishing pulls a collision-free item from another lane. Removing the per-agent bar makes the resulting imbalance a *win* — the verdict now PASSES a 2-vs-1 done split.
CHANGELOG.md:1466:- **(3) Lane balance** — a per-agent idle-tail line surfaces imbalance; `computeCollisions` reports overlapping concurrent claims (should be 0 — verifies the claim-lock containment invariant held).
CHANGELOG.md-1467-- `test/workstealing-verdict.sh` (6, end-to-end: beta steals C1 from a free lane → board drains all-done → **VERDICT PASS on a 2-vs-1 split**, the exact case the old bar failed) + `test/analyze.sh` (+2: 0 collisions, FAIL on an undone/broken lane). Additive JSON fields → `watchdog.sh`/`poll.sh` unaffected. `validate.sh` **87/87**. Deferred: runner auto-`take`-loop + wiring the verdict into a marathon exit gate.
CHANGELOG.md-1468-
CHANGELOG.md-1469-### GH-3 SHIPPED (Plan A lane 2, PR #100) — parked-claim detector no longer false-flags active autonomous agents
CHANGELOG.md-1470-`tick analyze`'s parked-claim detector (`src/analyze.js`) disqualified a fully-active 90%-concurrency run: its liveness signal was **`task.heartbeat`-only** and the fixed 10-min threshold is human-paced, but an autonomous subagent in a single long atomic tool call has **no yield point** to emit a `tick ping`, so it looked parked. Fixed events-only (keeps the detector's "no git" invariant):
CHANGELOG.md-1471-- **(2) Liveness = any `task.*` event from the agent** for that task inside the window — `scope_changed`, `commented`, a re-claim, `done` — not just `task.heartbeat`. The truest events-only proxy for "work happening."
CHANGELOG.md-1472-- **(1) `TICK_PARKED_THRESHOLD_MS`** env override (default unchanged, 10 min; **finite** positive only — a stray `Infinity` can't disable the gate, per the PR #100 cross-model review) so an autonomous-agent marathon can raise it without a code change.
CHANGELOG.md-1473-- `parked_suspects` shape/semantics **unchanged** (still "an activity gap over threshold") → safe for the live `watchdog.sh` reap + `poll.sh` count; a new `activity` count is reported alongside `heartbeats`. `test/heartbeat.sh` +4 checks (a `scope_changed` keeps a window live; the env override raises, suppresses, and rejects non-finite); `chaos-midturn-kill` (orphaned claim still parked) + `watchdog-liveness` green. `validate.sh` 85/85. Reviewed cross-model (Codex + agy → merge).

CHANGELOG.md-1674-### GH-72 CLOSED — registry lock hardened through a 4-round codex relay (5 real defects)
CHANGELOG.md-1675-The dogfood-built lock (Lane B) was **not** actually correct. A `/consult` found 1 defect; a headless codex relay review then found **4 more** over 4 rounds — a clean demonstration that *running/reviewing* beats *reasoning*, and that a concurrency stress test + an independent reviewer catch what a one-shot read misses. All fixed + verified (`validate.sh` 75/75, codex final **Approved**):
CHANGELOG.md-1676-1. **empty-pid TOCTOU** — loser deleted the winner's fresh lock before its pid was written. → empty pid now means "wait", not "reclaim".
CHANGELOG.md-1677-2. **retry/fail-open-under-contention** — `sleep 1` + give-up-after-5 made losers write *unlocked* under load (16→7 rows). → fast 0.1s retry + wall-clock deadline (`XYZ_LOCK_WAIT_S`).
CHANGELOG.md-1678-3. **unlocked bootstrap truncation** — header written with an unlocked `> "$reg"`. → header now created inside the locked atomic rewrite.
CHANGELOG.md:1679:4. **fail-open wrote unlocked** — timeout still ran the RMW unlocked. → best-effort side-effect now **skips** on timeout, never writes unlocked.
CHANGELOG.md-1680-5. **projection inside the registry lock** — slow git-pulse work starved registry writers. → projection published *after* the registry lock releases.
CHANGELOG.md-1681-Plus ownership-checked `release`/`cleanup`. New `test/registry-lock-concurrency.sh` (16 concurrent → 16/16, stable under 8 CPU burners; projection-enabled 16/16 ×3). Commits `24d5869`, `01de46c`, `46e0c3b`, `56433d6`. Minor follow-up noted on #72: `XYZ_GITPULSE_DIR=""` means auto-discover, not disabled (doc/UX nit).

CHANGELOG.md-1975-### poll.sh — `--turn-source file` (token-optional relay advance) + commit-signal gate
CHANGELOG.md:1976:Acting on the dueling-run field findings: [relay-automation/poll.sh](relay-automation/poll.sh) gains a **`--turn-source file`** mode that derives whose-turn from the relay file's **`NEXT:` field**, making the tick token **optional** — the fix for the two lock failures from the first cross-repo dueling run (a peer that never joins `tick` no longer strands the poll as `parked suspect`, and there's no `spent — not claimable` token to re-claim). Adds optional **`--peer-commit-repo`/`--peer-commit-match`** to also gate `run-runner` on the peer's fix commit landing (the hands-free "advance on commit" signal; idle = "waiting for peer commit"). `relay_field` now tolerates **`**bold**` markdown keys** (`**STATUS:**`/`**NEXT:**`, the real thread format) — a latent gap the tick-driven path never exercised. The token path is unchanged and remains the default; file-source skips the `tick analyze` read entirely (no `node`/token dependency).
CHANGELOG.md:1977:- **Verification:** 7 new assertions in [test/poll-driver.sh](test/poll-driver.sh) (bold-NEXT==me→run-runner with no token; NEXT==other-Claude→idle; NEXT==non-Claude→nudge; dirty-scope→idle; STATUS terminal→stop; commit-gate present→run-runner / missing→idle). Caught + fixed a real bug pre-merge: `git log | grep -q` tripped `set -o pipefail` via SIGPIPE → false "commit missing"; replaced with a pipe-free bash-ERE match. Repackaged the relay skill tarball (`skill-extract.sh` parity). Full `bash validate.sh` → **48/48**.
CHANGELOG.md-1978-- **Reversibility:** Easy — additive flags, default behavior (`--turn-source tick`) byte-for-byte unchanged; the bold-key tolerance is a superset of the old exact-match.
CHANGELOG.md-1979-- **Review:** **agy headless review (Path A via `relay-xyz`) → Approved.** agy graded 6×`[Pass]` (decision logic, bold-key regex + first-token extraction, the `commit_gate_ok` SIGPIPE reasoning — independently verified — backward-compat, `set -u` safety, test coverage) + 1×`[Nit]` (`head -1` → `head -n 1` for strict POSIX), which was applied across `poll.sh` + repackaged; suite still **48/48**. Thread: [relay-system/2026-06-26/poll-turn-source-review.md](relay-system/2026-06-26/poll-turn-source-review.md). Process note: the first drive over-ran the 300s turn cap because `ALLOW_PATHS` included the artifact, so agy started *editing/building* instead of reviewing — re-driven review-only with `ALLOW_PATHS=""` (relay file only) + a 600s cap closed it in one turn. CHANGELOG.md-1981-### Dueling-claudes — first real cross-repo run (KWFS bug-fix batch) + findings captured
CHANGELOG.md-1982-First **DUELING-CLAUDES** run against a foreign repo: the KISS-woo-fast-search bug-fix batch, four gate-verifiable phases (#72/#71/#68/#70). Reporter = an xyz window (files graded reports off the marathon handoff package), Maintainer = a Claude window on the plugin repo (fixes, runs the gate, stops for operator "go"); objective referee = the plugin's `bash tests/run.sh`. **Outcome: all four phases green, gate `12 passed / 1 failed`** (lone red = the #75 cache-key method, the deliberate human checkpoint — `GATE: FAIL` overall is the expected clean-run end state). Thread: [relay-system/2026-06-26/kwfs-dueling-bugfix.md](relay-system/2026-06-26/kwfs-dueling-bugfix.md).
CHANGELOG.md-1983-- **What worked:** the gate-as-referee made a same-model loop trustworthy; verify-first caught real Reporter planning errors (`get_edit_url()` was `private static`; two `post.php?post=` literals not one; #70's "delete the duplicate" was impossible under the gate).
CHANGELOG.md:1984:- **What didn't (captured as actionable):** (1) the tick token is dead weight when one peer never joins `tick` — the Maintainer worked entirely off the relay file + commits, so the token coordinated nothing and every handoff needed a manual `reap`+`claim`; (2) the single relay token went `spent — not claimable` mid-run; (3) the `#70` static-key-set gate **forced three duplicated-but-identical literals** (blocked the delegate/delete convergence the issue wanted); (4) re-running the gate under the Bash sandbox false-fails (PHP lock files) — un-sandboxed run is authoritative; (5) per-minute idle-poll churn → replaced mid-run with a **2-minute commit-watcher** that advances on the peer's fix commits.
CHANGELOG.md-1985-- **Mid-run pivot that worked:** retired the spent token and drove the back half **file-driven** — a commit-watcher keyed off the Maintainer's plugin commits auto-filed the next `REPORT` and auto-closed on the final one. Strictly better hands-free interface than the lock → now the next harness increment.

relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md-91-
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md-92-1. **[Critical] Process-Group Timeout Race Condition & Self-Kill Hazard in `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh::rtl_run_bounded`**
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md-93-   - **Location:** `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh:543-552`
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md-94-   - **Cause:** When starting `python3 -c 'import os, sys; os.setsid(); os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])' "$@" &`, the shell executes `pgid="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$apid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')"` immediately on the very next line. In a non-interactive shell without job control, the background child process inherits the calling shell's process group until `os.setsid()` executes. Because Python initialization takes ~10–30ms while `ps` executes in ~1–2ms, `ps` captures the **parent shell's PGID** (`my_pgid`).
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md:95:   - **Impact:** When the watchdog timeout expires, `kill -9 "-$pgid"` sends `SIGKILL` to the **caller's process group**, killing the calling script/test runner/shim itself (exit 137). When running `test/gh369-group-kill.sh`, the test runner was SIGKILLed at line 24 before any assertions completed, which masked the failure.
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md-96-   - **Remedy:** POSIX guarantees that when the child calls `os.setsid()`, its new PGID is equal to `$apid`. In the watchdog, kill the process group `-$apid` directly (e.g. `kill -9 "-$apid" 2>/dev/null || kill -9 "$apid" 2>/dev/null`), eliminating the startup `ps` race and preventing self-kill of the caller process group.
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-034929.md-97-   - **Verification:** Verified in an external `$TMPDIR` probe; with this fix, `test/gh369-group-kill.sh` runs all assertions to completion and reports `6 pass, 0 fail`.

relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md-91-
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md-92-1. **[Critical] Process-Group Timeout Race Condition & Self-Kill Hazard in `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh::rtl_run_bounded`**
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md-93-   - **Location:** `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh:543-552`
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md-94-   - **Cause:** When starting `python3 -c 'import os, sys; os.setsid(); os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])' "$@" &`, the shell executes `pgid="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$apid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')"` immediately on the very next line. In a non-interactive shell without job control, the background child process inherits the calling shell's process group until `os.setsid()` executes. Because Python initialization takes ~10–30ms while `ps` executes in ~1–2ms, `ps` captures the **parent shell's PGID** (`my_pgid`).
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md:95:   - **Impact:** When the watchdog timeout expires, `kill -9 "-$pgid"` sends `SIGKILL` to the **caller's process group**, killing the calling script/test runner/shim itself (exit 137). When running `test/gh369-group-kill.sh`, the test runner was SIGKILLed at line 24 before any assertions completed, which masked the failure.
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md-96-   - **Remedy:** POSIX guarantees that when the child calls `os.setsid()`, its new PGID is equal to `$apid`. In the watchdog, kill the process group `-$apid` directly (e.g. `kill -9 "-$apid" 2>/dev/null || kill -9 "$apid" 2>/dev/null`), eliminating the startup `ps` race and preventing self-kill of the caller process group.
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-033210.md-97-   - **Verification:** Verified in an external `$TMPDIR` probe; with this fix, `test/gh369-group-kill.sh` runs all assertions to completion and reports `6 pass, 0 fail`.

relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md-91-
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md-92-1. **[Critical] Process-Group Timeout Race Condition & Self-Kill Hazard in `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh::rtl_run_bounded`**
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md-93-   - **Location:** `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh:543-552`
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md-94-   - **Cause:** When starting `python3 -c 'import os, sys; os.setsid(); os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])' "$@" &`, the shell executes `pgid="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$apid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')"` immediately on the very next line. In a non-interactive shell without job control, the background child process inherits the calling shell's process group until `os.setsid()` executes. Because Python initialization takes ~10–30ms while `ps` executes in ~1–2ms, `ps` captures the **parent shell's PGID** (`my_pgid`).
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md:95:   - **Impact:** When the watchdog timeout expires, `kill -9 "-$pgid"` sends `SIGKILL` to the **caller's process group**, killing the calling script/test runner/shim itself (exit 137). When running `test/gh369-group-kill.sh`, the test runner was SIGKILLed at line 24 before any assertions completed, which masked the failure.
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md-96-   - **Remedy:** POSIX guarantees that when the child calls `os.setsid()`, its new PGID is equal to `$apid`. In the watchdog, kill the process group `-$apid` directly (e.g. `kill -9 "-$apid" 2>/dev/null || kill -9 "$apid" 2>/dev/null`), eliminating the startup `ps` race and preventing self-kill of the caller process group.
relay-system/2026-09-02/marathon-p2-turn-supervision-042119.md-97-   - **Verification:** Verified in an external `$TMPDIR` probe; with this fix, `test/gh369-group-kill.sh` runs all assertions to completion and reports `6 pass, 0 fail`.

   123	def rtl_classify_cited_claims(transcript_path, prompt_path, window=None):
   124	    """Python port of relay-turn-lib.sh's rtl_classify_cited_claims() (GH-235 A4 v0): for each
   125	    ALREADY-CITED claim line in <transcript_path>, decide whether the nearby citation string was
   126	    discovered firsthand in the transcript or merely echoed from the operator prompt text persisted
   127	    in <prompt_path>. Yields ("ECHOED", token) or ("FIRSTHAND", token) per claim, matching the awk
   128	    line-order. Missing/unreadable inputs yield nothing (mirrors the Bash early return). Known v0
   129	    limitation (shared with Bash): exact/whitespace-normalized substring matching only — no fuzzy
   130	    reformat matching."""
   131	    if window is None:
   132	        window = _citation_window()
   133	    if not (transcript_path and os.path.isfile(transcript_path) and prompt_path and os.path.isfile(prompt_path)):
   134	        return
   135	    try:
   136	        with open(prompt_path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
   137	            prompt_lines = f.read().splitlines()
   138	        with open(transcript_path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
   139	            lines = f.read().splitlines()
   140	    except OSError:
   141	        return
   142	    # awk builds prompt as each line + "\n" then norms it (newlines collapse to spaces).
   143	    prompt_norm = _rtl_norm("".join(pl + "\n" for pl in prompt_lines))
   144	    n = len(lines)
   145	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   146	        if _RTL_UNVERIFIED_RE.search(line):
   147	            continue
   148	        claim = bool(_RTL_PASS_TAG_RE.search(line)) or bool(_RTL_CLAIM_WORD_RE.search(line))
   149	        if not claim:
   150	            continue
   151	        first_token = None
   152	        echoed_token = None
   153	        window_end = min(n, i + window + 1)
   154	        for j in range(i, window_end):
   155	            for mo in _RTL_CITATION_RE.finditer(lines[j]):
   156	                token = mo.group(0)
   157	                if first_token is None:
   158	                    first_token = token
   159	                if _rtl_norm(token) in prompt_norm:
   160	                    echoed_token = token
   161	                    break
   162	            if echoed_token is not None:
   163	                break
   164	        if first_token is None:
   165	            continue
   166	        if echoed_token is not None:
   167	            yield ("ECHOED", echoed_token)
   168	        else:
   169	            yield ("FIRSTHAND", first_token)

   280	def wait_with_idle_bound(proc, out_path, remaining_s):
   281	    """Wait for one advisor, bounded by BOTH its wall remainder and an idle threshold.
   282	
   283	    Returns True if the advisor was killed for being idle, False if it exited on its own or hit
   284	    the wall remainder (the caller raises TimeoutExpired for both of those, preserving the
   285	    existing failure shape exactly).
   286	
   287	    GH-492. CONSULT_IDLE_S=0 disables the idle bound and restores pure wall-cap behaviour.
   288	
   289	    The advisor's transcript is the progress signal, not the worktree: all advisors share one
   290	    worktree, so a directory mtime cannot attribute progress to a model. Its own pid is the CPU
   291	    root for the same reason.
   292	    """
   293	    idle_cap = int(os.environ.get("CONSULT_IDLE_S", CONSULT_IDLE_DEFAULT_S))
   294	    if idle_cap <= 0:
   295	        proc.wait(timeout=remaining_s)
   296	        return False
   297	    diag = TurnDiagnostics(worktree=out_path, root_pid=proc.pid, interval=CONSULT_SAMPLE_S)
   298	    diag.start()
   299	    try:
   300	        deadline = time.monotonic() + remaining_s
   301	        while True:
   302	            if proc.poll() is not None:
   303	                return False
   304	            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
   305	                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(getattr(proc, "args", "advisor"), remaining_s)
   306	            idle = diag.idle_seconds()
   307	            # None is "not measured yet" and must never mean "kill" — see idle_seconds().
   308	            if idle is not None and idle >= idle_cap:
   309	                _reason, detail = diag.classify()
   310	                try:
   311	                    with open(out_path, "a") as f:
   312	                        f.write(f"\nconsult: advisor was IDLE for >={idle_cap}s (no CPU, no transcript "
   313	                                f"growth) and was killed before the {int(remaining_s)}s wall cap "
   314	                                f"[{_reason}: {detail}]. This is an EXTERNAL condition consult "
   315	                                f"detected and contained, not one it prevented.\n")
   316	                except OSError:
   317	                    pass
   318	                _kill_advisor_group(proc)
   319	                return True
   320	            time.sleep(CONSULT_POLL_S)
   321	    finally:
   322	        diag.stop()

   324	def _kill_advisor_group(proc):
   325	    """Kill an advisor's whole process group, then reap it.
   326	
   327	    Advisors spawn children; signalling only the launcher leaves them running and holding the
   328	    transcript open. Falls back to killing just the process when the group signal is refused —
   329	    consult launches advisors without start_new_session, so the group may be the caller's own and
   330	    must never be signalled.
   331	    """
   332	    if getattr(proc, "xyz_own_group", False):
   333	        kill_existing(proc.pid)
   334	        proc.wait()
   335	        return
   336	    try:
   337	        pgid = os.getpgid(proc.pid)
   338	        if pgid != os.getpgid(0):
   339	            os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM)
   340	        else:
   341	            proc.terminate()
   342	    except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, OSError):
   343	        try:
   344	            proc.terminate()
   345	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
   346	            return
   347	    try:
   348	        proc.wait(timeout=5)
   349	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
   350	        try:
   351	            proc.kill()
   352	            proc.wait(timeout=2)
   353	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
   354	            pass

    48	def _kill_turn_group(proc):
    49	    """Kill the turn's whole process group, not just the launcher.

    51	    agy spawns children; signalling only the parent leaves them running and holding
    52	    the log open, which is how a "killed" turn keeps burning the host. The process is
    53	    started with start_new_session=True so its pgid is its own pid and this cannot

    60	            return

    62	            proc.wait(timeout=wait_s)
    63	            return

    10	
    11	Meta ships Muse Spark 1.3 at two tiers. They are the same model; only the terms differ:
    12	
    13	    muse-spark-1.3              $1.25 / $4.25 / $0.15 per M   no data clause
    14	    muse-spark-1.3-contributor  $0.10 / $0.20 / $0.002 per M  "your content, including
    15	                                                               inter-session messages, may be
    16	                                                               used for product improvement"
    17	
    18	The operator's rule is that the discounted tier is for open-source repositories only. A relay
    19	turn ships repository content -- diffs, file bodies, review prose -- to whichever tier is
    20	dispatched, and content sent under that clause cannot be recalled. So the rule cannot be a
    21	comment that a future caller is trusted to remember; it has to be the default behavior.
    22	
    23	Hence resolve_model() FAILS CLOSED. It returns the clause-free model unless it can positively
    24	establish that EVERY repository in play -- the execution root and the coordination root, which are
    25	not required to be the same repo -- is public. Every uncertainty -- gh missing, gh unauthenticated,
    26	network down, not a GitHub remote, lookup timed out, unparseable answer -- lands on the safe tier.
    27	The expensive model is the safe one here, which is exactly why the failure direction has to be
    28	chosen deliberately: the cheap path is the one that leaks.
    29	
    30	`MUSE_MODEL` overrides everything, because an operator naming a model explicitly is making an
    31	informed choice; `MUSE_ALLOW_CONTRIBUTOR=0` pins the safe tier even for public repos.

    57	def repo_visibility(repo_root):
    58	    """Return (visibility, reason). visibility is 'PUBLIC', 'PRIVATE', or '' when undetermined.
    59	
    60	    '' is not an error state the caller should retry -- it is the answer "we do not know", which
    61	    resolve_model treats exactly like PRIVATE.
    62	    """
    63	    try:
    64	        proc = subprocess.run(
    65	            ["gh", "repo", "view", "--json", "visibility", "-q", ".visibility"],
    66	            cwd=repo_root,
    67	            capture_output=True,
    68	            text=True,
    69	            timeout=VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_S,
    70	            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    71	        )
    72	    except FileNotFoundError:
    73	        return "", "gh CLI not installed"
    74	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    75	        return "", f"gh repo view exceeded {VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_S}s"
    76	    except Exception as exc:
    77	        return "", f"gh repo view raised {exc!r}"
    78	
    79	    if proc.returncode != 0:
    80	        detail = (proc.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()
    81	        return "", "gh repo view exit %d%s" % (
    82	            proc.returncode, (": " + detail[0]) if detail else "")
    83	
    84	    answer = (proc.stdout or "").strip().upper()
    85	    if answer in ("PUBLIC", "PRIVATE", "INTERNAL"):
    86	        # INTERNAL is org-visible, not open source. Deliberately not treated as public.
    87	        return answer, "gh reported %s" % answer
    88	    return "", "gh returned unrecognized visibility %r" % (answer,)

    91	def resolve_model(*repo_roots):
    92	    """Pick the model for this turn. Returns (model_id, reason) -- the reason is logged, always.
    93	
    94	    EVERY repository in play must be independently confirmed public before the discounted tier is
    95	    used. One private or unknown root anywhere vetoes it.
    96	
    97	    This is deliberately stricter than "classify the repo we write to", and the reason is a wiring
    98	    trap found in review. `claim_task_or_exit()` returns `resolve_tick_repo_root(root)`, which
    99	    honors TICK_REPO_ROOT whenever that path merely EXISTS -- it never requires it to equal the
   100	    turn root. Meanwhile the CLI is launched with cwd=root (or a worktree derived from root). So a
   101	    private MUSE_TURN_ROOT paired with a public TICK_REPO_ROOT would classify the public
   102	    coordination repo and then execute against the private checkout: the discounted tier selected
   103	    by a repo whose content is not the content being sent.
   104	
   105	    Classifying only the execution root would fix that specific inversion, but leaves the mirror
   106	    case -- a public execution root beside a private coordination root -- resting on the claim that
   107	    no private content crosses over. Requiring unanimity removes the need to make that claim at all.
   108	    """
   109	    explicit = os.environ.get("MUSE_MODEL", "").strip()
   110	    if explicit:
   111	        # Accept colloquial names, so MUSE_MODEL=muse and MUSE_MODEL="Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor"
   112	        # both work. This goes through the catalog's NATIVE aliases, not resolve-model-alias.sh,
   113	        # which is OpenRouter-scoped and structurally cannot see a native model -- see
   114	        # model_alias.resolve_native_alias. A miss returns the literal unchanged, so an exact id
   115	        # or an unknown string is passed to the CLI as typed and rejected there rather than here.
   116	        try:
   117	            from model_alias import resolve_native_alias
   118	            resolved = resolve_native_alias(explicit, os.environ.get("XYZ_ROOT", ""))
   119	        except Exception:
   120	            resolved = explicit
   121	        if resolved != explicit:

   123	        return explicit, "explicit MUSE_MODEL"
   124	
   125	    if os.environ.get("MUSE_ALLOW_CONTRIBUTOR", "1") == "0":
   126	        return SAFE_MODEL, "contributor tier disabled by MUSE_ALLOW_CONTRIBUTOR=0"
   127	
   128	    # Deduplicate by real path: the common case is one repo passed twice, and that should cost one
   129	    # network round trip, not two.
   130	    seen = []
   131	    for candidate in repo_roots:
   132	        if not candidate:
   133	            continue
   134	        try:
   135	            real = os.path.realpath(candidate)

   137	            real = candidate
   138	        if real not in seen:

   149	    if len(seen) == 1:
   150	        return CONTRIBUTOR_MODEL, "repository is public"
   151	    return CONTRIBUTOR_MODEL, "all %d repository roots in play are public" % len(seen)

Four of the six issues are CLOSED with per-criterion evidence (#407, #417, #457, #461). **Residual scope, resolved at ship (2026-08-14).** Both entries'' gates are registered, green and control-observed — which is what this release''s exit criterion measures — but each carried acceptance criteria that did not ship, and an unshipped criterion is not a reason to hold a met goalpost open. **#375 is CLOSED** (this block previously said it remained open; that was stale). **#390''s residual is now [#546](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/546), milestoned Meter** — Layer 4''s host free-memory floor and packet-driven per-phase overrides, deferred by the source itself at `utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1509` (verbatim: `# Layer 4 (host free-memory floor) and packet-driven per-phase overrides are Phase 2.`). Meter is the right home rather than a parking space: a host floor is a precondition checked before spending, #382 is already a Meter member and its capture doc documents this exact deferral, and #392 is the static counterpart to this runtime one. #546 is **milestone backlog, NOT admitted to Meter''s frozen manifest** — it does not make Meter''s exit command fail, so "discovery is not admission" applies. #375''s shipped three-state `unverifiable` verdict still deliberately contradicts its criteria 1 and 5, because implementing them literally took `relay-self-sufficiency.sh` from 4/0 to 0/4 on a working machine; that is recorded on the issue and is a deliberate deviation, not an omission.', '2026-09-08T05:45:05Z');
releases.sql-345-INSERT INTO legacy_lines(release_gid, position, content, updated_at) VALUES('rel-01M0BTBRMJW4B6HWAHKW82GFGS', '107', 'Manifest: FROZEN 2026-08-08 — #375, #390, #407, #417, #457, #461. Six named decision gates, a fixed denominator rather than a percentage. "Every gate" was unshippable prose: `gate_inventory.py` reports 152 of 158 gates with no declared control, and retrofitting them is explicitly out of scope. Adding an entry is a RE-SCOPE, not a bugfix: a mid-release discovery joins only if it makes the exit command fail or falsifies a named invariant, has a reproducer demonstrating that, and the operator explicitly swaps out an existing entry or accepts a date slip. Discovery is not admission — #457, #460 and #461 were all filed while executing Litmus, which is what an unfrozen boundary looks like.', '2026-09-08T05:45:05Z');

CHANGELOG.md-860-- **GH-417: the tree asserted both that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` is the right ROOT default and that it is the bug "caught live" — the answer is a commit nobody had connected, and Marathon Plan K was two days early.** `utils/py/rtl.py:resolve_turn_root` defaults ROOT to `--show-toplevel` (GH-296); `relay-turn-lib.sh`'s GH-160 collapse carried a comment calling that construct the bug. Nothing reconciled them and no test could tell them apart, so the failure mode — exit 6, a legitimate in-allowlist edit reverted as a containment violation — could not be attributed to anything. **What actually resolved it: `312a2c3` (2026-07-21, GH-261), whose own commit message names `test/marathon-drive.sh`'s GH-171/GH-172 cases** — the exact failures Plan K measured on **2026-07-19** and explained by blaming `--show-toplevel`. GH-261 canonicalizes **both** `RTL_ROOT` and each absolute allowlist entry to physical form before stripping, so from that commit on either symlink form resolves. Both statements were true of different things: the GH-160 collapse runs *before* that normalization and must not change `RTL_ROOT`'s form, while `resolve_turn_root` runs after it. Both files now say so and point at each other; **the "caught live" sentence was kept, not deleted** — it is a real constraint on the GH-160 collapse, and only its scope was ever ambiguous. New `test/gh417-turn-root-symlink-prefix.sh`, **13/0**: a Python turn shim with `AGY_TURN_ROOT` **unset**, driven from a repo reached through a symlinked prefix, is not reverted. **The control is what makes it evidence** — reverting GH-261's canonicalization in a fixture copy brings exit 6 straight back with the original symptom in words (`OFF-ALLOWLIST change: relay.md — reverting`), and the *same reverted tree* passes when ROOT is pinned to the logical form, which is what identifies ROOT's symlink form as the axis rather than the fixture. Two traps sidestepped: the fixture builds its **own** `link -> phys` symlink instead of trusting `$TMPDIR` (macOS gives `/var -> /private/var` free, Linux CI does not, and a sandbox can hand back an already-physical `$TMPDIR` — the shape would vanish and every assertion would pass for the wrong reason, so the test asserts the shape first), and the **Python lane is proven** by a `python3` wrapper on `PATH` that records it ran, never certifying the frozen Bash twins as a proxy. **Comments only** in both files; the five GH-308-frozen Bash shims untouched. `marathon-drive` 144/0, `agy-turn` 62/0, `worktree-isolation` 33/0, `relay-target-root` 12/0. → [#417](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/417)
CHANGELOG.md-861-- **`swarm-preflight` crashed outright on any binary file under `test/` — found by agy mid-marathon, in code it was not asked to review.** `expand_effective_artifacts`'s inner `read()` helper (`utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:366`) did `open(..., "r")` with `except OSError:` only, while walking the entire `test/` tree to infer tests. One binary fixture there raised an uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError` and killed preflight before it could render any verdict — reproduced with a single probe file: `'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 3`, at `:1049 main → expand_effective_artifacts → :385 → :369`. **The tell was an asymmetry inside the same file:** codex's own new `find_frozen_artifacts` (`:631`), written two hundred lines away in the same turn, already used `encoding="utf-8"` + `except (OSError, UnicodeError)`; the pre-existing helper beside it did not. Now hardened and pinned by a binary fixture asserting both exit 0 **and** the absence of `UnicodeDecodeError` in the output — an exit-code assertion alone would pass if the error were merely swallowed. Weight: preflight is the tool that decides marathon-readiness, `/10days` Step 6 treats any non-zero exit as "drop this issue", and #343/#418/#425 are all about it returning *wrong* verdicts — a hard crash on a routine repo state outranks a wrong verdict. Folded into the gh418 lane by operator decision rather than deferred, because it is one line in a file already in that lane's write-set.
CHANGELOG.md-862-- **A reviewer had no sanctioned place to write, so proving a finding destroyed the turn that found it.** agy discovered the crash above and wrote `dummy.py` + `test/binary/` in-tree to demonstrate it — the same probe used to confirm it. Both are off-allowlist, so containment reverted them and failed the turn with exit 6 (correct per GH-410 case 3: a genuine off-lane *write* must still fail). The verdict survived only because `RELAY.md` happens to be on the reviewer's allowlist; written anywhere else it would have been lost, and the crash with it. **Containment is unchanged and not weakened** — instead the rendered reviewer prompt now carries instruction 4b: write probe files under `$TMPDIR`, never in the working tree, with the reason and this incident stated inline. Verified on the next two lanes: agy reviewed both with zero containment failures, and on `gh425` reported *"I executed `test/gh425-source-url-slug.sh` outside the test tree in an isolated `$TMPDIR` and all assertions passed"* — full verification, no violation. **Python lane only:** `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh` is a GH-308 frozen twin and is byte-unchanged (`gh308-frozen-twin-guard` 32/0, `marathon-drive` 142/0).
CHANGELOG.md:863:- **GH-397 — the reviewer's containment boundary was about to be moved onto an honor system the repo had already proven does not hold (#456, `ed937d8`).** `NEXT:` carries two incompatible value domains: `/relay` writes a ROLE (`Producer`/`Reviewer`), marathon-drive writes an AGENT ID, and the shared reader `rtl_is_reviewer_turn` understood only the former — so on every marathon reviewer turn it returned false and the reviewer kept the full `ALLOW_PATHS` allowlist over the artifact it was reviewing, which is the 2026-06-20 agy over-reach. The first fix asked the acting model, in prompt prose, to rewrite the header itself. **That was rejected in review on evidence already in the tree:** `test/agy-turn.sh` (S2) exists specifically to pin *"KNOWN GAP reproduced — NEXT was NOT flipped and nothing caught it"*, and the failure direction is OPEN — one forgotten flip silently restores artifact write authority. The role is now DERIVED from marathon-drive's machine-readable role directive plus `RELAY_AGENT`, which relay-drive exports from the **tick token** — two pieces of state no agent authors. Plain `/relay` threads, hand-run turns, and pre-directive relays fall through to the historical `NEXT:` test byte-for-byte; a `builder == reviewer` self-review lane carries no role signal and deliberately falls through rather than guessing. **Both lanes fixed by one change** — `utils/py/rtl.py` shells out to the same function and `relay-turn-lib.sh` is not a frozen twin, so the Bash fleet gets it too. `test/gh397-reviewer-turn-role.sh` (11 asserts) was confirmed RED against the pre-fix tree before being trusted green, on the case the whole design exists for: the reviewer stays scoped when the builder never flipped `NEXT:` at all.
CHANGELOG.md-864-- **GH-401 — `--dry-run` mutated the repo, and the audit written to catch exactly that class reported PASS the entire time (#456, `ed937d8`).** The relay write and `os.makedirs(phase_dir)` both now sit below the dry-run exit, so a dry run touches the filesystem not at all; the render is emitted to stdout between explicit fences instead, so the flag still shows its work. **The more useful half was the guard:** `test/marathon-root-audit.sh` is the GH-209 guard for *"every test invocation of the marathon driver is `MARATHON_ROOT`-scoped"*, and its scope was the two hardcoded filenames `marathon.sh` and `marathon-drive.sh` — `test/gh268-relay-cue-and-target-checks.sh` was out of its reach because of its FILENAME, not because it was safe. Widened to audit every test script, it immediately surfaced a **third** unscoped invocation nobody had reported, `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh:270`; coverage went 2 invocations → 40, all scoped. **Two existing tests had encoded the defect as the contract** and had to be corrected, not deleted: `marathon-drive.sh` case (1) asserted `[ -f phases/p1/RELAY.md ]` *after* a dry run — the suite would have failed if the bug were fixed — and `debug-mantra.sh` used the dry-run write as its render-inspection mechanism (a legitimate need: it must render without driving a phase or disturbing `.tick/attempts/<lane>`, the counter each of its cases hand-seeds), so it reads the fenced render from stdout instead. `test/gh401-dry-run-no-mutation.sh` carries a positive control so "nothing was written" cannot pass for the wrong reason, and aims at a throwaway `MARATHON_ROOT` so a future regression can never dirty the real repo just by running the suite — which is how the polluted file got committed in the first place. **The headline claim measured rather than asserted: `git status --porcelain` is now byte-identical before and after a full `validate.sh` run** (159 tests, exit 0; CI `tier1` pass).

CHANGELOG.md-883-- **Five more Litmus capture docs — #343, #358, #375, #388, #401 — all preflight READY, bringing the release to 12 gated lanes.** Each carries its issue's acceptance block verbatim (`match` at 6/7/7/7/5 criteria), a preflight contract whose probe polarity was verified against the tree, and a phase split. **#344 and #390 were deliberately excluded**: both have implementations in flight — #390's in PR #393, #344's root-resolution half already merged — and preparing them as fresh marathon lanes would queue a rebuild of existing work. **The pre-check was run first this time.** After #416 and #344 both turned out mostly-shipped, every one of these five was checked for an open PR, a branch, and a matching commit on `development` before a word was written; all five came back clean. That check costs a minute and is exactly what preflight cannot do, which is #418. **Each doc records what the codex+agy review changed about its criteria**, because the revision is often the most useful thing in it: #343's *"the two branches agree"* was satisfiable by making the **correct** branch wrong; #375's identity assertion named neither the field nor a valid response; #388's *"partial transcript"* was satisfiable by an empty pre-created file, and one of its criteria rested on a false premise about what the PDDA lint scans; #401's *"writes nothing into any git repository"* would have broken a legitimate existing test that renders into a caller-supplied fixture root. **#358 gained two criteria that came from reading the code rather than the issue** — every appender's exit status is discarded (`wait "$p" 2>/dev/null || true`, in two places), and two different lock bounds are in play, so a report naming "the timeout" is not actionable. **#401 is no longer a historical report:** its defect fired three times across these sessions, each needing a hand revert before unrelated work could be committed, and once nearly rode into a commit. Ratings and phase splits are provisional. → [#343](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/343) · [#358](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/358) · [#375](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/375) · [#388](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/388) · [#401](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/401)

CHANGELOG.md:886:- **PR triage: #411 closed as superseded, #393 diagnosed as 26 commits stale.** **#411** ("GH-329 + GH-344") was **CI-green and would have regressed the file**: its commits are not ancestors of `development`, but the same work landed independently via `1612878`, and `38af517` (GH-369) then built on it. Real tree divergence `development → #411` is **+6 / −64** — its `find-doc.sh` is 80 lines against `development`'s 94 and **lacks GH-369's valueless-`--root` guard entirely**, the fix for a script that otherwise spins forever. `git merge-tree` also reports conflicts. The green `tier1` is the point worth recording: it verified that the tests pass, not that the branch was stale, which is #416's shape. **#393** ("GH-390 Phase 1", +946/−12) fails four assertions, and three are staleness — `path-integrity`, the GH-189 doc-side stale-status scan, and GH-284 Phase 3's missing-`Milestone:` warning are exactly the guardrails #416 restored *after* this branch's last update, and a full suite on `development` has none of them. **The fourth is its own and is real:** `expected reason gate-killed for the CPU cap, got 'pre-advance-failed'` — a resource kill reported as the gate having found a defect, which is #407's mislabel and the exact criterion now written into #390's acceptance. Recommended a rebase rather than performing it; force-pushing a branch this session did not create is not a call to make unasked. → [#411](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/411) · [#393](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/393) · [#416](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/416)

CHANGELOG.md-889-- **GH-368: `marathon-plan.sh` documented `--check` as a drift guard running in `validate.sh`; `validate.sh` invokes it zero times.** The smallest, cleanest instance of the #419 class in the tree — *a documented guard that reads as active while nothing runs it* — same family as #315 (a stale relay token let a build-nothing run report success), #319 (the gate word-split its own path and passed on a 0-byte file) and #348 (parity evidence that did not cover forward drift). The flag itself works; nothing calls it, so a hand-edited or stale `MARATHON-PLAN-<date>.md` can diverge from what the ledger renders with the suite fully green. **Scoped to the issue's Option B** — delete the claim — with Option A (actually wiring it in) left open on #368, because it carries a real false-positive question the issue states plainly: `--check` fails whenever today's plan doc has not been re-rendered, so wiring it naively turns the suite red on an ordinary day, and *"a suite people learn to ignore protects nothing."* The determinism rationale the false parenthetical hung off is true and is kept; only the assertion about `validate.sh` is removed, and the Usage text at `:72`/`:123` already documented `--check` correctly as a manual command. **The edit target is a GH-308 FROZEN twin**, which is the whole reason this lane was sequenced before #418: that lane's new frozen-artifact check would refuse this one, and weakening the check to accommodate a one-line comment would have been the wrong trade. Declared instead through the mechanism that already exists for it — a per-file `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer (GH-321) — and verified with CI's own invocation, which reports *"utils/marathon-plan.sh — covered by a declared Frozen-twin-exception"* and *"every frozen-twin edit in this range is accounted for."* No behaviour change; `utils/py/marathon_plan.py` never carried the claim. → [GH-368-MARATHON-PLAN-CHECK-CLAIM.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-368-MARATHON-PLAN-CHECK-CLAIM.md) · [#368](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/368) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)

CHANGELOG.md-910-### Fixed
CHANGELOG.md-911-- **GH-416: the PDDA sync silently deleted three shipped guardrails, and CI stayed red on `development` for two days because the failures read as noise.** `cfd56b0` — *"land the upstream PDDA sync and close the two failures it arrived with"* — replaced the sync-managed `utils/pdda/**` tree wholesale. It closed two failures and left **three**, which were then carried as "pre-existing" by everyone who looked, including in PR #413's own body. They were not noise. Diffing across the commit: **(1)** GH-189's 3-COMPLETED stale-status scan — `non-terminal` went **4 occurrences → 0** in `pdda.sh` and existed nowhere else in the repo; **(2)** GH-189's entire **`roadmap-issue-state` subcommand**, **5 → 0**, so the test invoking it got `unknown command` and the file exited 2; **(3)** GH-284 Phase 3's missing-`Milestone:` warning — the release → issue-set join key `/10days` depends on — reduced to a bare `printf`; **(4)** the roll-up's explicit `Milestone: (none — release cannot resolve to an issue set)` line; **(5)** four broken path references introduced into `path-integrity`'s scan. Only (5) was cosmetic. **(2) and (4) were invisible until (1) and (3) were fixed**, because the test files fail-fast — the same broken-observation family as #315/#319/#351, where a failure that has been red a while stops being read as information at all. **The root cause is structural, not clerical:** local checks were living inside a tree that is replaced wholesale, and `pdda.sh` offers no extension seam (it sources only its own `pdda-lib.sh`), so every check this repo added upstream was on borrowed time. Fixed by moving them **out** of the sync surface into repo-owned `utils/pdda-local-checks.sh`, which sources only `pdda-lib.sh` and carries its own copy of the four private helpers that live in the un-sourceable CLI; findings are byte-identical and the functions were extracted mechanically from git rather than retyped. `test/pdda-local-checks.sh` guards them **falsifiably** — every check gets a fixture that must trip it *and* one that must not, plus a drift detector comparing the copied terminal-word list against upstream's, because an "exit 0" assertion would pass against a deleted check body, which is precisely the bug. Wired into `validate.sh` **and** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so they run against the real repository, which `pdda.sh run` used to do for them. `path-integrity` now skips `utils/pdda/**` with the reason recorded at the exemption: those tokens describe upstream's tree, and no edit here survives a sync. **Behaviour (4)'s INFO → WARN change is kept, not reverted** — upstream's reasoning (*"A check that could not run is NOT a check that passed"*) is better than what it replaced and is the same principle GH-400 applies to acceptance fidelity, so the stale test was updated to pin that the state is reported and never escalates to ERROR. Found while writing the fix: the `path-integrity` comment documenting the four broken paths **quoted them, and tripped the very check it documents** — they are now described rather than spelled out. `validate.sh` **0 failures**, the first fully green local suite since `cfd56b0`, and `tier1` green on PR #413. → [#416](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/416)
CHANGELOG.md-912-- **GH-399/GH-400: an agy QA relay found two real gate bypasses, and both were reproduced before being fixed.** Reviewed via `relay-xyz` with a review-only allowlist; 2 Blockers, 2 Shoulds, 1 Nit, all accepted. **(1)** An issue whose `## Acceptance` section *exists but lists nothing* returned `[]`, and the caller collapsed `[]` with `None` → `unknown` → **no block**, so a capture doc could invent arbitrary criteria under its own heading. `extract_acceptance_criteria`'s own docstring said the two cases must stay distinct *because collapsing them would let a doc dodge the gate*; the caller collapsed them anyway — the defect was in the gap between the documented intent and its one consumer. **(2)** Extraction stopped at the first **unindented** line, so an explanatory paragraph between criteria truncated the list — worse than reported, because `collect_inline_checklist` kept scanning: the two extractors **disagreed about the same document**, and the packet would inline three criteria while the fidelity check compared two. **(3)** `## Acceptance:` and `## Acceptance Criteria (draft)` read as "no section" → another silent `unknown` bypass; relaxed **more narrowly than proposed**, since dropping the `$` anchor outright would also match a prose heading like *"## Acceptance is not required here"* (pinned by a negative case). **(4)** The review correctly identified three cases that pass against the pre-fix code — they were exactly the 1 and the 2 that passed in the pre-fix runs. **Kept and labelled rather than deleted:** they are the cry-wolf controls, and a gate that flags faithful copies is precisely the failure that gets a gate switched off; each now names its falsifiable sibling. **(5)** An arrow inside a criterion broke `[changed]` parsing — **fixed differently than proposed**, because `rsplit` is also wrong: with three arrows neither the first nor the last is the separator, so the parser now offers every split as a candidate and reconciliation picks the one matching the actual diff. Suites 21 → **26/0** and **14/0**. **The review turn itself exited 6:** agy wrote `scratch-reviewer.md` off-allowlist and `rtl_check` reverted it — GH-22's backstop working — with the content recovered from `.tick/orphan-backups/`; another instance of the known agy-oversteps-allowlist pattern, on a turn whose `ALLOW_PATHS` was deliberately empty. → [thread](relay-system/2026-08-03/gh399-400-acceptance-qa.md)
CHANGELOG.md:913:- **GH-399: the packet's acceptance block kept only each criterion's first line, so every hard-wrapped requirement reached the builder as a half-sentence.** Second cut in the same chain as #400 — that one is the capture doc drifting from the issue, this is the packet drifting from the capture doc. Preflight matched only lines *beginning* a `- [ ]` bullet; capture docs hard-wrap at ~80 columns, so continuations were discarded **silently**, under a heading asserting the criteria were *"inlined from the capture doc."* **10 of 10 lanes** in one marathon lost 1–4 lines each. The issue's GH-201 evidence, now the test fixture: *"An explicit `--database` path that does not exist raises a clear error instead"* — the clause *"of silently resolving to the canonical DB"* never reached the builder, and the second criterion ended on an em dash, so what survived reads as an order to **preserve** the fallback the issue exists to remove. Because the reviewer grades against the same packet, there was no intact copy anywhere for either role to check. **Correction to the report:** it cites `utils/swarm-preflight.sh:882`; GH-308 **froze** that twin and it does not execute — the live defect was the identical regex in `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py`. **Fixed** with indent-gated continuation folding (reusing #400's extractor — ungated folding swallows a trailing `---` or the next paragraph, which is not theoretical: it produced a real false positive while dogfooding #400), extraction bounded to `## Acceptance` where one exists, an announced 25-item cap, and a lossless-copy check that re-parses the **rendered** block — deliberately not the structure that produced it, since comparing text to its own generator proves nothing — and sets NOT-READY rather than warning. `readiness.acceptance_inline` records scope, count, cap and losslessness for post-hoc audit. **One criterion was narrowed and the change declared** through #400's deviations mechanism, which is its first real use: bounding extraction *unconditionally* to `## Acceptance` — as the issue asks — would empty the acceptance block of **32 of this repo's 33 active capture docs**, which keep their checkboxes under `## Phase N`, deleting every lane's definition of done to close a leak the issue itself files as *"not yet observed."* **That declaration then exposed a hole in #400's own checker**, found by dogfooding: reconciliation only ran when the two lists differed, so a deviation declared against a still-verbatim list passed vacuously — a reader would believe a criterion was narrowed while the list said otherwise. Reconciliation now runs whenever the section exists (`test/gh400-acceptance-fidelity.sh` C8b, **21/0**). New `test/gh399-packet-acceptance-continuation.sh` **14/0** pins the whole chain — capture doc → `packet.md` → **relay file** — byte-for-byte at each hop, because asserting only the packet leaves the last hop, the one the builder actually reads, unproven; observed **2 pass / 12 fail** against pre-fix code. Writing that chain test cost one **orphaned `marathon_drive` holding `.git/relay-driver.lock` in the live repo** — the driver resolves ROOT to the harness clone unless `MARATHON_ROOT` is set, so the fixture run locked the real repository and hung — so the test now sets `MARATHON_ROOT` and runs under a hard 60s timeout, on the GH-369 principle that an unattended suite must fail on a hang rather than inherit it. → [GH-399-PACKET-ACCEPTANCE-CONTINUATION.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-399-PACKET-ACCEPTANCE-CONTINUATION.md) · [#399](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/399)
CHANGELOG.md-914-- **GH-400: `/10days` capture docs restated a GitHub issue's acceptance criteria instead of copying them, and preflight now refuses to emit a packet when the two have diverged without explanation.** Step 4 has a model summarise an issue into `PROJECT/2-WORKING/`, and everything downstream — preflight, the packet, the relay file, the builder, the reviewer — reads the **summary**; the issue text reaches none of them, so the summary silently becomes the contract and **no undamaged copy of the requirement exists anywhere in the pipeline**. **The measured case is an inversion, verified byte-for-byte against both source repos before any code was written:** `rebalance-OS` #202 requires a malformed row be *"proven to be either reconciled or surfaced, never silently dropped from the projection"*; the capture doc `/10days` wrote (commit `b941299`) instead requires asserting *"the exporter's actual current behavior (drop the row, continue processing the rest)"*; two criteria were dropped outright, including the one written specifically to prevent what shipped. The delivered artifact is **worse than the report claimed** — `3673257f` adds a test function literally named **`malformed_source_row_is_dropped`**, asserting `assert_not_contains "$out" 'truncated row'`, and a second independent run (`7525d047`) produced the same thing, because both were instructed to. Every gate was green, the reviewer approved, the phase closed; it surfaced only when a human read the issue and the test side by side weeks later. **Two corrections to the report, both load-bearing:** its suggested fix rests on *"preflight already fetches the issue for freshness checks"* — **it does not**, neither twin invokes `gh` in any form (freshness is `git fetch` + local probes), so this introduces the first issue-body fetch onto that path and has to carry its own offline contract; and companion #399 cites `utils/swarm-preflight.sh:882`, which GH-308 **froze** — the line that actually executes is `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:844`. **The fix is three parts.** (1) `skills/10days/SKILL.md` §4 now requires the `## Acceptance` block be reproduced byte-for-byte (re-wrapping allowed, nothing else), requires `source:` to carry the issue URL, and demotes the contract's `remediation.criteria` to an explicitly-labelled ranking summary rather than the definition of done. (2) `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py` re-fetches the issue and compares; unexplained divergence is **NOT-READY / exit 5 with no packet written**, and the packet now states in the builder's own context window whether its checklist was verified against the issue or merely inlined. (3) The only supported way to diverge is a machine-checked `## Acceptance — deviations from the issue` section (`- [dropped|changed|added] <text> — reason: <why>`) whose entries must reconcile the two lists **exactly** — an entry naming a criterion that is not actually different is rejected, so the section cannot become a rubber stamp, and there is deliberately **no env-var bypass**: a deviation belongs in the doc where the next reader finds it. **Undeterminable is not divergence** — no `gh`, unauthenticated, offline, or an issue with no acceptance section all report `unknown` loudly and never block, because an unreachable network is not evidence of drift. **Measured before choosing the posture rather than after:** all 33 `2-WORKING` docs carrying a `gh_issue` were compared against their live issues (33/33 fetches succeeded), **0** would newly read NOT-READY — 32 of the 33 issues have no `## Acceptance` section at all — so the hard fail the issue asked for costs nothing today. New `test/gh400-acceptance-fidelity.sh` (**20/0**, hermetic via a stubbed `gh`) pins the real GH-202 pair, and was **observed failing against the pre-fix code: 1 pass / 19 fail, with the inversion emitting `verdict: ready (exit 0)` and a written packet.** Cases 2–4 are the half that keeps it honest — a checker that flags the inversion but also flags a faithful copy is noise that gets switched off — and case 4 exists because **dogfooding this check against issue #400 itself caught a real false positive**: a GitHub body's trailing `---` and italic sign-off were being folded into the last criterion, so a byte-perfect copy reported as diverged. Continuation folding is indent-gated as a result, which also means the comparison sees the full text of a hard-wrapped criterion — the content #399 truncates at the packet-inlining site, deliberately left for #399 to fix rather than absorbed here. → [GH-400-CAPTURE-DOC-ACCEPTANCE-FIDELITY.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-400-CAPTURE-DOC-ACCEPTANCE-FIDELITY.md) · [#400](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/400) · [#399](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/399)

CHANGELOG.md-928-- **GH-372: removed `LICENSE.md`, leaving AGPL-3.0-only as the repo's single, unambiguous license.** Operator decision. Found during an artifact sweep, and **it was my error**: `1a1b5bc` added `LICENSE` (AGPL-3.0-only) + `LICENSE-COMMERCIAL.md` and flipped `package.json` from `ISC` to `AGPL-3.0-only` **without noticing `LICENSE.md` already existed** (`1b88b68`, 2026-06-14) declaring a *Personal-Use / Commercial* dual license © Neochrome, Inc. with an Apache-2.0 option. These were not two options in one scheme but two schemes making incompatible claims about the same code: AGPL grants everyone — companies included — commercial use conditioned on source disclosure, while `LICENSE.md` stated *"You may not use this software… for commercial purposes"* and routed all business use through a paid license. A recipient reading `LICENSE` could lawfully do what `LICENSE.md` forbade, and with neither file marked as superseding the other, ambiguity in a license is normally construed against the drafter. GitHub had already stopped being able to resolve it, classifying the repo as **`Other`**. Verified before removal that nothing depends on the file: **no reference in `test/`, `utils/`, `relay-automation/`, `validate.sh`, or the vendoring/packaging scripts**. Two remaining mentions are deliberately left alone — `REPO_MAP.md` is auto-generated and banner-marked *"do not edit by hand"*, and `ROADMAP.md`'s GH-71 entry is a point-in-time historical record, which that entry itself establishes as the convention. **Timing is why this was worth blocking on:** the contradiction existed on `development` only — `main` was 9 commits behind and never carried `LICENSE`, and `v0.1.0` was tagged before `1a1b5bc` — so it was resolved before reaching the release trunk rather than after. → [#372](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/372)
