CHANGELOG.md:931:- **GH-370: the GH-336 plan doc cited an engine that no longer exists — including a no-`gh`-call test that could not fail.** PR #350's own body recorded this re-test as outstanding; this closes that gap. Rounds 1–4 verified every code citation against `utils/py/_marathon_plan_node.js`, which **#340 deleted**. Re-run against `origin/development@9082328` in a clean worktree: **7 of 8 findings hold**, one broke, and two new defects surfaced that the original review could not have caught. **The sharpest is defect 2, and it is live rather than stale:** the kill-switch criterion specified a `gh` stub "that fails loudly if invoked," which against this engine is *undetectable* — `_resolve_gh` runs the binary with `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` and folds any non-zero exit into `GH_MODE = "off"`, so the scream is discarded and the failure is indistinguishable from "`gh` not installed." Demonstrated rather than argued: a stub echoing to stderr and exiting 42 produced **zero** observable output, while a **file tripwire** in the same run recorded `gh auth status`. A fixture written as specified would have been green and worthless — this repo's recurring family (#315/#319/#348/#368/#369), *a signal that reads as protection while nothing is checked*, and the sixth instance logged. The criterion now mandates a file tripwire and states why an exit code carries no information. **The claim that broke** was round 4's proudest `[Pass]` — that the hook point was "real and already proven," citing `_inject_review_lanes`. #340 folded it into the engine (`_marathon_plan.py:1297`) and `marathon_plan.py` shrank ~390 → **212** lines with no post-render *mutation* step, so a builder following the note would hunt a deleted function; the seam is now named as the gap between `engine.run()` (`:170`) and the first mode branch (`--check` `:181`, `--dry-run` `:197`, write `:201`). **Codex caught three citation defects in my own corrections** on review (PR #371) and all three were right: `:181` was cited as though it opened all three branches when it opens only `--check`; the `_marathon_plan.py:450` link did not actually span the `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` on `:451` or the `except` on `:452-453` that the claim rests on; and "no post-render step **at all**" was overstated — the wrapper still performs check/dry-run/write handling at `:181-205`, and the narrow true claim is that nothing rewrites the rendered bytes. Fixed in the same PR. Worth recording rather than smoothing over: this correction pass was itself imprecise in exactly the way it was written to catch. **Codex's second pass then found the sixth stale citation** — the out-of-scope bullet cited `marathon-plan.sh:54` for the `--check` drift-guard comment, but `:54` is a bare `#` and the claim is at **`:67`**. My citation audit missed it because it only walked markdown `(path#Lnnn)` links, and this one was written as a bare `` `file.sh:54` `` — **an audit whose scope didn't cover the shape the defect took**, which is the same family as the defects it was auditing for. The audit now walks bare `file:line` references too; all nine resolve in-range *and* content-match. Second pass verdict: 4 `[Pass]`, 1 `[Should]`, no pre-existing defects, and explicitly *"no remaining reference treats deleted `_marathon_plan_node.js` or `_inject_review_lanes` as live code."* Also corrected: `QP_GH_STATE_FILE` was offered as a usable env var when it is **internal to the Bash twin**, assigned from the real `QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE` at `marathon-plan.sh:179` — exporting it is a no-op on both lanes and silently runs a fixture live; two citations had drifted past end-of-file (`:378-391` against a 212-line file); and the `/10days` "no executable" claim was too strong now that the skill ships `find-doc.sh`/`install.sh`/`scan-issues.sh` (narrowed to *no plan-rendering entry point*, which is what the criterion actually needs). **Verified, not assumed:** all six surviving citations were checked in-range *and* content-matched by script; `QUEUE_PLAN_GH=off` and `QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE` each drive `gh` invocations to **0**; the fire list still renders 7 `**Wave N:**` lines ahead of the single `## How to fire a lane` anchor; churn re-measured at **528** commits/14d (`utils/py` 44, `relay-automation` 57) against round 4's 538/40/59 — same conclusion; `test/marathon-plan.sh` **72/0**. **The architecture is unchanged for the fifth time** — as with the three prior rewrites of its rationale, what needed fixing was the evidence and the test recipe, never the design. → [GH-336-PLANNING-CONTEXT.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-336-PLANNING-CONTEXT.md) · [#370](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/370)
CHANGELOG.md:932:- **GH-351: the registered dashboard gate rendered the artifact into the repo and then validated the copy it had just written.** `test/roadmap-dashboard.sh:27` ran the renderer — overwriting `$ROOT/ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md` — and `:34` then `--check`ed that file. The assertion could not fail, and its own pass string read *"--check passes on the committed artifact"*, which was false by the time it ran. **The renderer was never the defect and was not touched:** standalone `utils/roadmap-dashboard.sh --check` returned `rc=1` on all three of the day's stale dashboards, so the correct signal existed the whole time — the test overwrote its input before asking. A second, quieter fault: the test **wrote into `$ROOT`**, so `validate.sh` itself silently un-staled the dashboard mid-run, a suite repairing the evidence it was meant to judge and leaving the working tree dirty afterwards. Three stale dashboards reached `development` on 2026-07-30 alone from three different authors (GH-342, #356, #350); it fires on essentially every PR that edits `ROADMAP.md`, and the only reason it was ever caught was someone running the standalone checker by hand. Fixed with two rules whose case ordering is load-bearing: **`--check` runs first, against the committed artifact, before anything writes**, and nothing writes `$ROOT` — write-mode is exercised through `ROADMAP_DASHBOARD_OUTPUT`, which the renderer already supported, so no renderer change was needed. **4 → 9 cases**, adding a missing-artifact case, the source-drift direction that actually occurs in practice, a no-side-effect assertion, and — the one that keeps this honest — **a mutation proof**: cases 1 and 3 are unfalsifiable alone, so case 4 plants a canary line in a copy and requires `--check` to reject it. **Verified against the real commit rather than a synthetic fixture:** replaying `719867f` (the #350 merge, genuinely stale), the old test scores **4 pass / 0 fail** while the new one scores **6 pass / 3 fail**. Two things visible only by running it — the old test left `ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md` modified in the fixture afterwards, and **case 9 (section counts) was already correct in the old file and still reported green** because the regeneration ran first: the bug did not add a bad assertion, it *disabled a good one* (`roadmap=128 dashboard=127` is what it should have been saying). Sixth instance of *an assertion that compares a thing to a freshly-derived copy of itself*, after #348, #342, #362(B) and #369 — the last of which was in a test written earlier the same day. The recurring lesson is not "write more tests" but **run the new test against the old code**; every one of these was caught that way and none by review. → [GH-351-DASHBOARD-TEST-GRADES-ITS-OWN-ANSWER-KEY.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-351-DASHBOARD-TEST-GRADES-ITS-OWN-ANSWER-KEY.md) · [#351](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/351)
CHANGELOG.md:933:- **GH-369: `/10days`' capture-doc lookup spun forever on a valueless `--root`, and blamed a flag the caller never passed for a bad `$TENDAYS_ROOT`.** Found reviewing PR #364 before merge — #364's own fix is correct and shipped; these are defects in the argument parser it introduced. `find-doc.sh --root` with no value **looped indefinitely**: `shift 2` with one argument remaining shifts nothing and returns non-zero, and the script is deliberately `-e`-exempt (documented analysis-tool profile), so `$#` never decreased, `$1` stayed `--root`, and the branch re-ran forever. Confirmed under an `alarm(5)` wrapper — **rc=142/SIGALRM, no output**. That matters more than a usage nit because `/10days` is explicitly an *unattended* skill, so this stalls a sweep with no error, no output and no timeout: an absent signal, the same shape as #315/#319/#351 rather than a wrong answer. Second defect: a bad `$TENDAYS_ROOT` printed `--root not a directory:` — naming a flag never passed, with an **empty path**, because the message hardcoded `--root` and interpolated `$ROOT_ARG`. Now tracks which of the four sources (`--root`, `$TENDAYS_ROOT`, git toplevel, `$PWD`) supplied the value and reports that one. My first cut of that fix reproduced the same class of bug — it printed `$ROOT`, which the failed command substitution had already emptied — kept as `$ROOT_RAW` with a comment. New `test/gh369-find-doc-root-resolution.sh` (**14/0**) registered in `validate.sh`; the file previously had **no test at all** and was absent from `TESTS=()`, which is why both defects and GH-344 before them landed unchallenged. **Observed failing before the fix rather than merely passing after:** against `1612878` (post-#364, pre-fix) **12/2**, exactly cases 1 and 2, with the hang *reported as a failure instead of hanging the suite*; against `4dc27b4` (pre-#364, the GH-344 bug) **4/10**, case 6 catching it with *"answered GH-163 from the HARNESS tree"*. **Case 6 is itself a caught mistake worth recording:** as first written it probed issue 777, absent from both trees — so the harness-relative bug and correct behaviour both returned `null` and it passed against the very code it existed to catch. It now derives a real `GH-<N>` from the harness's own `PROJECT/` tree, which is what makes that pre-#364 failure detectable. A fifth member of this repo's recurring family: *an assertion that cannot distinguish the bug from the fix.* → [#369](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/369) · [#364](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/364)

CHANGELOG.md-988-- **GH-322 (the port): GH-284 Phase 2 shipped in July and had never once executed — *both* halves lived only in the Bash twin.** #324 stopped `--log-github` being silently discarded; this makes it do something. `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh` `exec`s `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` at its own **line 18**, while the `EXIT` trap that runs the run log and stops the heartbeat is installed at **line 244** — so under the default lane (`XYZ_PYTHON` unset since GH-264) the process was replaced before either could ever be wired up. Every marathon since Phase 2 merged ran, exited 0, reported success, and observed nothing. **#322's own scope statement was wrong, and the correction is the substantive finding here:** it deferred only the run log on the grounds that "the driver heartbeat *is* already in the Python twin (12 references)" — those 12 matches are `xyz_marathon_heartbeat_*`, the **GH-75 `XYZ.heartbeat.json` session record**, an unrelated file and feature; `grep -c driver_heartbeat utils/py/marathon_drive.py` returned **0**. Two different features named "heartbeat" in one file, told apart only by prefix, is what let a grep agree with the wrong conclusion. Both halves are now ported: the heartbeat (write, refresh thread, clear, `RTL_DRIVER_HEARTBEAT_FILE` honored) writes a record byte-compatible with `rtl_driver_heartbeat_write` — same six fields, same atomic `mkstemp`+`os.replace` — so the Bash reader and the Python writer agree; and `--log-github` is a real flag with `run_gate_result` tracking behind it. Exit handling mirrors the Bash trap's contract exactly (code resolved first, hooks in a `finally`, original code re-exited), so reporting can never change the driven run's result. `runlog_find_comment_id` sits at **module scope**: in Bash the same parser could only be reached through a `python3` subprocess, and the invocation shape itself (SC2259) silently broke it for a release — in-process kills the failure class, and importable means the test drives the real function instead of a copy of its logic. New `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh` (**5 pass / 19 fail against pre-change code, 26 / 0 after**) is the counterpart to `test/gh284-runlog-heartbeat.sh`, every driver invocation in which is pinned to `XYZ_PYTHON=0` — which is exactly why that suite could not see any of this; the new file `unset XYZ_PYTHON`s deliberately. `test/gh322-unknown-arg-rejection.sh`'s `--log-github` block was **inverted**: "refuse loudly and name the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` workaround" was an interim contract, and a lane that still refused a flag it now implements would be the bug. **Deliberately left as-is:** the run log's `driver still running` field can only ever read `running` — the hook asks for status *before* clearing the heartbeat, and the PID it checks is the process asking. The Bash twin has the identical ordering (`:238` then `:239`), so it is inherited, not introduced, and porting it faithfully beats opening a silent twin divergence — the exact disease #320 and #322 are. → [GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md) · [#322](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/322)
CHANGELOG.md-989-- **GH-320: the executing Python lane capped turns at a third of the documented budget.** An agy review turn died with `agy -p exceeded 300s wall-clock cap` on a shim whose header *and* code both read 900. XYZ has been Python-default since GH-264, so `relay-automation/agy-turn.sh` `exec`s `utils/py/agy-turn.py` — which defaulted to **300**. Same split in `codex-turn` (900↔300) and `claude-turn` (600↔300); `aider-turn` and `pi-turn` were consistent. Because Python is the lane that runs, 300 s was the **real** ceiling for three of five turn-takers while every operator-facing document said otherwise, and the failure surfaces as `exit 7` — *turn timeout / hang* — which reads as a hung model rather than a misconfigured ceiling. The natural response to that, retrying, burns another turn at the same wrong cap. **GH-308's freeze does not cover this class:** freezing the Bash twins stops them drifting *forward* and says nothing about values that had already diverged before the banners landed; nothing in the suite compared the two numbers. Fixed by aligning the three Python defaults with their twins. New `test/gh320-twin-timeout-parity.sh` reads the default out of **both** files for all five shims and compares them — **no expected value is hardcoded**, since a third copy of the number would just be a third thing to drift — and separately asserts that each Bash header's documented `(default: N)` matches that file's own code, because the header is what misled. 10 pass / 0 fail. **Deliberately still open:** nothing establishes the turn timeout was the only constant that diverged pre-freeze; a general Bash↔Python constant-parity sweep belongs to GH-308 Phase 2. → [GH-320-TWIN-TURN-TIMEOUT-DRIFT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-320-TWIN-TURN-TIMEOUT-DRIFT.md) · [#320](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/320)
CHANGELOG.md-990-- **GH-321: the frozen-twin escape hatch was range-scoped — one trailer excused every twin edit in the PR.** The `Frozen-twin-exception:` hatch shipped in PR #318 passed the guard for **every** frozen twin touched in `BASE..HEAD` as soon as *any* commit in the range carried the trailer — including files nobody reasoned about, in commits that declared nothing, possibly by a different author. CI then printed `1 commit(s) declare Frozen-twin-exception — allowing:` and listed the **declaring** commit, so the log read like a narrow reviewed exception while the undeclared edit was **never named**. The trailer's whole value is making an exception auditable, and range scoping broke exactly that property in the case where it counts. Marathon PRs are the common case and the worst shape for it: 4+ autonomous lanes on one branch make an undeclared twin edit riding behind someone else's declared exception the expected accident, not an exotic one. Same class as #319 and #315 — *a green signal that means less than it appears, with nothing in the output revealing the gap* — and it was disclosed at merge time rather than found later. A trailer must now **name the twin(s) it covers** (`Frozen-twin-exception: relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh — <reason>`), and every changed twin in the range must be named by some trailer; failures name the uncovered file. **The rule moved out of inline `ci.yml` shell and into the guard script as `--allow-exceptions`** — inline YAML is unreachable from the suite, which is part of why the looseness shipped at all; `ci.yml` is now a single call. Per-file *across the range*, deliberately not "the trailer must be on the same commit as the edit": a later fixup correcting an earlier commit is ordinary and should not need re-declaration, and what the looseness actually cost was attribution, which naming the file recovers. A typo'd path fails loudly rather than silently covering nothing; the bare path-less form no longer covers anything (that form *is* the looseness); reason text is not scanned for paths, so a reason may cite `validate.sh` without being read as a coverage claim; strict mode (what `validate.sh` and `--staged` use) is unchanged. `test/gh308-frozen-twin-guard.sh` **15/0 → 27/0**, with a fixture built on **two** frozen twins because with one the range-scoped and file-scoped rules are indistinguishable — which is how this shipped. One case **reproduces** the defect rather than only asserting its absence: it evaluates #318's exact predicate on the same fixture and asserts it *would* have allowed the PR, so the suite says so if the fixture ever stops exercising the bug. The single historical trailer (`07ae1e7`) is the bare form and would fail this rule; it is already merged and CI only judges an open PR's own range, so no existing history is re-evaluated. → [#321](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/321)
CHANGELOG.md:991:- **PR #318 agy review: two Blockers closed, one Should implemented differently, one declined.** The review of the marathon PR was itself driven through the harness (`--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`, exit 5 = changes requested). Both Blockers were re-verified against source before being acted on. **(1)** `AGENTS.md` asserted that "CI supplies `GH308_FROZEN_TWIN_BASE`" — `grep -rn GH308_FROZEN_TWIN_BASE .github/` returned **0 matches**, so the frozen-twin guard had no enforcement anywhere. Added the `Frozen Bash twin guard (GH-308)` step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, with a `Frozen-twin-exception: <reason>` commit trailer as the documented escape hatch so a legitimate exception is auditable in `git log` rather than invisible. **(2)** The reviewer argued a silently-fake safety gate outranks the freeze policy, so `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh:493` is patched too — but the obvious shape was wrong: `printf '%q'` is eval-safe yet backslash-escapes the space rather than removing it, so the preflight regex at `:511` still captured `.../GH\` and would have `die`d "script file does not exist", trading a false pass for a hard failure. Single-quoting is eval-safe *and* regex-tractable, and is byte-identical to `shlex.quote()`'s output for the same path; the preflight regex now matches a fully quoted token. `test/gh319-gate-path-with-space.sh` drives **both** lanes — the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` cases fail against pre-fix Bash (7/2) and pass after (9/0). **(3)** The proposed fix for the GH-293 guard-marker fragility required editing `relay-drive.sh`, a frozen twin, to satisfy a `[Should]` — the wrong trade; the manifest now matches the guard's user-facing **diagnostic** (`turn cannot report: relay file`), which does not get reflowed. The underlying point was sharper than the example: `test/gh293-vendored-guard-drift.sh` was itself restating the old literal, so a manifest change would have left the test green while the guard check was dead — the fixture now **derives** the pattern from `SAFETY_GUARD_PATTERNS` and asserts it stripped something (15/0). **(4)** Declined the suggestion to isolate `test/pdda-repo-contract.sh` from `validate.sh`: CI already fails the PR on those errors, so the coupling predates the change — what changed is finding out locally in 8 minutes instead of after a push, which is precisely what GH-311 exists to fix.
CHANGELOG.md-992-- **GH-319: every marathon phase reported "gate passed" without the gate ever running — the default gate word-split on the space in the repo's own path and executed an unrelated 0-byte file.** `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` built its default gate as an unquoted string (`f"bash {root}/validate.sh"`) and handed it to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. At a clone under `.../Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm` the shell split on the space and ran `bash $HOME/Documents/GH`, passing `Repos/.../validate.sh` as a positional argument. **`$HOME/Documents/GH` exists on this machine as a 0-byte file**, so bash executed an empty script: exit 0, no output, 0.0 s. Reproduced in isolation before anything was changed. **All four lanes of the 2026-07-27 gate-and-fleet-integrity marathon were approved with no gate**, while `bash validate.sh` on that exact tree was RED with two genuine failures (`relay-pkg-freshness`, `skill-extract` — GH-308's freeze banners had drifted `relay-pkg.tar.gz`). It was caught by timing, not by any signal the harness emits: `.tick/events/` showed **6.6 s and 7.5 s** between `agy-done` and `marathon.phase.approved` against a **483 s** real suite. **GH-238's gate-runnable preflight — which exists for exactly this — did not fire**, because its `^\s*(bash|/\S*/bash)\s+(\S+)` regex captured the same wrong fragment and `os.path.isfile()` on the decoy returned `True`; the guard and the gate agreed on the wrong file, and the preflight even carried quote-stripping logic for a quoted argument the default never produced. This is the third instance of one failure class in this program, after GH-315 (a stale relay token let a build-nothing run report success) and the sandboxed-`Monitor` liveness gap folded into GH-284 Phase 2: **a broken observation layer where failure is invisible and every available signal agrees.** Fixed with `shlex.quote` on the default path and `shlex.split` in the preflight, so the runnability check inspects the file the shell would actually execute. **Regression coverage was written to demonstrate the bug, not merely assert the fix** — `test/gh319-gate-path-with-space.sh` builds its fixture at a spaced path *and plants the same 0-byte decoy at the split point*, so a regression cannot hide behind a split prefix that happens not to exist; against pre-fix code the driver prints `phase p1 complete — STATUS: Approved, gate passed` and exits 0 while the fixture's gate exits 1 (4 pass / 2 fail), and post-fix it is 6/0 with the driver exiting 5. Registered in `validate.sh`. **Deliberately not fixed:** `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh:493` has the identical construction, but GH-308 froze that file in this same PR and AGENTS.md now directs behavior fixes to the Python twin — so an `XYZ_PYTHON=0` run at a spaced path still has a fake gate until GH-308 Phase 2 retires the twin. Historical marathon runs on this machine that reported "gate passed" are retroactively unverified; no audit of them is planned. Full `./validate.sh` 131/131, 0 FAIL lines, exit 0. → [GH-319-MARATHON-GATE-PATH-WORD-SPLIT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-319-MARATHON-GATE-PATH-WORD-SPLIT.md) · [#319](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/319)
CHANGELOG.md:993:- **MARATHON-2026-07-27 (gate + fleet integrity) fired: 4 sequential lanes, all approved, PR #318.** `gh311 → gh289 → gh293 → gh308`, builder codex / reviewer agy throughout, 2 turns per lane (4 for gh293). Each deliverable was verified by direct inspection of the diff against its brief rather than by the runner's summary line — which is how GH-319 surfaced. **GH-311** adds `test/pdda-repo-contract.sh`, running `utils/pdda/pdda.sh run` against the repo's real docs so `validate.sh` becomes a superset of tier1's PDDA contract; it immediately earned its place by catching two real errors in this changelog's own capture doc (a hardcoded `$HOME` path and a missing ROADMAP pointer). **GH-289** widens GH-245's fast-refusal from `--review-once` to every `--target-root` turn, so a BUILD turn refuses at startup instead of completing and discarding its Log; the `--review-once` diagnostic is preserved verbatim. **GH-293** adds a behavior-marker safety-guard manifest to `xyz-sync check` (a missing guard is now distinguishable from ordinary provenance drift, inspected in the installed copy rather than inferred from `source_commit`) and makes `update --all` refuse a dirty or non-canonical harness source without `XYZ_SYNC_ALLOW_UNSAFE_SOURCE=1`. **GH-308 Phase 1** stamps FROZEN banners on the 11 Tier-A Bash twins and records the policy in AGENTS.md/UPGRADE.md — no deletions, `XYZ_PYTHON=0` still reversible, with `utils/marathon-plan.sh` and `relay-turn-lib.sh` explicitly exempt. `relay-pkg.tar.gz` rebuilt (the freeze banners drift it). → [MARATHON.yaml](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-2026-07-27-GATE-AND-FLEET-INTEGRITY/MARATHON.yaml) · [#318](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/318)
CHANGELOG.md-994-- **GH-312: `xyz-sync update` / `xyz-vendor.sh` silently destroyed the target repo's live runtime state — fixed by preserving it across the vendor swap, with three more at-risk paths than the report identified.** `materialize_vendor()` builds a staged mirror of the harness and swaps it in over an unconditional `rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR"`. The stage is mirrored purely from `$HARNESS_ROOT`, so everything the *target* accumulated at runtime was deleted unread — and since `ensure_gitignore` keeps `.xyz/` out of git, nothing under it was ever hashed into a git object, leaving **no reflog, stash, or `git fsck --lost-found` recovery**. It exited 0 and printed success. A real incident on 2026-07-27 destroyed a completed two-round Codex relay thread plus its full `.tick/` event log; the findings survived only because the Codex CLI transcripts happen to live in `$TMPDIR`, outside the harness. **The intake report's requested fix was incomplete:** it named `relay-system/`, `.tick/`, and `.relay-driver.lock`, but auditing what `.xyz/` actually accumulates (repo `.gitignore` + GH-75) turned up the completion-telemetry family — `XYZ.json` (the locked record array, 1.8 MB and actively written on the reporting machine), `XYZ.json.lock/` (its `mkdir` advisory lock), and `XYZ.heartbeat.json` — with **identical exposure**: none are in `VENDOR_DIRS`, so the stage never recreated them either. Implementing the report literally would have left the bug half-fixed; the shipped preserve list carries **six** paths, and a failed copy now `die`s *before* the destructive swap rather than proceeding. Preservation was chosen over a warning or a refusal because both still depend on an operator reading output at the right moment, and the docs frame `update` as deliberate (pinned + manual) but never as destructive. **Regression coverage was written first and observed failing** — new `test/gh312-vendor-preserves-state.sh` produced 6 failures against the pre-fix code and passes 14/14 post-fix — and it pins the *other* half of the contract too: VERSION must still restamp to live HEAD and `bin/tick` must survive, so a "fix" that preserved state by skipping the update cannot pass. It also covers the direct `xyz-vendor.sh` re-run over an existing `.xyz/`, which the capture flagged as an unverified open question and which had the same destructive swap (**answered: yes**). Docs: `xyz-sync.sh`'s header and `skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md` now state what `update` does to runtime state and that a new `.xyz/` artifact must join the preserve list. Reviewed by **agy** through a driven relay (`--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`): Approved with 4 `[Pass]` findings and no defects raised — disclosed as a clean but shallow signal, not independent corroboration. `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` rebuilt via `make-pkg.sh` (the fix touches `relay-automation/`, which drifts the vendored tarball); `relay-pkg-freshness.sh` 3/3 and full `./validate.sh` green (10 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped). **Deliberately still open:** whether durable runtime state belongs under a disposable, gitignored `.xyz/` at all — the capture's own sharper question, listed in its `non_goals`, and **not** closed by this fix. → [GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md) · [#312](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/312)
CHANGELOG.md-995-- **GH-304: relay-drive turn-taker prompt + worktree seeding used a CWD-relative relay-file path — broke same-repo vendored `.xyz/` installs for Codex.** Scaffolding/driving a relay from CWD=`.xyz` (the relay-xyz skill's documented `cd "$HARNESS"`) with a CWD-relative `--relay-file` embedded that raw string in the turn-taker's prompt and used it for worktree seeding. Since a same-repo vendored `.xyz/` has no `.git` of its own, the turn-taker's worktree roots at the *outer* repo top-level, where `relay-system/…` doesn't exist (the file is at `.xyz/relay-system/…`) — a 100% failure for Codex, masked for agy (which absolutizes the path itself). Fix: `relay-drive.sh` and `utils/py/relay_drive.py` now **absolutize `$RELAY_FILE` before exporting it** to the turn-taker (mirrors the existing `--artifact-file` handling), so it resolves identically from any CWD; `rtl_turn_prompt` (`relay-turn-lib.sh`) derives the repo-root-relative EDIT path robustly (physical-path strip, matching `rtl_init`'s allowlist normalization) so the embedded path and the seeded path stay in lockstep at the true `.xyz/relay-system/…`. **Secondary:** when the relay file is gitignored (this repo gitignores parts of `relay-system/`), `rtl_enforce`'s empty-commit case now prints a distinct "relay file is gitignored, changes are NOT git-tracked (expected, not a stall)" message instead of the ambiguous "no tracked changes (token-only move?)" that a passing and a failing run printed byte-identically. Proof: new `test/gh304-vendored-relay-path.sh` (11/11) unit-tests the allowlist normalization, prompt path, worktree seeding, and both empty-commit messages; related relay/worktree tests green locally. → [#304](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/304)
CHANGELOG.md-996-- **GH-295: PR #302 tier1 CI — two real gaps found and fixed.** `test/pi-turn.sh`'s fake `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` test fixtures ("test-key"/"test-key-not-real") were never added to `security-scan-baseline.txt`, tripping the GH-64 active gate (same pattern already baselined for `aider-turn.sh`/`deep-research.sh`). Separately, `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` had drifted from an earlier README edit on this branch and was never rebuilt, tripping `test/relay-pkg-freshness.sh`. Both fixed; `security-scan.sh`/`relay-pkg-freshness.sh` green locally.

CHANGELOG.md-1007-- **GH-280: Aider+Qwen reliability investigation concluded — root cause found and fix confirmed.** A live GH-268 Wave-1 exercise against the real production repo and the real `qwen3.8-max-preview` endpoint caught the first real failure transcript of the whole investigation: Aider auto-selects `whole` edit format for unlisted/custom model ids, but Qwen emits standard unified diffs regardless, which Aider silently discards as "no tracked changes" — the actual explanation for the historical ~86% aider-qwen failure rate, not general model unreliability. Re-running with `AIDER_FLAGS="--edit-format diff"` forced took the same task from 0/3 real edits to a 90%-complete, correct implementation landing in round 1, confirming the fix. Getting to this transcript required first closing a real observability gap: `aider-turn.sh` (and, since `XYZ_PYTHON` defaults on, the actually-executing `utils/py/aider-turn.py` and `utils/py/agy-turn.py`) were never using the GH-161 persistent-log helper, so every prior investigation round genuinely could not have captured a failure log — fixed in [#288](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/288)/[#290](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/290). Also found and fixed along the way, independent of Qwen: a fully-retired OpenRouter default model id (`openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`) that silently broke any plain `aider`/`consult` call omitting both `AIDER_MODEL` and `AIDER_OPENAI_API_BASE` — [#291](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/291), no separate issue filed. **Recommendation:** codex+agy remains the default builder pairing; Aider+Qwen is usable as a fallback with `--edit-format diff` and a generous timeout set explicitly. A separate, genuinely new gap was surfaced by the same session and filed on its own: `swarm-preflight.sh`'s suggested marathon invocations never default to `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=1` — [#294](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/294) (filed, not yet fired). → [GH-280 findings](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-280-AIDER-QWEN-VS-SONNET-INVESTIGATION.md) · [marathon plan](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-2026-07-23-GH279-GH280-AIDER-QWEN-FOLLOWUP.md) · [#280](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/280)

CHANGELOG.md-1053-
CHANGELOG.md-1054-### Fixed
CHANGELOG.md:1055:- **GH-241: `MARATHON.example.yaml` now states that phases run strictly one at a time and that `depends_on` is scalar-only — docs-only; the report's first claim was partially falsified before the fix was scoped.** First bug filed *through* the new `/file-xyz-bug` skill (from `rebalance-OS`, vendored `.xyz/`), and the first to exercise the "verify the report, don't apply it" gate. **Claim (1) as filed — "nothing signals sequential execution", evidenced by a 0-match grep — does not hold:** line 3 already read "runs … **in depends_on order**; the chain **HALTS** on the first phase that fails". The grep was a false negative, searching the literal `"in order"` against the string `"in depends_on order"`. The DX complaint survives in a narrower form, which is what got fixed: the line documented *ordering* but not *exclusivity*, and "in depends_on order" is precisely how a dependency-ordered **parallel** scheduler (`make -j`) describes itself — so the new text states execution is strictly one-at-a-time and that `depends_on` **constrains** ordering rather than **creating** it, since restating "runs in order" would not move a reader who read that line and still concluded concurrency. **Claim (2) reproduced exactly** against a local two-phase fixture: `depends_on: [p1]` → `depends_on unknown phase '[p1]'`, scalar parses fine; root cause is the hand-rolled YAML reader not implementing flow sequences, so `[p1]` survives as a literal scalar into the phase-id lookup (`bin/marathon-yaml:102-105`). The field table now marks the field scalar-and-single with the exact failure text, and the header recommends `--dry-run` as the standard pre-fire step. **Consistency finding the issue didn't call out:** `depends_on` (scalar, single) and `artifact` (comma-separated, multi) are adjacent rows of the same field table carrying two different multiplicity conventions — `artifact` documented its own, `depends_on` did not, leaving the reader to infer from the neighbour. **Deliberately NOT taken: suggested fix (3)**, a `^\[.*\]$` guard in `bin/marathon-yaml` — that is a code change plus a regression test, not doc-only, and stays open as defence-in-depth (the docs fix stops the author writing the list form; the guard would catch the one who writes it anyway). Verified no runtime change: `node bin/marathon-yaml relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` emits a byte-identical phase table before and after; `relay-pkg-freshness` 3/3 (the example is not a vendored path). → [#241](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/241)

A dependency-free local generator (`utils/swe-diagram/scripts/git-history-to-json.js`) reads local and remote-tracking branch refs and emits a capped, auditable diagram spec while documenting Git's inability to recover deleted branch names or squash/rebase provenance. Added a self-contained newest-20 example at `ARCHITECTURE/git-history-diagram.json`/`.html`. Verification: focused fixtures 29/29; Node syntax and skill validation; zero dangling endpoints; headless-Chrome inspection; and an independent 7-commit forward test with two branch cuts and two non-fast-forward merges. → [GH-201-SWE-DIAGRAM-GIT-LANES.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-201-SWE-DIAGRAM-GIT-LANES.md)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md:110:- **GH-549 · the pre-push gate is silently skipped on any branch without `githooks/`** 🆕 **captured + BUILT 2026-08-14, ships inside PR #545** — `core.hooksPath` is repo-scoped, not branch-scoped, so on a checkout with no `githooks/` directory git resolves no hook and **runs nothing, with no warning**. Observed live, not predicted: pushing `chore/ship-litmus-nightwatch` produced no gate output at all. The trap is structural — **the hook is the thing that does not run**, so nothing inside it can detect its own absence. Fix moves the entrypoint out of the working tree: `install.sh` writes a dispatch stub into the clone's `.git/hooks/` (branch-independent, and shared by every linked worktree) which execs the in-tree hook, falls back to `validate.sh` announced on older branches, and **refuses** when neither exists. Cross-model consult (codex + agy) converged on this and both rejected a check in `validate.sh`/`ci-local.sh` — a detector inside the failing component. Their split on stub location was settled by measurement, not argument. Pinned by a **real `git push`** harness against a local bare remote (every prior case invoked the hook directly, which is exactly what this defect was invisible to), plus the negative control that reproduces the pre-fix wiring sailing through ungated. → [GH-549-PREPUSH-BRANCH-INDEPENDENT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-549-PREPUSH-BRANCH-INDEPENDENT.md) · [#549](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/549) · [#544](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/544)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-118-- **GH-435 · XYZ's coordination model is a sequential chain, not a DAG** 🆕 **captured 2026-08-06** — a question about whether XYZ does "graph engineering" turned up a documentation gap, not a defect. The multi-phase model is coherent and its limits look deliberate, but nothing a reader meets says so: `README.md`'s Glossary describes Marathon as chaining phases "in `depends_on` order" and stops, so anyone carrying standard agent-graph vocabulary infers a DAG, parallel stages, and dependency-derived scheduling — none of which exist. Verified against `development`@`80cab6b`: `depends_on` is **scalar-only**, so a join is inexpressible (`MARATHON.example.yaml:42-46`; a list form parses as the literal string and aborts); phases run **strictly one at a time** and a disjoint write-set buys no parallelism (`MARATHON.example.yaml:7-11`, `marathon.sh:168` — one serial `while read` loop); `depends_on` **validates** authored order rather than deriving it, inverting the graph model; failure **halts** with no conditional edge (`marathon.sh:214-226`, nine exit codes → nine halt reasons); and **`Wave` appears in no executor** — only the renderers (`utils/marathon-plan.sh`, `utils/py/_marathon_plan.py`) and reporting (`utils/hq/marathon-scan.sh`). What *does* match is the micro level: nodes with LLM bodies, a genuine LLM-selected edge (`relay_drive.py:278`, reviewer `STATUS:` → terminal or another round), gates that must be able to start before turn 1, and an inspectable state machine. Graph-shaped inside a phase, deliberately not between them — `swarm-preflight.sh:28-29` / GUIDING-PRINCIPLES §8 hand scheduling to the operator. Names the shared root of three open issues: **#354** (parallel stages; its own Phase 0 found the lock excludes marathon↔marathon but silently not marathon↔relay or relay↔relay), **#359** (wave grouping asserted in prose, unverifiable — sharper once the waves never execute), **#391** (the chain is hand-transcribed, so the graph is authored twice and only one copy runs), plus **#396**'s conflict-as-signal restated: disagreement escalates on a *count* rather than routing on substance. Ships the README FAQ; changes nothing in the model; makes "should XYZ execute a DAG?" an explicit decision downstream of #354's Phase 4 gate. cx/risk/eff 2/1/1 (provisional). → [GH-435-COORDINATION-MODEL.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-435-COORDINATION-MODEL.md) · [#435](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/435)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md:120:- **GH-396 · Accuracy Ledger — design constraints to settle before build** 🆕 **captured 2026-08-01** — four constraints recorded before the Ledger exists, from a contributor thread on the Mythos cryptanalysis results whose framing (a model "routing around its constraints") did not survive reading the published run — Claude edited a harness it already had write access to, which is strategy adaptation in-lane, not evasion. What is real: **(1) placement** — the Ledger lives outside every agent-writable path (#50's pillar 2 one level up), and since `rtl_enforce` deliberately skips gitignored files (`relay-turn-lib.sh:1011-1015`), a Ledger under `.tick/` would get *zero* containment — decide tracked-path-vs-close-the-gap up front; **(2) observed vs. declared writes** — `oracle-guard.sh` asserts `ALLOW_PATHS ∩ ORACLE_PATHS = ∅` from CSV lists and never observes what was written, the same declared-trust-vs-actual-execution class as #390, and **PR #393 does not close it** (resource caps only), though `rtl_enforce()` and `requires_test_delta()` are existing reuse candidates; **(3) external ground truth** — our only oracle is the pre-advance gate plus an opt-in `requires_test` that asserts a path merely *changed*, over a gate defaulting to the target's own `validate.sh` (GH-238), i.e. the workpiece — so the Ledger cannot be more trustworthy than its oracle and #390 is necessary but not sufficient; **(4) an untested premise** — per-advisor calibration assumes uncorrelated advisors, but `consult.sh:287` is `(codex agy gemini aider)` where `gemini` is a legacy alias for `AGY_BIN` (a default panel may be one binary twice), `claude` is a builder not an advisor, and `aider` is an OpenRouter harness — cheap divergence replay proposed, but **not** against `.tick/`, whose schema carries no verdict/status/finding field (`src/events.js:12-30`), so it runs on `relay-system/**` transcripts or waits on new emission. Also names one thing buildable now with no Ledger: relay disagreement escalates on a **count** (`relay_drive.py:439,620` → `cap-or-close-mismatch`) rather than on the substance of the dispute. Nothing implemented; the Ledger, reflection pipeline, and semantic-oracle wiring stay future-tense per the #40 post-close review. cx/risk/eff 3/2/3 (provisional). → [GH-396-ACCURACY-LEDGER.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-396-ACCURACY-LEDGER.md) · [#396](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/396)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-122-- **GH-343 · a target-relative gate program is checked against cwd/PATH instead of `target_root`, so a ready contract reports NOT-READY** ✅ **BUILT 2026-08-08 in the Litmus marathon — agy-approved, full gate passed (715s). Took THREE builds, and the first two failures were the PLAN's fault.** Acceptance criterion 3 ("a gate script **or** program that … is not executable sets NOT-READY, rather than passing readiness and failing at execution time") had a FALSE premise for the interpreter branch: `bash foo.sh` runs a mode-644 file fine. Two independent codex builds implemented it literally and both regressed `test/swarm-preflight.sh` **98/0 → 91/7** (T15/T33/T36). `chmod +x`-ing the fixtures would have shipped a NEW false NOT-READY for `gate: "bash validate.sh"` in any repo whose `validate.sh` is 644 — the lane shipping the bug it exists to fix. Criterion 3 was narrowed on the issue (operator-approved) to **directly-executed** programs only; the third build then produced the correct split — `isfile` alone on the interpreter branch, `isfile` + `X_OK` on the separator-containing program branch — first try. Same builder, same lane; only the criterion changed. **preflight READY, awaiting operator go** — the `bash`/`sh` branch joins the gate script onto `target_root`; the program branch calls `shutil.which()`, which for a separator-containing string tests it against the **process's** cwd. So the identical contract is `ready (exit 0)` from the target repo and `NOT-READY (exit 5)` from the harness clone, with the message blaming PATH. **A false NOT-READY silently drops an issue from a sweep** — `/10days` Step 6 treats any non-zero exit as a reason to drop, and exit 5 is indistinguishable from a real verdict. **Not a GH-308 regression:** the old exemption list never covered a target-relative interpreter, so it failed identically before. Criteria were **authored onto the issue** (it had none) and then **revised after a codex+agy review that found the original satisfiable by making the CORRECT branch wrong** — *"the two branches agree"* is met by resolving both against cwd. cx/risk/eff 2/1/2, 2 phases. → [GH-343-GATE-PROGRAM-TARGET-ROOT.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-343-GATE-PROGRAM-TARGET-ROOT.md) · [#343](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/343) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-124-- **GH-378 · a marathon can only run against a repo whose suite is already green** 🆕 **captured 2026-08-10 for release 0.3.0 Nightwatch, RE-SCOPED 2026-08-11 to release 0.6.0 Meter, doc drafted, NOT yet preflightable — its central design question is open** — `marathon.sh` takes ONE `--pre-advance-cmd` for a whole run, so the global gate is the full suite, and a marathon exists to work on repos whose suites are not green. Measured on rebalance-OS: all 9 lanes' own scoped gates pass, the full suite is red 5/1587, and the failures are unrelated to any lane. It bit this repo twice on 2026-08-10 — both Nightwatch waves halted an already-**Approved** phase on a red that had nothing to do with the lane. **The blocker is sharper than "parsing arbitrary gate output is hard":** `run_pre_advance_gate()` calls `subprocess.Popen(...)` with **no `stdout=`/`stderr=`** (`utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1352-1353`), so the driver retains **only an exit code** — there is no output for any baseline-allowance scheme to parse, and every option is gated behind a capture change first. The doc deliberately does **not** pick a design; it enumerates them and records the choice as the operator's. **Can never be a marathon lane** — it edits the live driver that would be gating its own change. cx/risk/eff TBD. → [GH-378-GATE-REQUIRES-GREEN-SUITE.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-378-GATE-REQUIRES-GREEN-SUITE.md) · [#378](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/378)

The divergence note lives in `marathon_drive.py`'s `route_agent`, NOT in the frozen Bash half, which was deliberately left untouched (twin guard 32/0). **Still open and NOT part of #414:** Pi as a REVIEWER is still rejected at `bin/marathon-yaml:95`, so there is still no fallback for a dead agy reviewer. cx/risk/eff 1/1/1. → [GH-414-PI-BUILDER-ROUTER.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-414-PI-BUILDER-ROUTER.md) · [#414](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/414) · [#451](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/451) · [#492](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/492)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-134-- **GH-387 · a builder turn killed at its wall-clock cap is committed and gated as if it completed** ✅ **BUILT 2026-08-11 as a direct PR — and the feared regression turned out not to exist** — a killed turn falls through to `rtl_enforce`, which commits (`relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh:1144`) and hands off the token, so `run_pre_advance_gate()` becomes **the first thing that ever executes work no human or reviewer inspected**. The tension that makes this hard, and that the issue never names: **committing a failed turn is GH-432's deliberate, already-shipped fix** — its title is literally "a failed builder turn skips `rtl_enforce` entirely, so its work is never committed and its token is never handed off", filed for a real outage of orphaned tokens and lost work. So "don't commit a killed turn" is not a fix, it is a revert. A second reason the naive fix falls short: `path_has_nonempty_phase_delta` (`utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1439`) accepts a newly-created **untracked** file as evidence of work, and the issue's own crash scenario is exactly that shape — suppressing the commit leaves the artifact behind anyway. The issue's severity is also dated: GH-390's guard shipped ~16h AFTER it was filed, so the described host takedown would very likely be killed today; the **structural** defect is untouched by that. **The fix is one deletion, and the reason it is safe is the finding:** the gate probe DECIDED NOTHING. Reading `recover_timeout_exit()` end to end, every branch is resolved by `artifacts_exist()`, `file_status()` and `token_state()` — the tick token records the builder's handoff directly, so the gate was only ever a proxy for a question the token already answers. Removing it preserves all five outcomes and every GH-205 recovery path. An earlier draft of this entry claimed GH-205 and GH-387 could not both hold; that was wrong and is corrected. What is actually given up is the `timeout-gate-failed` early exit — one wasted reviewer turn on work that was going to fail anyway, a fail-fast optimisation rather than a guarantee. **Verified:** all six GH-205 assertions pass unchanged (`test/marathon.sh` 33/0), GH-432 untouched, `test/gh387-gate-not-first-executor.sh` 9/0 with a gate that LOGS every invocation (the outcome alone cannot distinguish the fix — with a green gate the phase completes either way), and a pre-fix replay restoring the probe fails the pin 7/2. The frozen Bash twin still carries the old probe at `marathon-drive.sh:1208` — documented as a deliberate divergence, not taught the fix, since that needs a `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer. **Still open, sequenced second:** the untracked-partial leak. cx/risk/eff 4/5/4. → [GH-387-KILLED-TURN-GATED-AS-COMPLETE.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-387-KILLED-TURN-GATED-AS-COMPLETE.md) · [#387](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/387) · [#432](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/432) · [#390](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/390)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md:138:- **GH-492 · agy hangs headless with no CPU and no progress, and its only pre-flight warning fires on every turn** ✅ **BUILT 2026-08-10/11 — both surfaces done. Captured for release 0.3.0 Nightwatch — operationally urgent: agy is the reviewer half of the cross-model QA pipeline and it failed TWICE on 2026-08-10** — the 900s bound is **wall-clock only** (`utils/py/agy-turn.py:246` `subprocess.run(..., timeout=…)`); `TurnDiagnostics.classify()` runs post-hoc at `:301`, after `TimeoutExpired` already fired at `:247`, so nothing detects a process burning wall clock at zero CPU. The TTY warning is unconditional in headless mode (`utils/py/rtl.py:39-96` returns `"unverifiable"`, and headless always has `stdin=DEVNULL` at `agy-turn.py:22`), so the one available signal cannot distinguish a hang from three healthy runs. **The scope gap neither the issue nor the title names:** `utils/py/consult.py` — where the SECOND failure actually happened — has **zero** `TurnDiagnostics` (`agy-turn.py` has 2 references, `consult.py` has 0) and its own older 300s `CONSULT_TIMEOUT` (`:374`); implementing only in `agy-turn.py` leaves that surface exactly as blind. `consult.py` also lacks the empty-output guard `agy-turn.py:307-313` has — a distinct, unreported silent-success gap. Restored 2026-08-10 by an interactive `agy login`, itself the evidence: the failure was an expired auth session headless mode could not report as such. **This host has no GNU `timeout`/`gtimeout`**, so any fix assuming `timeout(1)` will not run here. **Built:** `TurnDiagnostics.idle_seconds()` measures forward from the last CPU growth or file write; `agy-turn.py` now bounds the turn by BOTH an idle threshold (`RELAY_TURN_IDLE_S`, default 300s, `0` disables) and the wall cap, killing the whole process group. The blocking `subprocess.run(timeout=)` became an explicit poll loop, because a blocking call cannot consult the sampler measuring it. `test/gh492-idle-kill.sh` 9/0 — and the **negative control is the point**: a slow-but-progressing turn measured 0.06s idle against the blocked turn's 4.09s. Proven falsifiable behaviourally, not just by a missing symbol: dropping worktree progress from the idle signal makes the control fail 2/9, which is exactly what a trigger-happy bound looks like. Criterion 3 was met WITHOUT touching the kernel — the every-turn `WARNING` is demoted to a one-line `NOTE` and re-raised in full only on the failure path, where an unverifiable auth probe is a live hypothesis rather than noise. Criterion 4 is satisfied by RECORDING the finding: no reliable headless agy probe exists and none is shipped, per GH-375's measured cost. **consult.py now covered too** — the surface where the SECOND 2026-08-10 failure actually happened. It needed a distinction a turn shim never does: a consult launches every advisor as a SIBLING under one parent inside ONE shared worktree, so measuring the parent sums all advisors and a fast codex answer masks a hung agy. `TurnDiagnostics` gained an explicit `root_pid` and now accepts a FILE as the progress signal, so each advisor is scoped to its own subtree and its own transcript. The test pins the masking BOTH ways — correctly scoped sees 2.99s idle, shared-parent scope sees 0.14s — so it cannot pass on a build where scoping does nothing. `CONSULT_IDLE_S` default 90s, `0` disables. Live consult re-run after the change: 1 answered, 0 failed, no false kill. 16/0. cx/risk/eff 4/4/4. → [GH-492-AGY-IDLE-HANG-DETECTION.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-492-AGY-IDLE-HANG-DETECTION.md) · [#492](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/492) · [#390](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/390) · [#414](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/414)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-140-- **GH-376 · relay-drive and marathon-drive take different locks from a linked worktree, so their mutual exclusion does not exist** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-08-11 (direct PR) — the fix was "adopt the resolver that already shipped", not "write one"** — both twins now call GH-448's shared resolver; `test/gh376-relay-drive-lock-parity.sh` 18/0 against a real `git worktree add`, with the pre-fix resolution replayed on BOTH lanes and observed sailing past a held lock, plus normal-clone and vendored controls and source guards pinning that the resolver is called rather than re-inlined. **Confirmed live, not only in fixture:** a marathon in a sibling clone (pid 39588) held the lock in this repo's common `.git/`, and post-fix `poll-relay` + `relay-escalation-not-stall` correctly refuse from a linked worktree (both 12/0 and 5/0 in a standalone clone) — the exact collision the issue describes, occurring by accident during its own fix. Consequence now documented: the suite can no longer run from a linked worktree while a driver holds the main clone's lock, which pre-fix it could *because* the worktree got its own private lock. Original capture below. — GH-448 (PR #449) shipped a proven 3-branch resolver, `driver_lock_path` (`utils/py/rtl.py:477`), plus a Bash twin; `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` imports and uses it (`:20`, `:611`) and **`utils/py/relay_drive.py` does not** — it still hand-rolls a 2-branch version at `:385-391` keyed on `os.path.isdir(root/.git)`, which is **false in a linked worktree** (there `.git` is a file), so the two drivers resolve different paths and neither excludes the other. GH-448's own doc explicitly scoped this out as "sibling issue #376". Also found: `rtl.py`'s docstring claims to match relay_drive's resolution too — currently false, a second stale comment in the same area. Traced why it only bites standalone: `marathon_drive.py:649` sets `RELAY_DRIVER_LOCKED=1` before invoking relay-drive, making it skip its own buggy acquisition — so the real collision is two independently-launched top-level drivers, not marathon's internal chaining. `relay-drive` is the per-turn subprocess the driver re-execs every turn, so the write-set is self-modifying in substance — **direct PR only.** Frozen-twin pair #8; Bash edits need a `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer. cx/risk/eff 2/3/2. → [GH-376-RELAY-DRIVE-LOCK-PATH-DIVERGENCE.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-376-RELAY-DRIVE-LOCK-PATH-DIVERGENCE.md) · [#376](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/376) · [#448](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/448)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md:162:- **GH-418 · swarm-preflight can pass a lane whose issue is closed and whose artifacts are frozen — it never checks either** ✅ **BUILT 2026-08-08 in the Litmus marathon — agy-approved, full gate passed (704s), and it grew a third phase from its own review.** Phases 1-2 add the issue-state and GH-308 FROZEN-banner checks preflight never had (`test/gh418-issue-state-frozen.sh`, 143 lines). **Phase 3 was operator-approved mid-run after agy found a PRE-EXISTING crash while reviewing Phase 1-2:** `expand_effective_artifacts`'s `read()` helper (`swarm_preflight.py:366`) did `open(..., "r")` + `except OSError:` only while walking all of `test/`, so ONE binary file there was an uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError` that killed preflight outright — reproduced with a single probe. The tell was the asymmetry: codex's own new `find_frozen_artifacts` already used `encoding="utf-8"` + `except (OSError, UnicodeError)`. Now hardened and pinned by a binary fixture asserting both exit 0 **and** the absence of `UnicodeDecodeError`, since an exit-code check alone would pass if the error were merely swallowed. **preflight READY, awaiting operator go** — the **designated first child of #419**. Preflight validates a contract's *internal consistency* (artifacts exist, probes still detect the bug, base is fresh) and never asks the two questions that decide whether the work should run: is the issue still open, and are the targets writable by policy. So a lane can read READY, emit a packet, and send a builder to edit a frozen Bash twin to close an issue that shipped two weeks ago. Measured on the 2026-08-03 four-plan triage: Plan J both lanes CLOSED, Plan K **16 of 17** CLOSED, 2026-07-23's #279 CLOSED, and Plan M targeting `relay-automation/consult.sh` — **FROZEN**, so following that plan's own gate would violate GH-308. None of it discoverable from preflight; it was re-derived by hand twice, weeks apart. Cheap now because #400 already added the `gh issue view` call — `state` is **one more field on a request that already happens**, and #400's `unknown`-never-blocks posture covers the offline case unchanged. **Collides with #368 by construction:** its frozen check would refuse that lane, whose only write target carries the banner — fire #368 first (recorded identically in both docs). cx/risk/eff 2/2/2, 2 phases. → [GH-418-PREFLIGHT-ISSUE-STATE-FROZEN.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-418-PREFLIGHT-ISSUE-STATE-FROZEN.md) · [#418](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/418) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-208-- **GH-312 · `xyz-sync update` destroys the target's live `relay-system/` and `.tick/` state** 🆕 (2026-07-27) - `update` re-vendors the whole `.xyz/` tree via an unconditional `rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR"` (`xyz-vendor.sh:281-282`) whose staged replacement is mirrored purely from `$HARNESS_ROOT` — so everything the *target* accumulated at runtime is deleted unread. Exits 0, prints success, no warning, no backup, no `--dry-run`, no preserve list anywhere in `xyz-vendor.sh` or `xyz-sync.sh`. **Deterministic — every time.** Three things make it worse than it reads: the destroyed paths are exactly what vendoring is *sold on* (`relay-xyz/SKILL.md`: a vendored install gives you your "own `.xyz/.relay-driver.lock`, `.tick/`, and worktrees"); `ensure_gitignore` makes `.xyz/` gitignored by construction, so nothing was ever hashed into a git object and there is no reflog/stash/`fsck` recovery; and a *closed* relay was the lucky case — the same command mid-review destroys an active thread and a claimed `tick` token, and the peer agent's turn simply vanishes. Docs actively mislead: `xyz-sync.sh`'s header frames updates as "pinned + manual, by design", i.e. deliberate, never destructive. **Real incident:** silently destroyed a completed 2-round Codex relay thread (both reviews, dispositions, closing block) + the full `.tick/` event log; survived only because the Codex CLI transcripts live in `$TMPDIR`, outside the harness. `xyz-sync list` showed **6 repos** vendored at the same stale commit — `update --all` would take them all out in one command. Requested fix: preserve `relay-system/`, `.tick/`, `.relay-driver.lock` into the stage before the swap (chosen over warn-or-refuse, both of which still depend on someone reading output at the right moment). Phase 0 carries the sharper open question — whether runtime state belongs under a disposable, gitignored `.xyz/` at all. Bug filed via /file-xyz-bug from `rebalance-OS` at harness `dff45d5`. **✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-27 (`4ec5928`)** — `materialize_vendor()` now carries target-owned state across the stage-then-swap. **The requested preserve list was incomplete:** auditing what `.xyz/` actually accumulates added the GH-75 telemetry trio (`XYZ.json`, `XYZ.json.lock/`, `XYZ.heartbeat.json`), which had identical exposure — not in `VENDOR_DIRS`, so never recreated by the stage — making the shipped list **six** paths, not three. Regression test `test/gh312-vendor-preserves-state.sh` was written first and observed **failing pre-fix (6 failures)**, passes 14/14 post-fix, and also pins that VERSION still restamps to live HEAD so a fix that "preserved" state by skipping the update cannot pass. Phase 0's open question about `xyz-vendor.sh vendor` over an existing `.xyz/` is **answered: same destructive path**, now covered. Reviewed by agy via a driven relay (Approved, 4 `[Pass]`, no defects raised — a clean but shallow signal). `validate.sh` green. **Still open, deliberately out of scope:** whether runtime state should live outside `.xyz/` entirely — needs its own issue. Issue [#312](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/312). -> [PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-212-- **GH-304 · Vendored `.xyz` relay lane is broken for Codex but works for agy** (2026-07-26) - second, independent reproduction of #304, captured via /file-xyz-bug from `rebalance-OS` at harness `e8cd951` (**newer than the original report's `efdb394c54ed` — not fixed at HEAD**). New finding beyond the existing diagnosis: the failure is **worker-dependent**. In one session, on the same vendored `.xyz/`, an agy review completed two full rounds and landed content while Codex failed 3× across both isolation modes — so the lane reports green to anyone who smoke-tests it with agy, which likely explains how a 100%-reproducible break in one of the two documented builders went unnoticed. Also refines the isolation-ON mechanism (Codex *can* read the pinned checkout; the **write** is rejected as "outside of the project" — seeding for read alone won't fix it) and corroborates the secondary false-negative `no tracked changes` message in a second repo with a gitignored `relay-system/`. Workaround confirmed: scaffold + drive from the live harness clone with `--embed`, at the cost of the per-repo driver lock vendoring exists to provide. GitHub's own PR↔issue linkage turned out to be **empty on every issue in this repo**, so "landed" is evidenced by a commit whose CONVENTIONAL SCOPE claims the issue (`type(GH-N):` / leading `GH-N`); a bare `#N` is the squash-merge PR number and is rejected. Reports `landed`/`mentioned`/`absent`, because the matcher under-reports (a fix inside a marathon commit claims no issue) and a silent binary would call that a clean "not done". `test/gh284-p4-release-lanes.sh` 33/0, mutation-tested. **P5-P6 scoped, not contracted.** Original capture: — after a marathon run completes successfully, open a non-merging PR (opt-in `--closeout-pr` flag) carrying deterministic notes built from the plan name/phase count/tick events, reusing `marathon-closeout.sh`'s existing PR-creation code behind a new `--open-only` flag. ./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md:451:- **GH-375 + GH-385 + GH-438 · three marathon-path checks that could not fail, or read the wrong state** ⚙️ **GH-375 and GH-385 COMPLETE; GH-438 PARTIAL — captured 2026-08-08, reworked from a superseded branch** — one release theme (#419) in three shapes. **#375**: the agy auth pre-flight decided on exit status alone, but `agy whoami` **exits 0** while failing to run when there is no TTY, and the probe passes `stdin=DEVNULL` — so the failing path is the *normal* path under automation and the guard could not fail in the one context it exists for; its captured output, the only place the failure was visible, was then deleted on the success branch. The verdict now lives once in `rtl.py` and both callers (`agy-turn.py`, `consult.py`) use it. **Matched on error PREFIXES, not a bare `"error"` substring** — a superseded attempt used the substring and would reject `terror-form-labs`, `org: error-budget-team`, `errors_last_24h: 0`; a false failure stops the run outright, which is worse than the bug. **#385**: `satisfied_lane_terminal()` read only the BASE token, so a phase that failed once, was re-run with `--retry` and completed on `-TURN-2` looked unfinished forever — observed rebuilding an Approved phase on a real 10-phase run, a full builder+reviewer cycle that **re-introduced work which had been reverted**; the driver now reads which task the relay was actually rendered for. **#438 PARTIAL**: a removal now counts as a phase delta (the existence test ran first and unconditionally, so a lane whose deliverable is *removing* a path could never register progress) — but **nothing re-evaluates `fix_probes` after the build**, which is the half that yields `Approved, gate passed` while nothing changed, so #438 needed a **Phase 2**, now IMPLEMENTED on `gh438-phase2-acceptance`: (post-build acceptance re-evaluation) is now specified in the doc with six open design decisions, tracked as a direct successor on #438 rather than a new issue: reuse `swarm_preflight.py`'s existing probe evaluator (`:151-170`) rather than growing a second one, re-derive the contract from the phase brief (packets are gitignored), no-probes must stay byte-identical to today, and a still-`unfixed` probe must escalate — advisory-only would reproduce the bug. Explicitly declined: the `--round-cap` 5→10 default bump (doubles fleet-wide cost, belongs to no issue here) and the frozen Bash twin edit (GH-308, no exception trailer). All three tests confirmed RED pre-fix on the discriminating assertion and registered in `validate.sh`; each carries a negative control, because the failure mode of all three fixes is a check that now always passes. cx/risk/eff 2/2/2, 2 phases (P1 shipped, P2 specified). → [GH-375-385-438-PREFLIGHT-TOKEN-DELTA.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-375-385-438-PREFLIGHT-TOKEN-DELTA.md) · [#375](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/375) · [#385](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/385) · [#438](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/438) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)

./docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-453-- **GH-442 · `/radar` — a per-repo strategic compass over the last 2-3 weeks** 🆕 **Phase 0 kill gate PASSED 2026-08-07; `skills/radar/SKILL.md` authored** — the repo reports volume and status but nothing reports **mix**; it can run marathons daily and still be 100% KTLO. Three lenses over a 21-day window: **flow distribution** (Run/Grow/Transform, with Transform *declared not inferred* — deliberately rejecting the usual `perf:`/`refactor:` → Transform mapping, since most refactors here are maintenance and auto-promoting them inflates the one number the exercise exists to keep honest); a **recurring-defect radar** that clusters repeat offenders into high-value fix targets; and **release recalibration** against `RELEASES.md`, advisory-only per its §GH-381 do-not-top-up rule. The Lens 2 signal already exists unread in the tree — [GH-440](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-440-VENDOR-TICK-GITIGNORE.md)'s `related:` block names #18/#314/#312 circling one function and records #18 as closed *doc-only, no code change*; the testable hypothesis is that doc-only closure of a code defect is this repo's strongest recurrence predictor. Persists a fixed-schema report to **two sinks holding different facts** — an immutable dated `RADAR-REPORT-*.md` owning the evidence, and one `radar`-labeled issue owning the live checklist — because the same facts in both is exactly the dual-source-of-truth defect §GH-381 names. Stable `RADAR-<seam-slug>` IDs make run N+1 carry unchecked items forward and report "open across N runs"; seam-slug fragility under renames is the flagged weak point. Per-repo only (no fleet roll-up, no rebalance integration), manual skill first, no enforcement; a `pdda.sh flow-distribution` graduation is named but gated on the taxonomy surviving hand-runs. **Phase 0 ran 2026-08-07 and passed by the strongest available route**: the top `related:`-block cluster is #419 (13 citations) — the cluster the Litmus release was already hand-derived from, i.e. the operator executed the radar's method manually before the radar existed. Two findings folded into the authored skill: a Harness bucket excluding machine-generated `relay:`/`marathon:` commits (165 of 438) from the RGT denominator, and class-shaped cluster IDs alongside seam-shaped. Remaining Phase 1: end-to-end runs on this repo + a low-structure vendored repo. Supersedes the `RGT.md` research capture (retained verbatim as Appendix A). cx/risk/eff 3/2/3 (provisional), 3 phases. → [GH-442-RADAR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-442-RADAR.md) · [#442](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/442)

./CHANGELOG.md-330-- **#129 — relay-drive misdiagnosed an unset `TICK_REPO_ROOT` and could report escalation as exit 0.** When the env is unset the driver now self-resolves it the way the turn shims root themselves (`resolve_turn_root`: CWD's git toplevel, else the harness root) and exports it, so the driver, `tick`, and the turn shim read one event log by construction in the vendored-`.xyz` layout. A token not found in the resolved log now prints the resolved root, the searched `.tick/events/` dir, and the `find-harness.sh --env` hint instead of the misleading "token missing"; every escalation path is pinned at exit 4 — never 0 — by test. The NOTE announcing self-resolution prints after the driver lock: a held lock must stay the first printable line, byte-identical to the frozen Bash twin (gh376's parity pin — the first full-gate run went red exactly on this ordering). The lane-attempt gate consumes the resolved root too (#136), so attempts and token live in one repo.
./CHANGELOG.md:331:- **#130 — an agy CLI without a `whoami` subcommand killed lanes as an auth failure.** `AGY_AUTH_USAGE_MARKERS` in `rtl.py` classify usage/CLI-syntax errors (`unexpected argument`, `unknown command`, …) as `unverifiable`, checked after the TTY markers and before the `error:` prefix (clap prints usage errors with that prefix). The non-zero probe exit routes its captured output through the same verdict on both callers (`agy-turn.py`, and `consult.py` per #135): usage errors proceed with a single NOTE; genuine credentials errors and silent non-zero exits still exit 5 with the `agy login` remedy.
./CHANGELOG.md-332-- **#131 — `--target-root` with a separate harness repo was a catch-22.** New `phase_commit_root()` routes the relay-file render and `ESCALATION.md` commits to the repo containing `phase_dir` — the TARGET under `--target-root` + a target `--phases-dir` (the layout relay-drive's containment advice prescribes), byte-identically `root` in every in-repo shape. The GH-514 write-set preflight probes each file against the repo that actually receives it. Transcripts deliberately stay with the harness root.
./CHANGELOG.md-333-- **#139 — GH-460's SIGPIPE shape swept out of the suite.** 369 of 482 pipe-into-`grep -q` assertions converted to the capture-then-match form (`grep -q PAT <<<"$(producer)"` — the substitution completes before grep starts, so no reader can vanish under a writer); the 113 unconvertible-by-mechanical-pass sites (function bodies, grouped conditions, lookalike prose) are inventoried in a baseline that may only shrink, enforced by the new `gh139-pipe-grep-guard.sh` suite, which fails on any new occurrence. Two live flakes during this work confirmed the class again (a first-line `git log | grep -q` match in the new gh131 suite; gh322 on a pristine clone).
./CHANGELOG.md:334:- **#140 — `datetime.utcnow()` deprecation warnings** no longer pollute captured driver output: the three sites (marathon transcript save, write-set probe, consult-verify archive day) now use timezone-aware `now(timezone.utc)` with byte-identical `strftime` output.
./CHANGELOG.md-335-- **#138 — the post-#129 Bash/Python twin divergence is pinned at the divergence site** (`relay_drive.py`'s post-lock block, the `marathon_drive.py` GH-414 style), so a `XYZ_PYTHON=0` run is not misread as a regression.
