./CHANGELOG.md-810-- **The "worktree isolation leaks an off-lane creation into the harness repo" defect is real, reproduces exactly as filed — and is not a worktree defect at all.** #426 named worktree teardown as the place to look, and explicitly warned against treating that as the answer: *"a builder that treats this as the answer will produce a fix shaped like the guess rather than like the defect."* A factorial control settled it in three runs — same fixture, one variable at a time: stub writes + isolation **ON** → leak; stub writes **nothing** + isolation ON → no leak; stub writes + isolation **OFF** → **leak**. The third case is fatal to the stated theory: the leak survives with isolation disabled, so teardown cannot be the mechanism. Logging every invocation of the agent binary showed the real one — there are **two per turn**, `agy whoami` (the GH-375 auth pre-flight) and then the turn itself, and **the pre-flight ran with the caller's CWD**, i.e. the harness clone, which is the one execution of the agent binary that happens entirely outside the turn's containment. The reproducing stub — like `test/gh410-containment-advisory.sh`'s — writes on *every* invocation, so the pre-flight invocation is what reached the harness root. The turn's own copy was always discarded, `worktree_end` always fired, and the worktree's `git-common-dir` always resolved to `AGY_TURN_ROOT`: **criterion 3 was already true and needed proof, not a change.** The fix is still worth making, for a different reason than the one filed — real `agy whoami` does not write to its CWD, but *"the binary we shell out to happens not to write"* is a claim about someone else's program rather than a property this harness enforces, and it is exactly the assumption that made a test stub indistinguishable from a containment failure. `agy_auth_preflight` now runs in a throwaway directory and **reports** anything the probe leaves there instead of discarding it silently. **`test/gh410-containment-advisory.sh`'s cleanup block is deleted, and its absence is the proof**: it used to `rm -f "$ROOT/offlane.md"` and print a NOTE, so a returning leak now makes that suite litter a live repo again rather than quietly tidying up after itself. `test/gh426-worktree-leak.sh` 7/0 — absence asserted in **both** repos in separate assertions (checking only the declared target is the miss this criterion exists for), exit 6 asserted **first** so a fix cannot buy containment by weakening the verdict, and criterion 3 read from the turn invocation's own `git-common-dir` *while the worktree still exists* (an earlier draft asserted it after teardown and reported "could not resolve", which is not a verdict). Controls: **2 red** here and **1 red** in gh410's new C4c against the pre-fix `agy-turn.py` (`test/baselines/GH-426-negative-control.md`). → [#426](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/426) · [#410](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/410) · [#375](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/375)
./CHANGELOG.md-811-- **The marathon orchestrator persisted nothing of its own, so the phase that dies was the one phase with no record — and building the fix found two more layers doing the same thing.** `marathon.sh` had no `tee`, no `exec >`, no log-file variable. What was durable got written **per phase, on completion**, which biases the archive toward success by construction: in the run that produced this issue, phases 1-4 each have a transcript and phase 5 — the one that panicked the host — has none. The only surviving account was a terminal stream the invoker had redirected to a path the platform clears at boot; after the reboot it was gone. That choice was theirs and a poor one, but the harness offered no alternative and gave no indication one was needed. **Where the run narrative goes is the harness's decision now**: a run log opens under the same transcript root the per-phase transcripts already use, is announced as `run log: <path>` at chain start, and is `tee`d as output is produced — armed after plan validation and before the first phase, so a usage error or an unparseable plan leaves no empty log implying a run happened (`--dry-run` is excluded for the same reason, and that exclusion is asserted). **Two further defects were found by the regression test rather than reasoned about, and both are the same bug one layer down.** (1) `marathon_drive.py`'s own narrative was **block-buffered** — Python block-buffers stdout when it is not a TTY, and a marathon is never a TTY, so this was not an edge case but *the* unattended path: the first kill-mid-run recovered a log holding the child turn-shim's output and none of the driver's, because subprocesses wrote straight to the fd while every `marathon-drive: …` line sat in a buffer SIGTERM discards. (2) **SIGTERM never reached the exit hooks at all** — the driver already ran them from a `finally`, but SIGTERM terminates CPython immediately; SIGINT raised `KeyboardInterrupt` and so already worked, and SIGTERM is what an unattended run actually receives. Now converted to `SystemExit(128+signum)`, the convention `_exit_meaning` and `marathon.sh`'s halt table already read. A phase killed mid-run leaves `PHASE-INTERRUPTED.md` carrying the phase id, the relay `STATUS:` read **at interruption**, the round count and the reason — asserted on *content* against a marker stamped after dispatch, because "writes a partial transcript" was satisfiable by an empty or pre-created file, a real hole the issue's own adversarial review caught. **SIGKILL and a host panic remain unreachable and the code says so** rather than implying coverage; that is why #384's recovery path is a separate lane. `test/gh388-run-log-durability.sh` 24/0 — Part C kills a running phase, Part D kills a running chain, because a green success path proves nothing on an issue defined by what is missing after a failure. Observed **9 red** pre-fix (`test/baselines/GH-388-negative-control.md`). → [#388](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/388) · [#382](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/382) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)
./CHANGELOG.md-812-- **`rtl_default_log` silently relocated turn transcripts into the one directory a reboot erases, and the assertion pinning that behaviour has been inverted rather than deleted.** On any resolver failure — a misconfigured `XYZ_ARCHIVE_ROOT`, an uncreatable directory — both lanes returned `${TMPDIR}/<tool>-<pid>.log` **with the diagnostic suppressed** (`quiet=True` in Python, `2>/dev/null` in Bash). The evidence was therefore already gone by the time anyone had a reason to look for it, and nothing in the run indicated a choice had been made at all. Both lanes now **refuse (exit 5) before the turn launches**, and the resolver's stderr is no longer swallowed, because *why* the root failed to resolve is the whole of the fix from the operator's side. The trade was reversed knowingly: refusing costs a turn that has not started, whereas the fallback cost the record of a turn that had. **Adding a warning while still writing to volatile storage was considered and rejected in the issue's review** — the logs would still be destroyed, and the message would only mean someone could have known. `test/relay-turn-trace.sh`'s case 3c asserted the old fallback verbatim and now asserts the refusal, with the reversal's rationale written in place rather than the old case quietly disappearing. **The non-durable locations are stated in ONE file read at runtime** — `relay-automation/non-durable-log-roots.conf`, consumed by `durable-log-lib.sh` (Bash, same shape as GH-448's `driver-lock-lib.sh`) and `rtl.py::non_durable_reason` (Python). Two hardcoded lists would have satisfied "stated in one place" on paper and drifted in practice, so the test asserts both readers agree on every probe path **and** that an invented entry changes the verdict — without that second assertion the conf could be decorative while the real list lived in the readers. **One honest scoping deviation, recorded on the capture doc:** the rule targets *relocation*, so a transcript inside the repo being driven is permitted even when that repo sits in `$TMPDIR`; applying the criterion literally refuses to run the harness inside every fixture in this suite, and a guard that cannot be exercised is not a guard. → [#388](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/388)
./CHANGELOG.md-813-- **`tick claim` announced its own failure and exited 0, and all three callers that could have read the announcement sent it to `/dev/null` — so the one command that knew the answer was silenced twice over.** At the per-agent cap (`MAX_ACTIVE_CLAIMS_PER_AGENT = 2`) `tick claim` printed `lost: claim limit reached (holding T-cite, T-offlane)` — the exact two tasks to release — and returned **0**. A caller doing the correct thing (`if ! tick claim …`) learned nothing, and the only remaining signal was stdout, which `rtl.claim_task_or_exit` and `marathon_drive`'s `_run_tick_loud` both discarded on *both* streams. **Both belts cut, so the turn failed with a message about the wrong thing**: `could not establish token ownership of TURN-2 (claimer=none) … inspect \`tick info TURN-2\`` — and `tick info` reports that token `status: open, handoff-to: agy`, perfectly healthy. The suggested diagnostic actively argued against the cause. On 2026-08-07 that cost roughly two hours of a live Litmus marathon. **Every `lost:` branch now exits 1** (cap, wrong owner, spent task), documented in `tick --help` alongside the existing 2/6/8 — and the idempotent re-claim by the holder, which `claim()` already reports as a *win*, still exits 0, which is the assertion that stops a naive "non-`won` is an error" fix from failing every healthy turn, since the shims all claim unconditionally on a token they may already hold. **The cap hit is now its own message** and names `tick reap <agent> --task <held>`; it mentions `tick info` only to say it will look healthy and is the wrong instrument, which is stronger than omitting it, because running it is exactly the operator's next reflex. The wrong-owner branch keeps the original wording, where `tick info` *is* right. **`_run_tick_loud` was a closure inside `main()`** whose name promised loudness while its body sent both streams to DEVNULL and then `sys.exit`ed on the result — the one path guaranteed to end the run was the one guaranteed to explain nothing; it is now module-level `run_tick_loud`, prints both streams on failure, stays silent on success (these fire four times per phase), and is directly testable for the first time. **The fix deliberately touches no `relay-automation/*-turn.sh`**: all five shims and `marathon-drive.sh` carry the GH-308 frozen banner, so `utils/py/` and `bin/tick` are the whole write-set. `test/gh408-tick-failure-visibility.sh` 22/0, observed **12 red** against the pre-fix sources with the full transcript in `test/baselines/GH-408-negative-control.md`. Criterion 6 (a resource failure still mislabelled `pre-advance-failed` when no gate ran) is **explicitly deferred to #407**, as that criterion's own wording allows — the mislabel remains, its cost does not. → [#408](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/408) · [#409](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/409) · [#407](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/407)
./CHANGELOG.md:814:- **A turn that died before its own cleanup kept its tick claim, and two of those wedged an agent permanently — self-inflicted, and it never cleared itself.** The claim is taken in `rtl.claim_task_or_exit`, several hundred lines before `rtl_enforce`, which is what normally releases or hands it off. GH-432 already fixed the neighbouring half — a failed *agent* now reaches enforce — but three paths exit **above** it and never consult the agent's result at all: worktree setup failing (`sys.exit(5)`), containment rejecting the turn (`sys.exit(6)`), and any exception escaping. The claim simply stayed held, and since the cap is 2, the **third** turn was refused for a reason two phases old. `claim_task_or_exit` now arms an `atexit` release, and the property that makes it safe is that it is **idempotent by construction**: it re-reads `tick info` and releases only if the task is *still* claimed by this agent, so after a normal turn — token already handed to the peer under GH-67, or done — it does nothing and cannot clobber the handoff a successful turn just made. A blanket release would; there is an explicit assertion for it. Deliberately a `release` and not a `reap` (this process is the legitimate owner cleaning up after itself, and the event log should say so), and deliberately **no auto-reap on a cap error** — silently stealing a claim trades a loud stall for a race against a genuinely busy agent, which is the issue's own non-goal. SIGKILL and host panics stay the watchdog's job; `atexit` cannot reach them, and the code says so rather than implying coverage. **`test/gh409-claim-leak.sh` fails every case TWICE before asserting**, because the cap is 2 and a single leak is invisible — a suite that fails one turn and then succeeds proves nothing, which is precisely the shape of the notes both prior sessions left on these issues. 8/0, observed **4 red** pre-fix; the recorded control (`test/baselines/GH-409-negative-control.md`) is worth reading as the incident itself, since case 2 leaks two claims and the later cases then fail at the cap without ever exercising their own paths — the cascade that wedged the live marathon. The suite reaps between cases so each is an independent measurement, and refuses to pass a case that did not reproduce rather than reporting a silent skip as green. → [#409](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/409) · [#432](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/432)

Its spine is **#419**, and the sessions since it was filed kept supplying evidence — #418 (preflight reads neither issue state nor FROZEN banners), #425 (the source-URL gate compares the issue number and ignores the repo slug, so an unrelated repo's same-numbered issue passes), #426 (containment exits 6 correctly and the file lands in the harness root anyway, while the obvious test checked the other repo and passed), #416 (three shipped guardrails deleted, CI red two days, read as noise), #375 (`agy whoami` exits 0 on a TTY error, so the probe cannot fail in the headless context it exists for), #344 (24 of 49 issues got an already-done verdict from same-numbered foreign documents), #368 (a `--check` documented as a `validate.sh` drift guard that `validate.sh` never runs). *Nightwatch* (15 issues, target 2026-10-10) is unattended durability against a real target repo: #384 (a crash leaves a clean tree containing ungated commits and nothing reports it), #387 (a turn killed at its wall-clock cap is committed and gated as if it completed), #383 (a hanging gate stalls an unattended run indefinitely), #382 (a kernel panic with no signal in the telemetry), #402 (the run commits to whatever branch the target happens to have checked out). **The ordering is the recommendation, not the calendar.** Nightwatch's fixes are verified by the instruments Litmus exists to make trustworthy; shipping durability first means measuring it with checks that have never been shown capable of reading anything but green — the #419 shape applied to a whole release. `Iterations:` bands reserve `0.2.0-0.2.4` and `0.3.0-0.3.4` per the admission rule, so patch releases inside an arc are recorded in this file only. So seven issues needed authorship, not ten. **47 criteria were written for #343, #344, #358, #375, #388, #390, #401**, leaning on each issue's own stated constraints rather than invented ones — #358's *"do not lower M from 16 or drop the distinctness check"*, #390's deferral of gate-in-container, the GH-308 frozen-twin boundaries on #343/#375. **The review was worth more than the drafting.** Codex returned REWRITE on five of seven, agy on two, and **both independently found the same blocker in #343**: *"the two branches agree"* is satisfied by changing the **correct** branch to match the broken one — a criterion whose plain reading permits making the defect worse. Codex alone found #390's: every kill-path criterion was satisfied by a guard that kills *every* gate, because nothing required a normal gate to still pass and advance. **Codex read the tree rather than the issue text, and five of its factual claims were verified before any were acted on** — all five held. ./CHANGELOG.md-970-- **GH-284 Phase 4: `utils/release-lanes.sh` closes the loop — a release becomes marathon input, and what landed is computed from git ancestry.** Two verbs on one script, both keyed on Phase 3's `Milestone:` join key. **`seed`** resolves a milestone (`--milestone`, else `--release NAME` matched against `Release:`/`Codename:`, else the single *in-progress* block carrying one — `Shipped` history excluded) and emits its open issues as JSON-lines with the same six keys and sort as `skills/10days/scan-issues.sh`, so release-driven selection is that pipeline with a different seed set rather than a new pipeline. A release with a blank `Milestone:` **exits 3**, never an empty list: an empty list is indistinguishable from a milestone with no open issues, which is the exact ambiguity the join key exists to remove. **`rollup`** classifies each issue against the derived trunk and prints `N/M landed`. **The obvious data source did not exist:** GitHub's `closedByPullRequestsReferences` is **empty on every issue probed in this repo** (#308, #319, #292, #274, #51, #261 — open and closed alike), because issues here are closed by hand; building on it would have reported `0/N landed` forever and looked like a fact. So evidence comes from the commit log, and three matchers were tested against issues of known state before one was chosen: *any `GH-N`/`#N` anywhere* is too loose (`#308` matched a commit that merely mentions it); *`GH-N` anywhere in the subject* is still too loose (`#308` matched `fix(RELEASES): correct the GH-308 release codename spelling`, `#284` matched `fix(GH-322): … port GH-284 Phase 2 …`); **`GH-N` as the commit's conventional scope** (`type(GH-N…):` or leading `GH-N`) rejects both and resolves every real implementing commit. A bare `#N` is deliberately **not** evidence — in a subject it is the squash-merge PR number, a different namespace, so it would land issue 326 off PR #326. **Three states, not two:** the matcher under-reports (#319/#320 were really fixed, inside a marathon commit whose subject claims no issue), so the report distinguishes `landed` / `mentioned` / `absent`, where `mentioned` means *"trunk activity exists but nothing claims to implement it"* — a flat binary would report those as a clean "not done" and be believed. **Trunk is derived and it matters:** `origin/HEAD` resolves to `origin/main` here, so Quicksilver is honestly **0/1 landed** on the release trunk and **1/1** on `origin/development` where work lands first; `--trunk REF` selects, and the report always names what it measured. Exit 4 for an empty milestone, because `gh` returns an empty list for an unknown milestone exactly as for an empty one and "nothing found" must not read as a successful selection. `RELEASES.md` is parsed directly rather than through `pdda.sh releases-current` — that is a human-facing report whose wording is free to change, and parsing a report to drive automation is how you get a silent break. Bash only, no Python twin: a new non-Tier-A script does not need a second copy to drift (#320/#322). New `test/gh284-p4-release-lanes.sh` **33/0**, registered in `validate.sh`, hermetic, using this repo's real false-positive subjects verbatim — and **mutation-tested**: loosening the matcher back to a subject-mention fails exactly the discriminating assertions (29/4), so the green run is not green by construction. Three defects were caught in this implementation by inspection rather than by any exit code: the rollup fed its issue JSON to a `python3` heredoc that already owned stdin (the same SC2259 collision that broke the P2 run log for a release), `fail()` used `"$*"` and printed its own exit code into the operator's message, and the empty-milestone path rendered `0/0 landed` *before* exiting 4. → [GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md) · [#284](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/284)
./CHANGELOG.md-971-- **GH-284 Phase 3: `RELEASES.md` gains `Milestone:`, the release → issue-set join key.** A release could not drive marathon selection because it had no way to resolve to a *set* of issues — `GH_URL:` holds exactly one link (Quicksilver → GH 308), which cannot express scope. The linkage now lives in **GitHub**, where it maintains itself as issues open and close, and the ledger carries only a milestone **title**. Deliberately *not* a hand-maintained issue list: `PROJECT/PDDA.md` records that this light ledger already replaced a heavier design with "linked marathons/issues, a GitHub release-tag cache" that was "too much data to keep current," and re-adding one would walk straight back into that. The zero-field alternative — repointing `GH_URL:` at the milestone — was rejected because it silently changes an existing field's meaning. `pdda_releases_list` parses `Milestone:` as a 7th `\037`-delimited field; `pdda.sh releases` warns when a block has a `Target Date`, isn't `Shipped`, and has no milestone (scoped to *dated* blocks so the example entry stays quiet; `Shipped` releases exempt, since backfilling history buys nothing; still never gates the exit code); `pdda.sh releases-current` prints the milestone and prints `(none — release cannot resolve to an issue set)` when absent, because a roll-up that silently omits the join key is the same quiet gap this program keeps finding. GitHub milestone **Quicksilver** created (#1, due 2026-08-01 matching the ledger) with #308 assigned; broader membership is a scoping call left to the operator. New `test/gh284-p3-release-milestone.sh` is the **first test the `releases` check has ever had**, so it pins the pre-existing behaviors (empty version → error, bad date → warn, overdue → warn, never gates) alongside the new field, plus a field-ordering case — appending to a `\037` record could silently hand `line_no` to `milestone` and every other assertion would still pass by accident. Observed **10 pass / 5 fail** against pre-Phase-3 code, **15 / 0** after. Phase 4 can now ask `gh issue list --milestone "Quicksilver" --state open` for a release's scope with no new cache and no new file format. → [GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md) · [#284](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/284)

./CHANGELOG.md:974:- **GH-347: `pi` was installed inside another application's private Node runtime — working, and invisible to every shell. The convention that would have prevented it did not exist, so it does now.** Surfaced while driving GH-336's round-4 review: `find-harness.sh --check` reported `pi` absent, yet `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.81.1` was installed and functional at `~/.hermes/node/lib/node_modules`. **The cause is ambient rather than a mistake anyone made twice.** `~/.hermes` is a separate agent application (own `SOUL.md`, `sessions/`, `memories/`, `state.db`, `.env`, `skills/`, `cron/`, `hooks/`) shipping a bundled Node runtime, and on 2026-06-03 it symlinked that runtime onto PATH (`~/.local/bin/npm -> ~/.hermes/node/bin/npm`). npm derives its global prefix from its own node install, so `npm config get prefix` returns `~/.hermes/node` — **with no `~/.npmrc` and no explicit prefix setting anywhere** — and a plain `npm install -g` deposits our tools into that app's folder silently, exit 0. The break completes because only `node`/`npm` were symlinked back out; nothing symlinks `pi`, and `~/.hermes/node/bin` is not itself on PATH. The two lanes that never had this problem show the correct shape: `~/.local/bin/agy` (real binary) and `~/.local/bin/codex -> ~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/bin/codex` (own app dir, own symlink). **Why it matters more than a papercut:** `~/.hermes/.install_method` reads `git` and the folder carries a 10.8 MB `hermes-setup` plus an `.update_check`, so a Hermes update that rebuilds `node/` deletes `pi` on that app's schedule — and the only signal would be `find-harness.sh --check` reporting `pi` not on PATH, which is *precisely what it reports today*. Wiped and never-installed are byte-identical to the observation layer: the same disease as GH-315 and GH-319, where the guard and the ground truth agree on the wrong answer. **A guidance audit found nothing wrong — it found nothing at all.** `relay-automation/README.md:29` names the package but not its location; `GH-295-PI-BUILDER-INTEGRATION.md` covers the config surface and containment posture but never where the binary belongs; `skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md` requires workers *on PATH* and ships `--check` for exactly that, which is the right check for a different question; `GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md` had no tool-install-path convention whatsoever. So the fix is a new convention, not a correction: **"Tool install paths — never inside another app's folder (GH-347)"** now sits under Conventions, carrying the rule, the invisible-failure mode, the `npm install -g` trap with an explicit instruction to run `npm config get prefix` **before** any global install, the positive pattern, and a deliberate scope note that this is a convention and a warning — **never a gate**, since where a working binary lives is the operator's call and a false positive that blocks a relay is worse than the papercut it prevents. **Blast radius is small, and that is load-bearing for the scoping:** `~/.hermes/node/lib/node_modules` holds only `@earendil-works/`, `corepack/`, and `npm/`, so `pi` is the *sole* misplaced third-party package — one isolated instance, not a systemic cleanup. Phase 2 (the convention) is landed here; **Phase 1 — actually relocating `pi` — remains open**, as does an optional warn-only detection phase in `find-harness.sh --check` that is explicitly droppable if it cannot be done cleanly. Deliberately out of scope: repointing Hermes's own `node`/`npm` symlinks or the machine's global npm prefix (that app's business, and riskier than the problem). → [GH-347-TOOL-INSTALL-PATHS.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-347-TOOL-INSTALL-PATHS.md) · [#347](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/347)

./CHANGELOG.md-977-- **GH-340: marathon-plan's Python path is now a native Python engine — the copied Node renderer is deleted and Node is no longer required to run it.** `utils/py/marathon_plan.py` used to `exec node utils/py/_marathon_plan_node.js` — a copy of the planner embedded in `utils/marathon-plan.sh` that GH-112 duplicated to preserve behavior quickly. That copy drifted (GH-154 found it missing the GH-48 zone model) and GH-255 papered over two more gaps by pre/post-processing *around* the copied program in `marathon_plan.py`: `_normalize_roadmap` mutated the ROADMAP input so the copy's older `docOf` would resolve the bash-correct doc (shim `S`), and `_inject_review_lanes` appended the GH-86 "Review lanes" overlay section after the copy rendered (shim `N`). Both were symptoms of the copy being a second, worse source of truth — the reason GH-308 carved marathon-plan out as the exception to the Python-authoritative policy. This ports the **canonical** engine (the one embedded in `utils/marathon-plan.sh`, which already has native `docOf(item, gh)` own-doc precedence and native `parseLanesTable`/review-lanes rendering) into a new `utils/py/_marathon_plan.py`, stdlib-only. The two shims are **folded into the native logic** — `doc_of()` implements the correct precedence directly (no ROADMAP input mutation) and the review-lanes overlay renders in place (no post-render patch) — and `_marathon_plan_node.js` is deleted. `marathon_plan.py` drops the `node --version` hard-require and the `QP_*` env plumbing; a production Python run now needs neither Node nor the JS file (verified by running the Python path with **no `node` on `PATH`**, exit 4, full report + JSON emitted). **The bet:** the native engine must be byte-identical to the Bash/node engine, since a superficially similar plan with changed scheduling or safety semantics is the real risk (issue's own reversibility note) — proven by fixture-level output comparison, not a smoke run. Against the live 160-item ROADMAP, `XYZ_PYTHON=0` (Bash/node) vs `XYZ_PYTHON=1` (native Python) are **byte-identical** across the text report, `--format json`, `--policy derisk-first`, `--require-gh`, and the full 285-line rendered doc; a synthetic corpus proves the two folded shims (docOf divergence + review-lanes overlay) match byte-for-byte too. JS→Python fidelity traps handled explicitly: `JSON.stringify` parity (`separators=(",",":")`, `ensure_ascii=False`, insertion-order keys), JS `String(number)` integer rendering, a ready-but-unrated lane's `null` score coercing to `0` in the sort (JS `a.score - b.score`), and `readdirSync`/`os.listdir` sharing OS order for coverage-drift finding order. `test/marathon-plan.sh` **60/0** (Scenario T's `XYZ_PYTHON=1` parity assertions included). **GH-308's marathon-plan exception is left as documented** — this does not flip authority: `utils/marathon-plan.sh` stays the authoritative, dual-maintained twin and the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` fallback is untouched (the rollback path). The frozen-twin guard still asserts marathon-plan is the Bash-authoritative exception (27/0). **Correction on merge review:** the citation of Scenario T as parity evidence does **not** hold — `run_qp()` never sets `XYZ_PYTHON` and `utils/marathon-plan.sh:6` defaults `${XYZ_PYTHON-1}` to `1`, so T compares the Python lane against itself. Mutating the Bash engine's rendered output at `utils/marathon-plan.sh:956` leaves the suite at **60/0** with both T assertions green. The port is still genuinely proven — the live-ROADMAP comparison sets `XYZ_PYTHON=0` explicitly and was independently reproduced at merge time (text × both policies × `--format json`, byte-identical once the clock is pinned; `timestamp` fields make an unpinned comparison differ on every line) — but *forward* drift protection for the one file GH-308 deliberately exempted does not exist. Filed as [#348](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/348). Also filed from the same review: [#349](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/349) — an unknown flag exits **0** on the default lane where Bash exits 2 (`marathon_plan.py:91-94`, `usage()` ends in `sys.exit(0)` so the following `die()` is unreachable; pre-existing, same class as #322), carrying the three now-stale `UPGRADE.md` references to the deleted `_marathon_plan_node.js`. → [GH-340-NATIVE-PYTHON-MARATHON-PLAN.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-340-NATIVE-PYTHON-MARATHON-PLAN.md) · [#340](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/340)
./CHANGELOG.md-978-- **Quicksilver's scope is now stated as what GH-308 actually commits to: "Python-authoritative Tier-A twins."** The ledger said *"Phase out Bash scripts,"* which the epic explicitly does not do — `GH-308-BASH-TWIN-RETIREMENT.md:19` (`non_goals`) rules out porting the 21 Bash-only scripts and `:263` puts `relay-turn-lib.sh` out of scope, and the shipped policy is **freeze, not delete**, with the Bash twins retained as the rollback path. A release description that promises removal it isn't doing makes the milestone unfalsifiable. `RELEASES.md:30` and the GitHub milestone description now both name the Tier-A twins and spell out the two non-goals. **Membership set to #308 + #342** (the last known Bash-only behavior, the `XYZ_DEBUG_LOG` Sentinel Tier-1 capture) — deliberately two issues rather than a wider sweep, so `release-lanes.sh rollup` reports a ratio that means something. It currently reports **0/2 landed on `origin/development`**: #308 `IN FLIGHT` (claimed by `f664dae` but the epic is still open) and #342 `ABSENT` (no trunk reference). #340/#341 is **not** in the milestone — it removed marathon-plan's Node dependency, but marathon-plan is GH-308's carve-out, so it advances the codebase without advancing this release's stated goal.

./CHANGELOG.md:980:- **GH-336: the planning-context proposal survived a three-round cross-model relay review and came out materially different — one Blocker was a source that does not exist, and the reversibility claim was prose.** Doc-only; no code shipped. Round 1 (**codex**, `--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`) returned *Changes requested* with 2 Blockers: the proposal claimed to consume an existing `utils/release-lanes.sh seed|rollup` foundation — **no such file exists anywhere in the tree**, and the cited companion issue GH-334 has neither a `PROJECT/**` doc nor a ROADMAP line — and Phase 2's "remains opt-in and must retain that escape hatch" was an aspiration with no mechanism behind it. The false premise was **deleted rather than replaced with a prerequisite build**: `RELEASES.md` already carries `Milestone:` as the release → issue-set join key (GH-284 Phase 3, above), so Phase 1 reads it directly and needs no release helper. **The architecture decision neither reviewer raised is the load-bearing one.** `AGENTS.md` names `utils/marathon-plan.sh` as GH-308's one *deliberate* dual-maintained exception, but auditing what that costs found it is **triple**-maintained: `utils/py/marathon_plan.py:10-21` states it delegates rendering to `utils/py/_marathon_plan_node.js`, a hand-maintained 46 KB **copy** of the Bash JS engine with **no sync mechanism**, already "drifted on two points," carrying two standing parity shims, and already repaired once by a dedicated parity marathon (GH-154). New logic in that render path would be maintained in three places, so the overlay is now specified as a standalone Python-only `utils/py/planning_context.py` that appends a section to an already-rendered plan — touching neither engine, needing no `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer, and leaving the untouched Bash lane as a **free permanent parity oracle for "feature off."** Rounds 2–3 (**agy**, independent QA per P12 separated grading, `GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md` as the stated tie-breaker) confirmed that architecture with citations and caught the revision's own worst defect: the Producer had defaulted the feature to `auto`, which still must *ask* whether a release resolves and whether `gh` is reachable and therefore puts an outward network reach on **every ordinary planning run** — the doc cited **P1** (*a coordination primitive that reaches out is a coordination primitive that can fail or leak*) to justify its `gh`-failure handling while defaulting to a mode that breaches it. Default is now **`off`**, and the kill-switch criterion asserts the **no-flag** invocation is byte-identical *and* issues zero `gh` calls, verified with a `gh` stub that fails loudly if invoked. Also landed: **four signals → three** (issue themes deferred out of Phase 1 on the *Relevant* pillar — no taxonomy exists and creating one is a standing non-goal, so clustering without one is low-confidence by construction); the stickiness closure table's *"no other tool may read the shape"* row became an **enforced CI grep** over `utils/` and `relay-automation/` rather than an assertion; the unauditable *"three real planning runs"* Phase 2 start condition became a **dated in-doc evidence table, empty by construction** (P9 doc-as-runtime-state, not a cache — a point agy explicitly checked against the doc's own non-goals); and every acceptance criterion was rewritten to name a runnable check, with `./validate.sh` / `pdda.sh run` **explicitly demoted to verification-only** so a phase can no longer pass on green gates that never exercised the new behavior. A doc-only **Phase 0** was added for the record-correction work. Net: `phases` 2 → 3, `risk` 3 → 2 on the strength of a structural rather than argued kill switch, and three operator questions reduced to **zero**. The last of them dissolved rather than being decided: Phase 0 had proposed deleting the live `Release: 0.1.0` EXAMPLE block on the grounds that release selection "would otherwise have to special-case" it — but the stated selection rule already skips any block with an empty `Milestone:`, which that block has, so **nothing in GH-336 needs it gone** and the item was removed. GH-336 stays read-only against `RELEASES.md`; the placeholder is genuinely expired (its own `Description` says to delete it "once real entries exist below," and `Quicksilver` now exists) but that is unrelated hygiene for a separate trivial doc fix. agy Approved at round 3/4 — **and a fourth round with a third model then proved that Approved was premature.** Driven with **pi + `qwen3.8-max-preview`** (direct Alibaba `qwen-token-plan` MaaS endpoint, the pairing GH-303 validated at 91 trials / 0 failures), charged specifically with finding what two models that had already agreed **both missed**: 5 `[Should]`, 2 `[Nit]`, 2 verified `[Pass]`, escalated at the round cap. It found **two factually false assertions in the Approved version**, both since verified independently at source. **(1)** The load-bearing kill-switch criterion claimed `off` mode "issues zero `gh` calls, asserted with a `gh` stub that fails loudly if invoked" — but the *base planner* shells out to `gh` in its ordinary render path, so a loud-fail stub fires on the base planner before the overlay is ever reached and the test fails in `off` mode for reasons unrelated to the feature. The criterion conflated "zero *overlay* `gh` calls" with "zero `gh` calls"; agy had `[Pass]`'d it. Fixtures now run under the hermetic `QP_GH_STATE_FILE` seam as a stated precondition, with the loud-fail stub scoped to the overlay's own `gh issue list --milestone`. **(2)** The operator-set churn threshold of "3 or more" was uncalibrated **by an order of magnitude**: measured over the trailing 14 days this repo shows **538 commits**, with `utils/py/` at **40** distinct commits and `relay-automation/` at **59** — so a ladder topping out at 8+ would park the primary code directories permanently at "consider bounded refactor," a signal that fires every run forever. Sharper still, `utils/py/`'s churn *is* the GH-308 Bash phase-out under the `Quicksilver` milestone, so an absolute rule would flag precisely the directed, release-aligned work the release-alignment signal already reports — **double-reporting known work as a discovery**. Replaced with a trailing-baseline ratio (window ÷ trailing-90-day median, laddered 2×/3×/5×), a 3-commit floor so 0→1 cannot spike, the baseline printed beside every signal, release-aware suppression labelling directed work as such, and the issue-linkage parse pinned to the **full commit message body** — round 4 showed the rung swings on that alone (subject-only gives 6 linked commits where whole-message gives 40+). Three further defects: `/10days` is a **prose skill with no executable**, so a criterion promising a "`/10days` dry-run … asserted with a stubbed `gh` state file" described a binary that does not exist (recast as an assertion about `skills/10days/SKILL.md` step ordering); that same hook made `skills/10days/SKILL.md` a **fourth file** absent from the three-file removal seam *and* outside the no-parser CI grep, which covered only `utils/` and `relay-automation/` (both widened); and the advisory **row format was undefined**, so two builders would have emitted incompatible output (pinned as `Claim | Kind | Source | Window`, with `Kind ∈ {fact, inference}` making the *Attested* pillar test-failable rather than stylistic). Round 4 also **confirmed the architecture rather than echoing it**, tracing evidence the earlier rounds asserted: the append seam genuinely existed, and the three-way byte-identical claims can all hold at once — verified through the real firing path, which closed the one risk flagged as unproven. Acting on its latent finding that `marathon_plan.py --check` re-renders with the default mode and `cmp`s against the committed doc (so a plan written under `auto`/`on` then checked under `off` reports **false drift**), the output moved to a **sidecar** `MARATHON-PLAN-<date>.context.md` that never touches the plan doc — which kills the drift hazard, makes "plan doc byte-identical in every mode" true *by construction* instead of by test, and sharpens the removal seam, all at once. **The architecture survived all four rounds unchanged; every defect was in the criteria that were supposed to prove the safety claims** — which is the reusable lesson here, and an argument for a third model over a second. Two out-of-scope pre-existing findings recorded rather than fixed: `marathon-plan.sh:54` documents `--check` as "a drift guard in `validate.sh`" that `validate.sh` never wires (why the drift hazard is latent, not active), and `relay-drive.sh:353-356` rejects a bold-backticked artifact path in a relay Setup line (hit live while scaffolding this review). `utils/pdda/pdda.sh run` green throughout. **Pi reported `cost.total: 0` for the round-4 turn — treat the spend as unmeasured, not free**, given GH-303's history of token-capture bugs in exactly this path. **Correction on rebase (2026-07-30): two of the findings above were true against `c6b98c2` and are no longer true on `development`, which advanced 6 commits during the review.** (i) `utils/release-lanes.sh` **exists** — #330 (GH-284 Phase 4) landed it with exactly the `seed`/`rollup` verbs the original draft claimed to consume, so round 1's Blocker was **premature rather than false**. Re-verified here: `test/gh284-p4-release-lanes.sh` **38/0**, and `release-lanes.sh rollup --milestone Quicksilver` runs live reporting `2/2 landed on origin/main` with per-issue evidence. The claim is restored and Phase 1 now **calls** the script instead of re-deriving release scope, which removes most of that signal's implementation. (ii) The "**triple**-maintained" argument for the standalone module is retired — #340 deleted the copied Node renderer (`utils/py/_marathon_plan_node.js`) and ported the engine natively to `utils/py/_marathon_plan.py`. The decision is unchanged but now rests on narrower, still-true ground: the planner remains **dual**-maintained (the JS engine embedded in `utils/marathon-plan.sh` plus the native Python engine) with **no forward drift guard** — a gap #340's own merge review found and filed as [#348](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/348). **The reusable lesson is the one this repo keeps re-learning:** every verification across four rounds was honestly derived and correctly cited against a tree that had moved. Re-check the base before trusting a long-running review's citations. **Deliberately still open:** no code has been written, so every criterion above is a claim about a build that has not happened — and `relay-drive.sh:353-356`'s Setup preflight was found to reject a `**`bold-backticked`**` artifact path (it strips `**` but leaves the backticks, failing a valid path as "not found in worktree"), which is unfiled. → [GH-336-PLANNING-CONTEXT.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-336-PLANNING-CONTEXT.md) · [#336](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/336)

./CHANGELOG.md-983-- **GH-349 + GH-346: marathon-plan accepted a typo'd flag as success, and stamped every generated plan with a hardcoded trunk.** Two front-door defects found while merge-reviewing #341, fixed together because they touch the same entry point. **(a) An unknown flag exited 0 on the lane that runs.** `utils/py/marathon_plan.py`'s `usage()` ended in an unconditional `sys.exit(0)`, which made the `die(f"unknown argument: {arg}")` on the very next line **unreachable** — so `utils/marathon-plan.sh --bogus` returned **0** on the default Python lane while the Bash twin returned 2. The practical bite is the drift gate: `utils/marathon-plan.sh --check --requre-gh || alert "plan drifted"` printed usage, compared nothing, and reported **success**. Same class as #322. Fixed by splitting printing from exiting — `print_usage()` prints and returns, `--help` calls it then exits 0, the unknown-argument branch calls it then `die()`s — which is exactly the Bash shape (`:102` prints only; `:139` is `usage; die "unknown argument: $1"`), so usage lands on stdout and the error on stderr on both lanes. **(b) `branch:` was the string literal `"main"`.** Reported against `rebalance-OS`, whose trunk is `development`, so every generated plan asserted a branch that exists but is not the trunk and is not where any lane would land — and of 41 docs in that repo's `PROJECT/2-WORKING`, only the two *generated* plans said `main`, so a reader had good reason to trust the field. **#346's own fix note was already stale when filed:** it said the Python lane had no `branch:` string of its own so fixing `:945` covered both, which was true only while `marathon_plan.py` shelled out to the copied JS — GH-340 (merged `1d06862`) replaced that with a native engine carrying its own `o.append("branch: main")` at `_marathon_plan.py:1151`. Both engines now derive it, and #348's newly-working parity gate is what makes "both" verifiable rather than hopeful. Deliberately the **trunk, not the current branch**: deriving `HEAD` would make `--check` report drift merely because someone cut a feature branch. Order is `QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCH` (override + hermetic test seam, since the suite's fixture roots are plain directories) → `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` with the prefix stripped (the same source `release-lanes.sh` uses) → `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` → `unknown`. The floor is `unknown` rather than `main` because PDDA does not require this key (`pdda.sh:39`) and no consumer was found — a wrong value is worse than an absent one, which is the whole complaint. New Scenarios **U** and **V** in `test/marathon-plan.sh`: **72 passed / 0 failed**, observed **65/7 against pre-fix sources**. The three pre-fix passes are each a thing that was already correct — usage already went to stdout, `--help` already exited 0, and the Bash lane already exited 2, that last being the entire premise of #349. V asserts neither engine still holds the literal, that a non-git root renders `branch: unknown`, that `QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCH` overrides on both lanes, and that **the whole rendered doc stays byte-identical across the two engines** — a derived value computed independently in two places is precisely the drift class #348 exists to catch. Checked by hand on the live 160-item ROADMAP too: both lanes emit the same 233-line doc. **Also corrected:** three `UPGRADE.md` spots (`:164`, the `:246` interpreter matrix, and `:251`'s "the 10 non-marathon-plan twins") still described `_marathon_plan_node.js`, which GH-340 deleted. Low severity — Node remains a baseline requirement via `bin/tick`, so the document's operative conclusion was never wrong — but two pointed at a path that no longer exists, and the carve-out had inverted: marathon-plan's Python lane is now the one entry point that does *not* need Node for its own work. → [GH-349-346-MARATHON-PLAN-CLEANUP.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-349-346-MARATHON-PLAN-CLEANUP.md) · [#349](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/349) · [#346](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/346)
./CHANGELOG.md-984-- **GH-348: the repo's only Bash↔Python parity assertion compared the Python lane to the Python lane, and so could not fail.** `test/marathon-plan.sh`'s `run_qp()` invoked `bash "$QP"` and never set `XYZ_PYTHON`, while `utils/marathon-plan.sh:6` reads `${XYZ_PYTHON-1}` — **default 1**. So Scenario T, labelled *"matches between shell and `XYZ_PYTHON=1`"*, compared Python against Python. Proven by mutation, not by argument: corrupting the Bash engine's rendered banner at `utils/marathon-plan.sh:956` left the file at **60 passed / 0 failed**, both T assertions green. **Why this one mattered more than a generic coverage gap:** `marathon-plan` is the *deliberate* exception to GH-308's Python-authoritative policy — `utils/marathon-plan.sh` stays dual-maintained — so cross-lane drift here is a live risk that has already materialised twice, in **GH-154** (the copy missing the GH-48 zone model) and **GH-255** (two further gaps papered over by pre/post-processing *around* the copied program). Scenario T was added by GH-154 to prevent the third instance and never could. Surfaced while merge-reviewing #341, which cited Scenario T as its parity evidence; the port itself was still genuinely proven, by a live-ROADMAP comparison that sets `XYZ_PYTHON=0` explicitly. Fixed with three things, not one: a new **`run_qp_sh()`** forcing `XYZ_PYTHON=0` for T's left side (the other 58 cases deliberately keep `run_qp` — unset is what production runs, so they are correctly exercising the live lane); a **loud counted `SKIP`** when `node` is absent, since the Bash engine hard-requires it at `:146` and falling back to `run_qp` there would restore the exact tautology while looking like a pass; and an **in-run mutation self-check** that renders with a mutated copy of the Bash engine and asserts the difference *is* detected, so a future refactor cannot quietly point both sides at one lane again — with a failure message that names both possible causes instead of guessing one. **61/0** on a clean tree, and the mutation that previously left 60/0 now yields **59 passed / 2 failed**, which is the acceptance criterion the issue set. The dry-run half of T still passes under that particular mutation, correctly: the banner appears only in the rendered doc, which is why the self-check compares the doc. On a no-node PATH: 57/1/**2 skipped**, the one failure (`F: json lines not all valid`) reproducing identically pre-fix and left alone — Node is a hard baseline requirement (UPGRADE.md §2), so a no-node run is not a supported configuration. **Third instance this week of one shape:** an assertion comparing a thing to a freshly-derived copy of itself — this, #342 (GH-281's test `sed`-extracted the helpers from the *Bash* file, passing for a year while the shipped lane had zero references), and #351 (the dashboard test regenerates the artifact it then validates). In all three the output reads as coverage and the gap is invisible from the pass line. → [GH-348-MARATHON-PLAN-PARITY-GATE.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-348-MARATHON-PLAN-PARITY-GATE.md) · [#348](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/348)
--
./CHANGELOG.md-1003-- **GH-296: `relay-drive.sh`/turn-shim EPERM on the tick lock in a same-repo vendored `.xyz/` install — root-caused as a regression via incomplete Python port, not a fresh instance of #263.** Captured via `/file-xyz-bug` from `pdda`; a Codex review turn driven against an artifact outside the vendored `.xyz/` failed to claim the tick token under both worktree-isolation settings. **#263's fix genuinely landed** in the Bash `relay-automation/codex-turn.sh` (commit `8c361a0`) — but this repo later flipped its default turn-shim runtime from Bash to Python (GH-264, `af7bb4d`), *after* #263 shipped, and `utils/py/codex-turn.py` — the file that actually executes by default now — never received the #263/GH-36 fix at all, and separately defaulted its own `root` variable to the harness's own directory (`XYZ_ROOT`) instead of falling back to the CWD's git toplevel the way the Bash version does. Confirmed via `git stash`/rerun: pre-fix, the new regression test reproduced the exact bogus `--add-dir <wrong>/.tick` sandbox path from the original bug report. Fixed: new `resolve_turn_root()` helper in `utils/py/rtl.py` (explicit override → CWD git toplevel → `XYZ_ROOT` fallback, mirroring Bash) used by `codex-turn.py`'s `root`; its `--add-dir` sandbox flag now builds off `tick_repo_root` unconditionally (both isolation states), porting #263's actual intent. **Follow-up folded into the same fix (not filed as a separate issue — same root cause, found while reviewing this one):** `agy-turn.py`/`claude-turn.py` shared the identical `root` defect, manifesting as their own pre-launch `tick claim --paths` call computing an escaping `../../../relay.md`-style path instead of a clean repo-relative one (the shared bridge into `relay-turn-lib.sh`'s worktree/containment logic already self-corrects a subdirectory root via the existing GH-160 fix, so this only bit the native, unbridged Python computation, `rtl.claim_paths_for_turn`). A second, independent bug surfaced while building the regression test for this: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns the *physical* path (macOS resolves `/var`/`/tmp` symlinks to `/private/var`/`/private/tmp`), which could mismatch a caller-supplied `relay_file` still in unresolved logical form — the same GH-51 physical/logical-path class of bug `relay-turn-lib.sh` already guards against on the bridged side, ported natively into `claim_paths_for_turn` via `os.path.realpath()` on both sides of the comparison. 5 new/extended regression cases across `test/{codex,agy,claude}-turn.sh` — each independently verified to **fail against the pre-fix code and pass post-fix** via a `git stash`/rerun/`stash pop` cycle, not just written and trusted. Also caught and fixed along the way: editing `test/*.sh` drifted the bundled `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz`, caught by `relay-pkg-freshness.sh` — rebuilt via `make-pkg.sh`. Full `validate.sh`: only the two long-standing, unrelated environmental reds remain (`acorn-extract.sh` missing the `acorn` npm module, `python:test_python_layer.py` missing `pytest`, neither installed in this local clone) — confirmed neither test file references any of the touched files. **Related, not verified:** the fix may also resolve the open #272 (same `TICK_REPO_ROOT`-in-vendored-lane root-cause family, a different symptom — a successful turn whose `tick release` lands in the wrong namespace) — flagged in the doc for a human to confirm separately. → [GH-296-RELAY-DRIVE-TICK-EPERM.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-296-RELAY-DRIVE-TICK-EPERM.md) · [#296](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/296) · [#263](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/263)
./CHANGELOG.md-1004-- **GH-279: two real in-repo gaps from the aider-qwen marathon trial fixed — zero-byte/unchanged artifacts no longer pass as builder progress, and the aider-turn API key no longer leaks into `ps` argv.** Closes out the GH-279/GH-280 marathon: re-grounded all 6 original punch-list items against the live repo before scoping (items 1/2 resolved via #280, item 3 tracked separately as #278, items 5 and 6b confirmed **not applicable** — no in-repo failure-tally/watchdog mechanism exists anywhere, and `timeout(1)` portability is already solved via `relay-turn-lib.sh`'s `rtl_run_bounded()`). Only two real gaps remained. **(4)** `artifacts_exist_for_timeout()` (`marathon-drive.sh`) / `artifacts_exist()` (`marathon_drive.py`) checked file existence only, so a killed/no-op builder turn's 0-byte pre-created stub passed as "artifact appeared" — fixed by generalizing the existing `requires_test_delta()` non-empty+git-delta pattern (`path_has_nonempty_phase_delta()`) to the artifact-appeared check too, in both runtimes, preserving `--requires-test`'s existing contract byte-for-byte. **(6a)** `aider-turn.sh`/`aider-turn.py`'s `AIDER_OPENAI_API_BASE` seam passed the API key as a literal `--openai-api-key` CLI argument, visible to any local `ps` call — fixed by passing it via the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable instead (which Aider/LiteLLM reads natively), dropping the CLI flag. Fired via `swarm-preflight → marathon-drive` (Codex builder, agy reviewer). **Process note:** the first turn implemented both fixes correctly and added solid regression coverage (verified: key absent from captured argv AND present in the subprocess env; zero-byte and unchanged-artifact cases both correctly classified as no-progress), but also made two off-allowlist edits — a `CHANGELOG.md` entry and a rewrite of an unrelated, concurrently-open `utils/swe-diagram/NEW.md` scratch file — both correctly caught and reverted by containment (exit 6). A re-fire collided with `--require-clean` against the operator's own live edits on that same scratch file, so this phase was closed out manually rather than risk a third automated invocation: the already-correct in-scope diff was reviewed directly, `test/aider-turn.sh` (63/63) and `test/marathon-drive.sh` (137/137) run standalone, and a full `validate.sh` pass confirmed only the pre-existing `acorn-extract.sh`/`python:test_python_layer.py` environmental reds plus one confirmed-flaky `relay-turn-timeout.sh` (9/9 clean standalone). **Agy's independent review did not run** (auth expired in this environment) — reviewed by the orchestrating session instead of a second model; disclosed here rather than silently treated as equivalent. → [GH-279-AIDER-QWEN-MARATHON-TRIAL-FINDINGS.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-279-AIDER-QWEN-MARATHON-TRIAL-FINDINGS.md) · [#279](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/279)

./CHANGELOG.md:1007:- **GH-280: Aider+Qwen reliability investigation concluded — root cause found and fix confirmed.** A live GH-268 Wave-1 exercise against the real production repo and the real `qwen3.8-max-preview` endpoint caught the first real failure transcript of the whole investigation: Aider auto-selects `whole` edit format for unlisted/custom model ids, but Qwen emits standard unified diffs regardless, which Aider silently discards as "no tracked changes" — the actual explanation for the historical ~86% aider-qwen failure rate, not general model unreliability. Re-running with `AIDER_FLAGS="--edit-format diff"` forced took the same task from 0/3 real edits to a 90%-complete, correct implementation landing in round 1, confirming the fix. Getting to this transcript required first closing a real observability gap: `aider-turn.sh` (and, since `XYZ_PYTHON` defaults on, the actually-executing `utils/py/aider-turn.py` and `utils/py/agy-turn.py`) were never using the GH-161 persistent-log helper, so every prior investigation round genuinely could not have captured a failure log — fixed in [#288](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/288)/[#290](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/290). Also found and fixed along the way, independent of Qwen: a fully-retired OpenRouter default model id (`openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`) that silently broke any plain `aider`/`consult` call omitting both `AIDER_MODEL` and `AIDER_OPENAI_API_BASE` — [#291](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/291), no separate issue filed. **Recommendation:** codex+agy remains the default builder pairing; Aider+Qwen is usable as a fallback with `--edit-format diff` and a generous timeout set explicitly. A separate, genuinely new gap was surfaced by the same session and filed on its own: `swarm-preflight.sh`'s suggested marathon invocations never default to `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=1` — [#294](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/294) (filed, not yet fired). → [GH-280 findings](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-280-AIDER-QWEN-VS-SONNET-INVESTIGATION.md) · [marathon plan](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-2026-07-23-GH279-GH280-AIDER-QWEN-FOLLOWUP.md) · [#280](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/280)

./CHANGELOG.md-1031-- **GH-255: `agy-turn.py` no longer fails open on an isolation breach — the GH-178 B1 grounding check was never ported, so Python silently accepted what Bash fails (exit 5).** Found by the first complete `XYZ_PYTHON=1` suite run. `relay-automation/agy-turn.sh:238-249` scans the agy transcript after `rtl_worktree_end` and fails the turn if it cites the **real repo root** instead of the throwaway worktree — an agent that escaped isolation. `utils/py/agy-turn.py` implemented the off-lane-edit half (exit 6) but omitted the grounding scan entirely, so `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=1` was enforcing materially less under Python than under Bash. **Diagnosis rested on a differential, not a guess:** the two GH-183/GH-187 *false-positive* guard cases (tick-command narration, markdown `file://` citations) were already **passing** under Python while only the genuine-breach case failed — the signature of a check that is *absent* (negatives pass trivially) rather than mis-tuned. Falsified the alternative that the scan lived in `rtl.py` or elsewhere in `utils/py/` before porting: zero matches anywhere. Ported the block verbatim, preserving all four false-positive filters (`[trace] ` prefix, `TICK_REPO_ROOT=`, `file://`, `](`) and the transcript `[FAIL]` breadcrumb append. **Breadcrumb worth recording:** `agy-turn.sh` is the *only* turn shim carrying this check — `codex/claude/aider` have no equivalent in either language — so their green Python tests were consistent with the finding rather than contradicting it. Verified: `test/agy-turn.sh` green in **both** modes (the breach case now exits 5, both false-positive guards still pass, so the check is not over-firing), and the full `XYZ_PYTHON=1` suite moves 104/116 → 105/116 with no new failures. Bash unchanged. → [#255](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/255)

./CHANGELOG.md-1034-- **GH-258: `vendor-stack` skill — one-step XYZ harness + PDDA governance install into a target repo.** New `skills/vendor-stack/` (SKILL.md + `find-pdda.sh` + `install.sh`) orchestrates the two independent installers rather than reimplementing either: it vendors the XYZ harness into `<target>/.xyz/` via `relay-automation/xyz-vendor.sh`, then **asks** the operator whether to also install the PDDA doc-governance runtime and, if yes, runs the pdda clone's `install.sh` in observe mode. **Design fork the operator raised — prompt + PDDA path resolution live at the skill layer, not baked into `xyz-vendor.sh`:** that script is copied verbatim into every vendored `.xyz/` and runs headlessly from marathon/relay automation, so teaching it to find and run PDDA would ship dead cross-repo resolution logic to machines with no pdda clone and put an interactive prompt inside a must-stay-non-interactive script. Each tool keeps its own installer and its own per-user upgrade registry (`~/.config/xyz/registry.tsv`, `~/.config/pdda/registry.tsv`), so `xyz-sync check/update` and `pdda-sync status/push` carry updates forward independently — the skill just runs them in sequence. `find-pdda.sh` is a device-agnostic resolver mirroring `relay-xyz/find-harness.sh` (env override → harness sibling `<harness-parent>/pdda` → conventional `~/…/pdda` paths; no hardcoded machine path), and an unresolved pdda clone downgrades to XYZ-only with a note, never a hard error. **Verification:** `find-pdda.sh --check` resolves the pdda clone both via the harness-sibling rule and via `PDDA_REPO` override; `bash -n` clean on both scripts; XYZ was vendored into `hyper-pandas-python-stack` (`.xyz/` present, `bin/tick` runs, `.xyz/` gitignored, registry row written) as the original driving task. Retroactive intake: the skill was authored first, then issue #258 + the `1-INBOX` capture were filed to bring the work into PDDA compliance per the issue-first SOP. → [#258](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/258) · [GH-258-VENDOR-STACK-SKILL.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-258-VENDOR-STACK-SKILL.md)

./CHANGELOG.md-1036-- **GH-255: `TEST_SOFT_FAIL=1` — first complete `XYZ_PYTHON=1` run of `validate.sh`; 10 test files fail *only* under Python, where the tracked blocker list held one.** The suite had never run to completion in Python mode. Two layers of fail-fast were conflated: `validate.sh`'s top level was *already* not fail-fast (it collects `FAILED`), but `test/_setup.sh`'s `fail()` called `exit 1` on the first failed assertion — the exact mechanism that hid [#223](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/223) behind [#215](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/215). Added opt-in `TEST_SOFT_FAIL=1` (default-off; fail-fast byte-identical when unset). **Second, non-obvious half:** most tests end in a bare `exit 0` — correct under fail-fast, a *false green* under soft-fail — so the `_setup.sh` EXIT trap now re-asserts non-zero when `FAIL > 0`, preserving `$?` verbatim when the flag is unset. Verified all three paths: passing test → 0, flag-unset failing test → exit 1 with one FAIL line, flag-on → exit 1 with all of them. **A same-commit Bash baseline was run and subtracted**, without which pre-existing failures get misattributed to the port: baseline 114/116 (2 files, 9 assertions) vs. Python 104/116 (12 files, 62), at HEAD `607dd7c`. Three findings outrank the rest. (1) **`agy-turn.py` fails open on containment** — `genuine breach should exit 5, got 0`; Bash fails the turn, Python silently accepts. A safety regression, since containment is what stops the GH-177-class incidents. (2) **Bash and Python `marathon-drive` fail in *disjoint* sets** — Bash fails GH-171/GH-172 (vendored chain, exit 6), Python passes those and instead fails GH-207/GH-238/`--require-clean`-in-a-linked-worktree; neither is a superset, so "port the remaining fixes forward" is the wrong model and the **union** needs reconciling. (3) **Fixing one gap reliably unmasks the next** — GH-215 → GH-223 → now #235: `consult.sh` is still red *after* GH-223 shipped, with 7 assertions covering the whole untported provenance surface (`FIRSTHAND_COUNT`/`ECHOED_COUNT`, `t.PROMPT.txt`). Four failing files (`debug-mantra.sh`, `marathon.sh`, `relay-artifact-file.sh`, `relay-turn-trace.sh`) have no Python twin at all — they fail because they drive `marathon-drive.sh`/`relay-drive.sh`, so the blast radius exceeds `utils/py/`. **Process note, recorded because it nearly shipped bad data:** the first sweep ran against a local `development` 31 commits behind origin that predated the GH-223 fix, and its results were filed before the staleness was caught; the issue body was invalidated and re-measured at merged HEAD. A clean `git status` says nothing about whether the branch is *current*. **Side finding:** the local baseline does not reproduce [#170](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/170)'s 9 pre-existing failures or [#232](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/232)'s ~12 — only `marathon-drive.sh` and a stale `relay-pkg.tar.gz` — so both look stale or ubuntu-specific. Supersedes the cutover criterion in [GH-172-CUTOVER-RECOMMENDATION.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-172-CUTOVER-RECOMMENDATION.md), which assumed a single blocker; proposed replacement is *no Python-attributable failures against a same-commit Bash baseline*. No production code changed — test harness only. → [#255](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/255)

./CHANGELOG.md-1055-- **GH-241: `MARATHON.example.yaml` now states that phases run strictly one at a time and that `depends_on` is scalar-only — docs-only; the report's first claim was partially falsified before the fix was scoped.** First bug filed *through* the new `/file-xyz-bug` skill (from `rebalance-OS`, vendored `.xyz/`), and the first to exercise the "verify the report, don't apply it" gate. **Claim (1) as filed — "nothing signals sequential execution", evidenced by a 0-match grep — does not hold:** line 3 already read "runs … **in depends_on order**; the chain **HALTS** on the first phase that fails". The grep was a false negative, searching the literal `"in order"` against the string `"in depends_on order"`. The DX complaint survives in a narrower form, which is what got fixed: the line documented *ordering* but not *exclusivity*, and "in depends_on order" is precisely how a dependency-ordered **parallel** scheduler (`make -j`) describes itself — so the new text states execution is strictly one-at-a-time and that `depends_on` **constrains** ordering rather than **creating** it, since restating "runs in order" would not move a reader who read that line and still concluded concurrency. **Claim (2) reproduced exactly** against a local two-phase fixture: `depends_on: [p1]` → `depends_on unknown phase '[p1]'`, scalar parses fine; root cause is the hand-rolled YAML reader not implementing flow sequences, so `[p1]` survives as a literal scalar into the phase-id lookup (`bin/marathon-yaml:102-105`). The field table now marks the field scalar-and-single with the exact failure text, and the header recommends `--dry-run` as the standard pre-fire step. **Consistency finding the issue didn't call out:** `depends_on` (scalar, single) and `artifact` (comma-separated, multi) are adjacent rows of the same field table carrying two different multiplicity conventions — `artifact` documented its own, `depends_on` did not, leaving the reader to infer from the neighbour. **Deliberately NOT taken: suggested fix (3)**, a `^\[.*\]$` guard in `bin/marathon-yaml` — that is a code change plus a regression test, not doc-only, and stays open as defence-in-depth (the docs fix stops the author writing the list form; the guard would catch the one who writes it anyway). Verified no runtime change: `node bin/marathon-yaml relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` emits a byte-identical phase table before and after; `relay-pkg-freshness` 3/3 (the example is not a vendored path). → [#241](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/241)

./CHANGELOG.md:1059:- **`/file-xyz-bug` — cross-repo bug front-door into this repo's `PROJECT/1-INBOX/`, QA'd by an agy `/relay-xyz` review (Approved, r3).** Lets a Claude Code session standing in *any other repo* file a harness bug where it will actually be triaged: harvest-first intake (reconstructs the failing command, error text, and caller repo from the live transcript before asking the operator anything, capped at 3 questions), a redaction step, one preview → one confirmation, then `gh issue create` + a `GH-<n>-*.md` capture + a `ROADMAP.md` queue park. Ships `find-xyz.sh`, a device-agnostic locator with no hardcoded machine path (env override → skill's own real location via symlink resolution → relay-xyz's `find-harness.sh` → current repo); it **deliberately rejects a vendored `.xyz/` copy**, which `find-harness.sh` prefers — a vendored copy has no `PROJECT/1-INBOX`, so a report filed there is unreadable. Two guardrails carry real incident weight: it writes **nothing** into the caller's repo (no breadcrumbs, no cached absolute paths), and it **never commits or pushes** the capture, because this clone is shared with marathon/relay drivers that can leave it dirty or parked on a `marathon/*` branch. **agy review (`relay-system/2026-07-18/file-xyz-bug-qa.md`): 3 `[Blocker]` + 2 `[Should]` + 1 `[Nit]` → 5 implemented, 1 declined on evidence.** Best catch: `$XYZ_*` exports from the locator don't survive to the next Claude Code Bash call (CWD persists, shell state does not), so a later `gh issue create --repo "$XYZ_SLUG"` would have expanded empty at the one moment it mattered — fixed with an explicit callout plus scrubbing all four bare references. **Declined** agy's third Blocker (that `status: Proposed (1-INBOX — not yet active)` violates a `status: Proposed` enum) as incorrect: no such enum exists — `PROJECT/PDDA.md:230` prescribes that exact string as the minimum frontmatter for a `GH-` inbox capture, `PDDA.md:456` documents `status:` as "free-text, unvalidated by design", and `GH-226` carries the long form in-tree; applying it would have moved the doc *away* from the contract. agy verified the citation and **retracted the finding** in r3. Also fixed by smoke-testing rather than review: `install.sh` reported success when `ln -s` failed under the Bash sandbox (`~/.claude` is write-denied), leaving the skill uninstalled while claiming otherwise. Locator verified from a foreign repo, a spaces-in-path repo, a non-git dir, and a bogus `XYZ_REPO` override; slug regex verified across all six GitHub URL forms.
./CHANGELOG.md:1060:- **GH-235: Consult A4 provenance v0 — "prompt-trace classifier for cited claims" (FIRSTHAND vs ECHOED) shipped, built by a live Codex↔agy relay after a live Codex+agy consult picked the scope.** Closes the shipped A4 slice's structural blind spot: the binary `NO FIRSTHAND VERIFICATION CITED` check (`consult.sh:310-336` via `rtl_has_uncited_claim()`) can't tell a citation an advisor found firsthand from one it echoed out of the operator's prompt — both look "cited." **Scope decided by dogfooding Consult:** a parallel Codex+agy consult (`relay-system/2026-07-17/a4-scope-181325/`) on the fork "4-category taxonomy vs. 2-category v0" converged independently on **v0**, both citing Principle 7 + the reuse tie-breaker; Codex read the actual code with exact line-cites, agy reached the same call. **Built by dogfooding the relay:** Codex (Producer) implemented across `consult.sh` (persist `PROMPT_TEXT`-only to `$RUN_DIR/${LABEL}.PROMPT.txt`; wire per-advisor `${LABEL}.${model}.PROVENANCE.txt` sidecar + a single ECHOED warn line gated on `uncited==0 && echoed>0`) and `relay-turn-lib.sh` (new read-only `rtl_classify_cited_claims()` sibling to `rtl_has_uncited_claim()`, reusing `RTL_CLAIM_WORD_RE`/`RTL_CITATION_RE` verbatim and keeping `/\[Pass\]/` inline to dodge the macOS-awk `-v` unescape trap), plus 20 `test/consult.sh` assertions — worktree-isolated, file-scoped commit `bfbd357`, no push. agy (Reviewer) returned **VERDICT: Approved** with 5 `file:line`-cited `[Pass]` findings. The existing `NO FIRSTHAND VERIFICATION CITED` stamp is unchanged (no regression). Independently re-verified rather than trusting self-reports: diff read + `test/consult.sh` 62/62 + `bash validate.sh` 115/115. **Honest limitation retained in-code:** exact/whitespace-normalized substring matching false-FIRSTHANDs when an advisor reformats a prompt citation (prompt "consult.sh lines 117-126" vs. answer `consult.sh:117`) — v0 accepts this; the INFERENCE/UNSUPPORTED-ASSERTED split, reconciliation backstop, and false-consensus detection stay deferred. **Two dogfood findings surfaced by the consult itself:** (1) both consult transcripts tripped the shipped binary stamp — correct for agy (an uncited `[Pass]`), but a **false-positive** on Codex's heavily-cited answer (one claim-word line in its long streamed reasoning had no citation within 3 lines), real evidence the current check over-fires on long transcripts; (2) the consult prompt contained `consult.sh:117` while Codex answered `relay-automation/consult.sh:117` — a live instance of the exact format-drift the classifier can't catch. **Relay note:** agy's review turn exited 6 (containment) because it left a stray `*.tmp` scratch file, off-allowlist for a relay-file-only review — the shim correctly reverted it and declined to auto-commit; agy's surviving Approved review was committed by hand (`6158eed`). Proposal + capture: [GH-178-A4-PROVENANCE-TAXONOMY-PROPOSAL.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-178-A4-PROVENANCE-TAXONOMY-PROPOSAL.md), [GH-235-CONSULT-A4-PROVENANCE-V0.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-235-CONSULT-A4-PROVENANCE-V0.md). Coordinates with #226. → [#235](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/235)

./CHANGELOG.md-1103-- **[GH-198](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/198) Bug 1 — `rtl_enforce`'s "file-scoped" commit had no pathspec, so pre-existing staged content silently rode along into the relay's commit.** `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh`'s commit step staged each allowlisted path independently (`git add -A -- <path>`, tolerant of a non-matching entry) but then committed with a bare `git commit` — no trailing pathspec — which commits the ENTIRE staged index, not just what the turn just staged. Reproduced live twice (2026-07-10/11) driving `relay-drive.sh --target-root` against a repo with pre-existing staged WIP: it rode into the relay's auto-commit under a message that only named the relay file. Fixed by scoping the commit to the allowlist — but a naive `git commit -- "${RTL_ALLOW[@]}"` reintroduces the GH-29 class of bug (unlike `git add -A --`, `git commit --` is NOT per-path independent: one pathspec entry that matches nothing aborts the WHOLE commit), caught by `test/relay-target-root-newfile.sh` regressing during my own fix. Corrected: cross-check each allowlist entry against what's actually staged (`git diff --cached --name-only`) before including it in the commit pathspec, and treat an empty result (only pre-existing unrelated content was staged, the turn changed nothing) as the existing "no tracked changes" no-op rather than either an aborted commit or a commit-everything fallback. Kernel-path change (`relay-turn-lib.sh` is orchestrator-only per this repo's own zone model) — implemented directly, not via a headless marathon builder turn. New `test/relay-commit-pathspec.sh` (9/9): proves pre-existing staged content is excluded and remains staged/untouched, plus a control case confirming a real allowlisted artifact still commits normally. Full regression sweep across every test touching `rtl_enforce` (`archive-commit.sh`, `relay-self-sufficiency.sh`, `relay-concurrent-commit.sh`, `relay-turn-trace.sh`, `relay-dep-drift.sh`, `shim-worktree.sh`, `relay-turn-handoff.sh`, `relay-target-root-newfile.sh`) green. Rebuilt `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz`. Full `validate.sh` green except the pre-existing, tracked [#208](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/208) environment red. GH-198's Bug 2 (doc/UX gap around reviewing an uncommitted same-repo artifact) remains open.
