A local Gemma worker (via LM Studio) fuzzes Aider CLI-flag combinations against an OpenRouter/GLM-5.2 target for hours unattended while a frontier model supervises via `checkin.py`; the full cycle — run Aider, capture the error, document it, file it — is now chained end to end, verified with real subprocess execution (a stub failing `aider` + a stub `gh`), not just read: `run_variations.py` auto-invokes `compile_issue.py` when it stops (time limit/abort/safety cap), which files **one** GitHub issue titled `ATE - [test-name] yyyy-mm-dd` containing every finding from that run as a single severity-ranked checklist — no manual second step. A `/consult` with Codex + agy (agy's transcript flagged `FAIL` by the isolation-grounding guard for citing real-repo paths, but its findings still cross-checked cleanly) surfaced and fixed ~10 unattended-run robustness bugs beyond the three found solo: crash-on-malformed-LM-Studio-response, `compile_issue.py` `IndexError` on empty stderr, `AttributeError` on a JSON-`null` classification, stale `control.json` abort persisting into a fresh run, non-process-tree-safe subprocess timeouts (orphaned `aider` children), `UnicodeDecodeError` on non-UTF8 subprocess output, an `install.sh` self-deletion risk, and a `dict | None` (PEP 604) annotation that crashed every script outright on this machine's Python 3.9 — found only by actually executing the scripts, not `py_compile`. Confirmed via direct code trace + `grep` that the implementation is hardcoded to Aider specifically (binary name, `--edit-format`/`--map-tokens`/`--no-auto-commits` flags, the variation-grid schema, the classifier prompt's pipeline framing) despite the skill's generic description; generalizing it to other harnesses is deliberately deferred, not urgent — captured as [#191](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/191), parked in `ROADMAP.md`'s queue, and given a `ROUTER.md` routing hint.

./CHANGELOG.md-2355-### Part A Phase 3.5 — `--artifact`: marathon can now produce REAL code (not just relay conversations)
./CHANGELOG.md-2356-- **`marathon-drive.sh` gains `--artifact PATHS`** (comma-separated repo-relative files). When set, the driver exports `ALLOW_PATHS` to the turn-takers (a flag all three shims already honor) and renders the relay template with a real write surface: the builder is told to *create/edit the artifact*, the tick `claim --paths` declares `relay,artifact`, and the edit-scope line allows `RELAY.md + artifact` (reviewer still edits only the relay). Without `--artifact` the phase stays relay-only and `ALLOW_PATHS` is left unset — containment default unchanged. This is the piece that turns the loop-prover into a code-producer: the shared safety core (`relay-turn-lib.sh`) still reverts any edit outside the declared allowlist, so the builder gains exactly one bounded write surface and nothing more.

./skills/file-xyz-bug/SKILL.md:3:description: File a bug against the xyz-3-agents-swarm harness from ANY repo or session — lands a PDDA-compliant capture in that repo's PROJECT/1-INBOX/ (GH-<n>-*.md), files the tracking GitHub issue, and parks a one-line ROADMAP pointer, without touching the repo you are standing in. Use when the xyz harness misbehaves while you are working somewhere else — a relay/marathon driver fails, `tick` misbehaves, a turn shim exits wrong, a vendored `.xyz/` drifts, an xyz skill (relay-xyz, consult, hq, xyz) breaks — and you want it recorded where it will actually be triaged instead of lost in the current session. Trigger on /file-xyz-bug, "file an xyz bug", "report this to the swarm repo", "log this harness bug upstream", "send this bug to xyz". NOT for bugs in the repo you are currently working on (use that repo's own intake, e.g. /idea or /triage).

Three stale dashboards reached `development` on 2026-07-30 alone from three different authors (GH-342, #356, #350); it fires on essentially every ROADMAP-touching PR. Fixed by two rules: `--check` runs **first** against the **committed** artifact, and nothing writes `$ROOT` (write-mode goes through `ROADMAP_DASHBOARD_OUTPUT`, which the renderer already supported — no renderer change). **4 → 9 cases**, including a mutation proof (case 4 plants a canary and requires `--check` to reject it, since cases 1 and 3 are unfalsifiable alone) and a no-side-effect assertion. **Verified against the real commit, not a synthetic fixture:** replaying `719867f`, the old test scores **4 pass / 0 fail** on a genuinely stale dashboard while the new one scores **6 pass / 3 fail**. Two findings only visible by running it — the old test left `ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md` modified afterwards, and **case 9 (section counts) was already correct and still reported green**, because the regeneration ran first: the bug did not add a bad assertion, it *disabled a good one*. docs/ROADMAP-UPSTREAM-ARCHIVE.md-208-- **GH-312 · `xyz-sync update` destroys the target's live `relay-system/` and `.tick/` state** 🆕 (2026-07-27) - `update` re-vendors the whole `.xyz/` tree via an unconditional `rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR"` (`xyz-vendor.sh:281-282`) whose staged replacement is mirrored purely from `$HARNESS_ROOT` — so everything the *target* accumulated at runtime is deleted unread. Exits 0, prints success, no warning, no backup, no `--dry-run`, no preserve list anywhere in `xyz-vendor.sh` or `xyz-sync.sh`. **Deterministic — every time.** Three things make it worse than it reads: the destroyed paths are exactly what vendoring is *sold on* (`relay-xyz/SKILL.md`: a vendored install gives you your "own `.xyz/.relay-driver.lock`, `.tick/`, and worktrees"); `ensure_gitignore` makes `.xyz/` gitignored by construction, so nothing was ever hashed into a git object and there is no reflog/stash/`fsck` recovery; and a *closed* relay was the lucky case — the same command mid-review destroys an active thread and a claimed `tick` token, and the peer agent's turn simply vanishes. Docs actively mislead: `xyz-sync.sh`'s header frames updates as "pinned + manual, by design", i.e. deliberate, never destructive. **Real incident:** silently destroyed a completed 2-round Codex relay thread (both reviews, dispositions, closing block) + the full `.tick/` event log; survived only because the Codex CLI transcripts live in `$TMPDIR`, outside the harness. `xyz-sync list` showed **6 repos** vendored at the same stale commit — `update --all` would take them all out in one command. Requested fix: preserve `relay-system/`, `.tick/`, `.relay-driver.lock` into the stage before the swap (chosen over warn-or-refuse, both of which still depend on someone reading output at the right moment). Phase 0 carries the sharper open question — whether runtime state belongs under a disposable, gitignored `.xyz/` at all. CHANGELOG.md-859-- **GH-407: `pre-advance-failed` claimed a gate verdict for phases where the gate never ran.** Several unrelated failures reach the same relay exit 5 — a builder shim that failed to start, a builder that exhausted its turn cap, a reviewer turn discarded by containment — and every one of them was escalated with the label that means *the gate ran and rejected the change*. Observed three times in one 10-lane marathon on 2026-08-02, wrong all three times; in one case the relay file read `STATUS: Approved` while the phase was reported as though the gate had failed it. It costs real time because the reason is the operator's entry point: `pre-advance-failed` sends them to read a diff and test output that does not exist. Every escalation now records `gate: not-run|green|red` — **on every reason, not only the gate-related ones**, so the line resolves the ambiguity even where the reason taxonomy is incomplete — and exit 5 without a gate run escalates as `relay-failed-before-gate`. **Deliberately narrower than the issue asked:** it suggested three distinct reasons (builder-failed, cap-exhausted, reviewer-containment), and the driver has no channel telling it which cause occurred — #408 is that same missing channel from the other side — so a label that guessed would trade one confident wrong answer for another. `test/gh407-gate-ran-attribution.sh` **7/0**, including the assertion that protects the other direction: a gate that **did** run and failed is still `pre-advance-failed` with `gate: red`, because reserving the label is easy to over-apply and every other criterion would still pass while real gate failures stopped being reported as failures. Control: the pre-fix revision replayed inside the fixture reproduces the mislabel with no `gate:` line at all. → [#407](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/407)
CHANGELOG.md-860-- **GH-417: the tree asserted both that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` is the right ROOT default and that it is the bug "caught live" — the answer is a commit nobody had connected, and Marathon Plan K was two days early.** `utils/py/rtl.py:resolve_turn_root` defaults ROOT to `--show-toplevel` (GH-296); `relay-turn-lib.sh`'s GH-160 collapse carried a comment calling that construct the bug. Nothing reconciled them and no test could tell them apart, so the failure mode — exit 6, a legitimate in-allowlist edit reverted as a containment violation — could not be attributed to anything. **What actually resolved it: `312a2c3` (2026-07-21, GH-261), whose own commit message names `test/marathon-drive.sh`'s GH-171/GH-172 cases** — the exact failures Plan K measured on **2026-07-19** and explained by blaming `--show-toplevel`. GH-261 canonicalizes **both** `RTL_ROOT` and each absolute allowlist entry to physical form before stripping, so from that commit on either symlink form resolves. Both statements were true of different things: the GH-160 collapse runs *before* that normalization and must not change `RTL_ROOT`'s form, while `resolve_turn_root` runs after it. Both files now say so and point at each other; **the "caught live" sentence was kept, not deleted** — it is a real constraint on the GH-160 collapse, and only its scope was ever ambiguous. New `test/gh417-turn-root-symlink-prefix.sh`, **13/0**: a Python turn shim with `AGY_TURN_ROOT` **unset**, driven from a repo reached through a symlinked prefix, is not reverted. **The control is what makes it evidence** — reverting GH-261's canonicalization in a fixture copy brings exit 6 straight back with the original symptom in words (`OFF-ALLOWLIST change: relay.md — reverting`), and the *same reverted tree* passes when ROOT is pinned to the logical form, which is what identifies ROOT's symlink form as the axis rather than the fixture. Two traps sidestepped: the fixture builds its **own** `link -> phys` symlink instead of trusting `$TMPDIR` (macOS gives `/var -> /private/var` free, Linux CI does not, and a sandbox can hand back an already-physical `$TMPDIR` — the shape would vanish and every assertion would pass for the wrong reason, so the test asserts the shape first), and the **Python lane is proven** by a `python3` wrapper on `PATH` that records it ran, never certifying the frozen Bash twins as a proxy. **Comments only** in both files; the five GH-308-frozen Bash shims untouched. `marathon-drive` 144/0, `agy-turn` 62/0, `worktree-isolation` 33/0, `relay-target-root` 12/0. → [#417](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/417)
CHANGELOG.md-861-- **`swarm-preflight` crashed outright on any binary file under `test/` — found by agy mid-marathon, in code it was not asked to review.** `expand_effective_artifacts`'s inner `read()` helper (`utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:366`) did `open(..., "r")` with `except OSError:` only, while walking the entire `test/` tree to infer tests. One binary fixture there raised an uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError` and killed preflight before it could render any verdict — reproduced with a single probe file: `'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 3`, at `:1049 main → expand_effective_artifacts → :385 → :369`. **The tell was an asymmetry inside the same file:** codex's own new `find_frozen_artifacts` (`:631`), written two hundred lines away in the same turn, already used `encoding="utf-8"` + `except (OSError, UnicodeError)`; the pre-existing helper beside it did not. Now hardened and pinned by a binary fixture asserting both exit 0 **and** the absence of `UnicodeDecodeError` in the output — an exit-code assertion alone would pass if the error were merely swallowed. Weight: preflight is the tool that decides marathon-readiness, `/10days` Step 6 treats any non-zero exit as "drop this issue", and #343/#418/#425 are all about it returning *wrong* verdicts — a hard crash on a routine repo state outranks a wrong verdict. Folded into the gh418 lane by operator decision rather than deferred, because it is one line in a file already in that lane's write-set.
CHANGELOG.md-862-- **A reviewer had no sanctioned place to write, so proving a finding destroyed the turn that found it.** agy discovered the crash above and wrote `dummy.py` + `test/binary/` in-tree to demonstrate it — the same probe used to confirm it. Both are off-allowlist, so containment reverted them and failed the turn with exit 6 (correct per GH-410 case 3: a genuine off-lane *write* must still fail). The verdict survived only because `RELAY.md` happens to be on the reviewer's allowlist; written anywhere else it would have been lost, and the crash with it. **Containment is unchanged and not weakened** — instead the rendered reviewer prompt now carries instruction 4b: write probe files under `$TMPDIR`, never in the working tree, with the reason and this incident stated inline. Verified on the next two lanes: agy reviewed both with zero containment failures, and on `gh425` reported *"I executed `test/gh425-source-url-slug.sh` outside the test tree in an isolated `$TMPDIR` and all assertions passed"* — full verification, no violation. **Python lane only:** `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh` is a GH-308 frozen twin and is byte-unchanged (`gh308-frozen-twin-guard` 32/0, `marathon-drive` 142/0).
CHANGELOG.md:863:- **GH-397 — the reviewer's containment boundary was about to be moved onto an honor system the repo had already proven does not hold (#456, `ed937d8`).** `NEXT:` carries two incompatible value domains: `/relay` writes a ROLE (`Producer`/`Reviewer`), marathon-drive writes an AGENT ID, and the shared reader `rtl_is_reviewer_turn` understood only the former — so on every marathon reviewer turn it returned false and the reviewer kept the full `ALLOW_PATHS` allowlist over the artifact it was reviewing, which is the 2026-06-20 agy over-reach. The first fix asked the acting model, in prompt prose, to rewrite the header itself. **That was rejected in review on evidence already in the tree:** `test/agy-turn.sh` (S2) exists specifically to pin *"KNOWN GAP reproduced — NEXT was NOT flipped and nothing caught it"*, and the failure direction is OPEN — one forgotten flip silently restores artifact write authority. The role is now DERIVED from marathon-drive's machine-readable role directive plus `RELAY_AGENT`, which relay-drive exports from the **tick token** — two pieces of state no agent authors. Plain `/relay` threads, hand-run turns, and pre-directive relays fall through to the historical `NEXT:` test byte-for-byte; a `builder == reviewer` self-review lane carries no role signal and deliberately falls through rather than guessing. **Both lanes fixed by one change** — `utils/py/rtl.py` shells out to the same function and `relay-turn-lib.sh` is not a frozen twin, so the Bash fleet gets it too. `test/gh397-reviewer-turn-role.sh` (11 asserts) was confirmed RED against the pre-fix tree before being trusted green, on the case the whole design exists for: the reviewer stays scoped when the builder never flipped `NEXT:` at all.
CHANGELOG.md-864-- **GH-401 — `--dry-run` mutated the repo, and the audit written to catch exactly that class reported PASS the entire time (#456, `ed937d8`).** The relay write and `os.makedirs(phase_dir)` both now sit below the dry-run exit, so a dry run touches the filesystem not at all; the render is emitted to stdout between explicit fences instead, so the flag still shows its work. **The more useful half was the guard:** `test/marathon-root-audit.sh` is the GH-209 guard for *"every test invocation of the marathon driver is `MARATHON_ROOT`-scoped"*, and its scope was the two hardcoded filenames `marathon.sh` and `marathon-drive.sh` — `test/gh268-relay-cue-and-target-checks.sh` was out of its reach because of its FILENAME, not because it was safe. Widened to audit every test script, it immediately surfaced a **third** unscoped invocation nobody had reported, `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh:270`; coverage went 2 invocations → 40, all scoped. **Two existing tests had encoded the defect as the contract** and had to be corrected, not deleted: `marathon-drive.sh` case (1) asserted `[ -f phases/p1/RELAY.md ]` *after* a dry run — the suite would have failed if the bug were fixed — and `debug-mantra.sh` used the dry-run write as its render-inspection mechanism (a legitimate need: it must render without driving a phase or disturbing `.tick/attempts/<lane>`, the counter each of its cases hand-seeds), so it reads the fenced render from stdout instead. `test/gh401-dry-run-no-mutation.sh` carries a positive control so "nothing was written" cannot pass for the wrong reason, and aims at a throwaway `MARATHON_ROOT` so a future regression can never dirty the real repo just by running the suite — which is how the polluted file got committed in the first place. **The headline claim measured rather than asserted: `git status --porcelain` is now byte-identical before and after a full `validate.sh` run** (159 tests, exit 0; CI `tier1` pass).

CHANGELOG.md-883-- **Five more Litmus capture docs — #343, #358, #375, #388, #401 — all preflight READY, bringing the release to 12 gated lanes.** Each carries its issue's acceptance block verbatim (`match` at 6/7/7/7/5 criteria), a preflight contract whose probe polarity was verified against the tree, and a phase split. **#344 and #390 were deliberately excluded**: both have implementations in flight — #390's in PR #393, #344's root-resolution half already merged — and preparing them as fresh marathon lanes would queue a rebuild of existing work. **The pre-check was run first this time.** After #416 and #344 both turned out mostly-shipped, every one of these five was checked for an open PR, a branch, and a matching commit on `development` before a word was written; all five came back clean. That check costs a minute and is exactly what preflight cannot do, which is #418. **Each doc records what the codex+agy review changed about its criteria**, because the revision is often the most useful thing in it: #343's *"the two branches agree"* was satisfiable by making the **correct** branch wrong; #375's identity assertion named neither the field nor a valid response; #388's *"partial transcript"* was satisfiable by an empty pre-created file, and one of its criteria rested on a false premise about what the PDDA lint scans; #401's *"writes nothing into any git repository"* would have broken a legitimate existing test that renders into a caller-supplied fixture root. **#358 gained two criteria that came from reading the code rather than the issue** — every appender's exit status is discarded (`wait "$p" 2>/dev/null || true`, in two places), and two different lock bounds are in play, so a report naming "the timeout" is not actionable. **#401 is no longer a historical report:** its defect fired three times across these sessions, each needing a hand revert before unrelated work could be committed, and once nearly rode into a commit. Declared instead through the mechanism that already exists for it — a per-file `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer (GH-321) — and verified with CI's own invocation, which reports *"utils/marathon-plan.sh — covered by a declared Frozen-twin-exception"* and *"every frozen-twin edit in this range is accounted for."* No behaviour change; `utils/py/marathon_plan.py` never carried the claim. → [GH-368-MARATHON-PLAN-CHECK-CLAIM.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-368-MARATHON-PLAN-CHECK-CLAIM.md) · [#368](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/368) · [#419](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/419)

CHANGELOG.md-911-- **GH-416: the PDDA sync silently deleted three shipped guardrails, and CI stayed red on `development` for two days because the failures read as noise.** `cfd56b0` — *"land the upstream PDDA sync and close the two failures it arrived with"* — replaced the sync-managed `utils/pdda/**` tree wholesale. It closed two failures and left **three**, which were then carried as "pre-existing" by everyone who looked, including in PR #413's own body. They were not noise. Diffing across the commit: **(1)** GH-189's 3-COMPLETED stale-status scan — `non-terminal` went **4 occurrences → 0** in `pdda.sh` and existed nowhere else in the repo; **(2)** GH-189's entire **`roadmap-issue-state` subcommand**, **5 → 0**, so the test invoking it got `unknown command` and the file exited 2; **(3)** GH-284 Phase 3's missing-`Milestone:` warning — the release → issue-set join key `/10days` depends on — reduced to a bare `printf`; **(4)** the roll-up's explicit `Milestone: (none — release cannot resolve to an issue set)` line; **(5)** four broken path references introduced into `path-integrity`'s scan. Only (5) was cosmetic. **(2) and (4) were invisible until (1) and (3) were fixed**, because the test files fail-fast — the same broken-observation family as #315/#319/#351, where a failure that has been red a while stops being read as information at all. **The root cause is structural, not clerical:** local checks were living inside a tree that is replaced wholesale, and `pdda.sh` offers no extension seam (it sources only its own `pdda-lib.sh`), so every check this repo added upstream was on borrowed time. Fixed by moving them **out** of the sync surface into repo-owned `utils/pdda-local-checks.sh`, which sources only `pdda-lib.sh` and carries its own copy of the four private helpers that live in the un-sourceable CLI; findings are byte-identical and the functions were extracted mechanically from git rather than retyped. `test/pdda-local-checks.sh` guards them **falsifiably** — every check gets a fixture that must trip it *and* one that must not, plus a drift detector comparing the copied terminal-word list against upstream's, because an "exit 0" assertion would pass against a deleted check body, which is precisely the bug. Wired into `validate.sh` **and** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so they run against the real repository, which `pdda.sh run` used to do for them. `path-integrity` now skips `utils/pdda/**` with the reason recorded at the exemption: those tokens describe upstream's tree, and no edit here survives a sync. **Behaviour (4)'s INFO → WARN change is kept, not reverted** — upstream's reasoning (*"A check that could not run is NOT a check that passed"*) is better than what it replaced and is the same principle GH-400 applies to acceptance fidelity, so the stale test was updated to pin that the state is reported and never escalates to ERROR. Found while writing the fix: the `path-integrity` comment documenting the four broken paths **quoted them, and tripped the very check it documents** — they are now described rather than spelled out. `validate.sh` **0 failures**, the first fully green local suite since `cfd56b0`, and `tier1` green on PR #413. → [#416](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/416)
CHANGELOG.md-912-- **GH-399/GH-400: an agy QA relay found two real gate bypasses, and both were reproduced before being fixed.** Reviewed via `relay-xyz` with a review-only allowlist; 2 Blockers, 2 Shoulds, 1 Nit, all accepted. **(1)** An issue whose `## Acceptance` section *exists but lists nothing* returned `[]`, and the caller collapsed `[]` with `None` → `unknown` → **no block**, so a capture doc could invent arbitrary criteria under its own heading. `extract_acceptance_criteria`'s own docstring said the two cases must stay distinct *because collapsing them would let a doc dodge the gate*; the caller collapsed them anyway — the defect was in the gap between the documented intent and its one consumer. **(2)** Extraction stopped at the first **unindented** line, so an explanatory paragraph between criteria truncated the list — worse than reported, because `collect_inline_checklist` kept scanning: the two extractors **disagreed about the same document**, and the packet would inline three criteria while the fidelity check compared two. **(3)** `## Acceptance:` and `## Acceptance Criteria (draft)` read as "no section" → another silent `unknown` bypass; relaxed **more narrowly than proposed**, since dropping the `$` anchor outright would also match a prose heading like *"## Acceptance is not required here"* (pinned by a negative case). **(4)** The review correctly identified three cases that pass against the pre-fix code — they were exactly the 1 and the 2 that passed in the pre-fix runs. **Kept and labelled rather than deleted:** they are the cry-wolf controls, and a gate that flags faithful copies is precisely the failure that gets a gate switched off; each now names its falsifiable sibling. **(5)** An arrow inside a criterion broke `[changed]` parsing — **fixed differently than proposed**, because `rsplit` is also wrong: with three arrows neither the first nor the last is the separator, so the parser now offers every split as a candidate and reconciliation picks the one matching the actual diff. Suites 21 → **26/0** and **14/0**. **The review turn itself exited 6:** agy wrote `scratch-reviewer.md` off-allowlist and `rtl_check` reverted it — GH-22's backstop working — with the content recovered from `.tick/orphan-backups/`; another instance of the known agy-oversteps-allowlist pattern, on a turn whose `ALLOW_PATHS` was deliberately empty. → [thread](relay-system/2026-08-03/gh399-400-acceptance-qa.md)
CHANGELOG.md:913:- **GH-399: the packet's acceptance block kept only each criterion's first line, so every hard-wrapped requirement reached the builder as a half-sentence.** Second cut in the same chain as #400 — that one is the capture doc drifting from the issue, this is the packet drifting from the capture doc. Preflight matched only lines *beginning* a `- [ ]` bullet; capture docs hard-wrap at ~80 columns, so continuations were discarded **silently**, under a heading asserting the criteria were *"inlined from the capture doc."* **10 of 10 lanes** in one marathon lost 1–4 lines each. The issue's GH-201 evidence, now the test fixture: *"An explicit `--database` path that does not exist raises a clear error instead"* — the clause *"of silently resolving to the canonical DB"* never reached the builder, and the second criterion ended on an em dash, so what survived reads as an order to **preserve** the fallback the issue exists to remove. Because the reviewer grades against the same packet, there was no intact copy anywhere for either role to check. **Correction to the report:** it cites `utils/swarm-preflight.sh:882`; GH-308 **froze** that twin and it does not execute — the live defect was the identical regex in `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py`. **Fixed** with indent-gated continuation folding (reusing #400's extractor — ungated folding swallows a trailing `---` or the next paragraph, which is not theoretical: it produced a real false positive while dogfooding #400), extraction bounded to `## Acceptance` where one exists, an announced 25-item cap, and a lossless-copy check that re-parses the **rendered** block — deliberately not the structure that produced it, since comparing text to its own generator proves nothing — and sets NOT-READY rather than warning. `readiness.acceptance_inline` records scope, count, cap and losslessness for post-hoc audit. **One criterion was narrowed and the change declared** through #400's deviations mechanism, which is its first real use: bounding extraction *unconditionally* to `## Acceptance` — as the issue asks — would empty the acceptance block of **32 of this repo's 33 active capture docs**, which keep their checkboxes under `## Phase N`, deleting every lane's definition of done to close a leak the issue itself files as *"not yet observed."* **That declaration then exposed a hole in #400's own checker**, found by dogfooding: reconciliation only ran when the two lists differed, so a deviation declared against a still-verbatim list passed vacuously — a reader would believe a criterion was narrowed while the list said otherwise. Reconciliation now runs whenever the section exists (`test/gh400-acceptance-fidelity.sh` C8b, **21/0**). New `test/gh399-packet-acceptance-continuation.sh` **14/0** pins the whole chain — capture doc → `packet.md` → **relay file** — byte-for-byte at each hop, because asserting only the packet leaves the last hop, the one the builder actually reads, unproven; observed **2 pass / 12 fail** against pre-fix code. Writing that chain test cost one **orphaned `marathon_drive` holding `.git/relay-driver.lock` in the live repo** — the driver resolves ROOT to the harness clone unless `MARATHON_ROOT` is set, so the fixture run locked the real repository and hung — so the test now sets `MARATHON_ROOT` and runs under a hard 60s timeout, on the GH-369 principle that an unattended suite must fail on a hang rather than inherit it. → [GH-399-PACKET-ACCEPTANCE-CONTINUATION.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-399-PACKET-ACCEPTANCE-CONTINUATION.md) · [#399](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/399)
CHANGELOG.md-914-- **GH-400: `/10days` capture docs restated a GitHub issue's acceptance criteria instead of copying them, and preflight now refuses to emit a packet when the two have diverged without explanation.** Step 4 has a model summarise an issue into `PROJECT/2-WORKING/`, and everything downstream — preflight, the packet, the relay file, the builder, the reviewer — reads the **summary**; the issue text reaches none of them, so the summary silently becomes the contract and **no undamaged copy of the requirement exists anywhere in the pipeline**. **The measured case is an inversion, verified byte-for-byte against both source repos before any code was written:** `rebalance-OS` #202 requires a malformed row be *"proven to be either reconciled or surfaced, never silently dropped from the projection"*; the capture doc `/10days` wrote (commit `b941299`) instead requires asserting *"the exporter's actual current behavior (drop the row, continue processing the rest)"*; two criteria were dropped outright, including the one written specifically to prevent what shipped. The delivered artifact is **worse than the report claimed** — `3673257f` adds a test function literally named **`malformed_source_row_is_dropped`**, asserting `assert_not_contains "$out" 'truncated row'`, and a second independent run (`7525d047`) produced the same thing, because both were instructed to. Every gate was green, the reviewer approved, the phase closed; it surfaced only when a human read the issue and the test side by side weeks later. **Two corrections to the report, both load-bearing:** its suggested fix rests on *"preflight already fetches the issue for freshness checks"* — **it does not**, neither twin invokes `gh` in any form (freshness is `git fetch` + local probes), so this introduces the first issue-body fetch onto that path and has to carry its own offline contract; and companion #399 cites `utils/swarm-preflight.sh:882`, which GH-308 **froze** — the line that actually executes is `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:844`. **The fix is three parts.** (1) `skills/10days/SKILL.md` §4 now requires the `## Acceptance` block be reproduced byte-for-byte (re-wrapping allowed, nothing else), requires `source:` to carry the issue URL, and demotes the contract's `remediation.criteria` to an explicitly-labelled ranking summary rather than the definition of done. (2) `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py` re-fetches the issue and compares; unexplained divergence is **NOT-READY / exit 5 with no packet written**, and the packet now states in the builder's own context window whether its checklist was verified against the issue or merely inlined. (3) The only supported way to diverge is a machine-checked `## Acceptance — deviations from the issue` section (`- [dropped|changed|added] <text> — reason: <why>`) whose entries must reconcile the two lists **exactly** — an entry naming a criterion that is not actually different is rejected, so the section cannot become a rubber stamp, and there is deliberately **no env-var bypass**: a deviation belongs in the doc where the next reader finds it. **Undeterminable is not divergence** — no `gh`, unauthenticated, offline, or an issue with no acceptance section all report `unknown` loudly and never block, because an unreachable network is not evidence of drift. **Measured before choosing the posture rather than after:** all 33 `2-WORKING` docs carrying a `gh_issue` were compared against their live issues (33/33 fetches succeeded), **0** would newly read NOT-READY — 32 of the 33 issues have no `## Acceptance` section at all — so the hard fail the issue asked for costs nothing today. New `test/gh400-acceptance-fidelity.sh` (**20/0**, hermetic via a stubbed `gh`) pins the real GH-202 pair, and was **observed failing against the pre-fix code: 1 pass / 19 fail, with the inversion emitting `verdict: ready (exit 0)` and a written packet.** Cases 2–4 are the half that keeps it honest — a checker that flags the inversion but also flags a faithful copy is noise that gets switched off — and case 4 exists because **dogfooding this check against issue #400 itself caught a real false positive**: a GitHub body's trailing `---` and italic sign-off were being folded into the last criterion, so a byte-perfect copy reported as diverged. Continuation folding is indent-gated as a result, which also means the comparison sees the full text of a hard-wrapped criterion — the content #399 truncates at the packet-inlining site, deliberately left for #399 to fix rather than absorbed here. → [GH-400-CAPTURE-DOC-ACCEPTANCE-FIDELITY.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-400-CAPTURE-DOC-ACCEPTANCE-FIDELITY.md) · [#400](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/400) · [#399](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/399)

CHANGELOG.md-931-- **GH-370: the GH-336 plan doc cited an engine that no longer exists — including a no-`gh`-call test that could not fail.** PR #350's own body recorded this re-test as outstanding; this closes that gap. Rounds 1–4 verified every code citation against `utils/py/_marathon_plan_node.js`, which **#340 deleted**. Re-run against `origin/development@9082328` in a clean worktree: **7 of 8 findings hold**, one broke, and two new defects surfaced that the original review could not have caught. **The sharpest is defect 2, and it is live rather than stale:** the kill-switch criterion specified a `gh` stub "that fails loudly if invoked," which against this engine is *undetectable* — `_resolve_gh` runs the binary with `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` and folds any non-zero exit into `GH_MODE = "off"`, so the scream is discarded and the failure is indistinguishable from "`gh` not installed." Demonstrated rather than argued: a stub echoing to stderr and exiting 42 produced **zero** observable output, while a **file tripwire** in the same run recorded `gh auth status`. A fixture written as specified would have been green and worthless — this repo's recurring family (#315/#319/#348/#368/#369), *a signal that reads as protection while nothing is checked*, and the sixth instance logged. The criterion now mandates a file tripwire and states why an exit code carries no information. **The claim that broke** was round 4's proudest `[Pass]` — that the hook point was "real and already proven," citing `_inject_review_lanes`. #340 folded it into the engine (`_marathon_plan.py:1297`) and `marathon_plan.py` shrank ~390 → **212** lines with no post-render *mutation* step, so a builder following the note would hunt a deleted function; the seam is now named as the gap between `engine.run()` (`:170`) and the first mode branch (`--check` `:181`, `--dry-run` `:197`, write `:201`). **Codex caught three citation defects in my own corrections** on review (PR #371) and all three were right: `:181` was cited as though it opened all three branches when it opens only `--check`; the `_marathon_plan.py:450` link did not actually span the `stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` on `:451` or the `except` on `:452-453` that the claim rests on; and "no post-render step **at all**" was overstated — the wrapper still performs check/dry-run/write handling at `:181-205`, and the narrow true claim is that nothing rewrites the rendered bytes. Fixed in the same PR. Worth recording rather than smoothing over: this correction pass was itself imprecise in exactly the way it was written to catch. **Codex's second pass then found the sixth stale citation** — the out-of-scope bullet cited `marathon-plan.sh:54` for the `--check` drift-guard comment, but `:54` is a bare `#` and the claim is at **`:67`**. My citation audit missed it because it only walked markdown `(path#Lnnn)` links, and this one was written as a bare `` `file.sh:54` `` — **an audit whose scope didn't cover the shape the defect took**, which is the same family as the defects it was auditing for. The audit now walks bare `file:line` references too; all nine resolve in-range *and* content-match. Second pass verdict: 4 `[Pass]`, 1 `[Should]`, no pre-existing defects, and explicitly *"no remaining reference treats deleted `_marathon_plan_node.js` or `_inject_review_lanes` as live code."* Also corrected: `QP_GH_STATE_FILE` was offered as a usable env var when it is **internal to the Bash twin**, assigned from the real `QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE` at `marathon-plan.sh:179` — exporting it is a no-op on both lanes and silently runs a fixture live; two citations had drifted past end-of-file (`:378-391` against a 212-line file); and the `/10days` "no executable" claim was too strong now that the skill ships `find-doc.sh`/`install.sh`/`scan-issues.sh` (narrowed to *no plan-rendering entry point*, which is what the criterion actually needs). **Verified, not assumed:** all six surviving citations were checked in-range *and* content-matched by script; `QUEUE_PLAN_GH=off` and `QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE` each drive `gh` invocations to **0**; the fire list still renders 7 `**Wave N:**` lines ahead of the single `## How to fire a lane` anchor; churn re-measured at **528** commits/14d (`utils/py` 44, `relay-automation` 57) against round 4's 538/40/59 — same conclusion; `test/marathon-plan.sh` **72/0**. **The architecture is unchanged for the fifth time** — as with the three prior rewrites of its rationale, what needed fixing was the evidence and the test recipe, never the design. → [GH-336-PLANNING-CONTEXT.md](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-336-PLANNING-CONTEXT.md) · [#370](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/370)
CHANGELOG.md-932-- **GH-351: the registered dashboard gate rendered the artifact into the repo and then validated the copy it had just written.** `test/roadmap-dashboard.sh:27` ran the renderer — overwriting `$ROOT/ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md` — and `:34` then `--check`ed that file. The assertion could not fail, and its own pass string read *"--check passes on the committed artifact"*, which was false by the time it ran. **The renderer was never the defect and was not touched:** standalone `utils/roadmap-dashboard.sh --check` returned `rc=1` on all three of the day's stale dashboards, so the correct signal existed the whole time — the test overwrote its input before asking. A second, quieter fault: the test **wrote into `$ROOT`**, so `validate.sh` itself silently un-staled the dashboard mid-run, a suite repairing the evidence it was meant to judge and leaving the working tree dirty afterwards. Three stale dashboards reached `development` on 2026-07-30 alone from three different authors (GH-342, #356, #350); it fires on essentially every PR that edits `ROADMAP.md`, and the only reason it was ever caught was someone running the standalone checker by hand. Fixed with two rules whose case ordering is load-bearing: **`--check` runs first, against the committed artifact, before anything writes**, and nothing writes `$ROOT` — write-mode is exercised through `ROADMAP_DASHBOARD_OUTPUT`, which the renderer already supported, so no renderer change was needed. **4 → 9 cases**, adding a missing-artifact case, the source-drift direction that actually occurs in practice, a no-side-effect assertion, and — the one that keeps this honest — **a mutation proof**: cases 1 and 3 are unfalsifiable alone, so case 4 plants a canary line in a copy and requires `--check` to reject it. **Verified against the real commit rather than a synthetic fixture:** replaying `719867f` (the #350 merge, genuinely stale), the old test scores **4 pass / 0 fail** while the new one scores **6 pass / 3 fail**. Two things visible only by running it — the old test left `ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md` modified in the fixture afterwards, and **case 9 (section counts) was already correct in the old file and still reported green** because the regeneration ran first: the bug did not add a bad assertion, it *disabled a good one* (`roadmap=128 dashboard=127` is what it should have been saying). Sixth instance of *an assertion that compares a thing to a freshly-derived copy of itself*, after #348, #342, #362(B) and #369 — the last of which was in a test written earlier the same day. The recurring lesson is not "write more tests" but **run the new test against the old code**; every one of these was caught that way and none by review. → [GH-351-DASHBOARD-TEST-GRADES-ITS-OWN-ANSWER-KEY.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-351-DASHBOARD-TEST-GRADES-ITS-OWN-ANSWER-KEY.md) · [#351](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/351)
CHANGELOG.md:933:- **GH-369: `/10days`' capture-doc lookup spun forever on a valueless `--root`, and blamed a flag the caller never passed for a bad `$TENDAYS_ROOT`.** Found reviewing PR #364 before merge — #364's own fix is correct and shipped; these are defects in the argument parser it introduced. `find-doc.sh --root` with no value **looped indefinitely**: `shift 2` with one argument remaining shifts nothing and returns non-zero, and the script is deliberately `-e`-exempt (documented analysis-tool profile), so `$#` never decreased, `$1` stayed `--root`, and the branch re-ran forever. Confirmed under an `alarm(5)` wrapper — **rc=142/SIGALRM, no output**. That matters more than a usage nit because `/10days` is explicitly an *unattended* skill, so this stalls a sweep with no error, no output and no timeout: an absent signal, the same shape as #315/#319/#351 rather than a wrong answer. Second defect: a bad `$TENDAYS_ROOT` printed `--root not a directory:` — naming a flag never passed, with an **empty path**, because the message hardcoded `--root` and interpolated `$ROOT_ARG`. Now tracks which of the four sources (`--root`, `$TENDAYS_ROOT`, git toplevel, `$PWD`) supplied the value and reports that one. My first cut of that fix reproduced the same class of bug — it printed `$ROOT`, which the failed command substitution had already emptied — kept as `$ROOT_RAW` with a comment. New `test/gh369-find-doc-root-resolution.sh` (**14/0**) registered in `validate.sh`; the file previously had **no test at all** and was absent from `TESTS=()`, which is why both defects and GH-344 before them landed unchallenged. **Observed failing before the fix rather than merely passing after:** against `1612878` (post-#364, pre-fix) **12/2**, exactly cases 1 and 2, with the hang *reported as a failure instead of hanging the suite*; against `4dc27b4` (pre-#364, the GH-344 bug) **4/10**, case 6 catching it with *"answered GH-163 from the HARNESS tree"*. **Case 6 is itself a caught mistake worth recording:** as first written it probed issue 777, absent from both trees — so the harness-relative bug and correct behaviour both returned `null` and it passed against the very code it existed to catch. It now derives a real `GH-<N>` from the harness's own `PROJECT/` tree, which is what makes that pre-#364 failure detectable. A fifth member of this repo's recurring family: *an assertion that cannot distinguish the bug from the fix.* → [#369](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/369) · [#364](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/364)

CHANGELOG.md-987-- **GH-333: the run log's `driver still running` field could only ever say `running` — dropped, and the surviving exit code now says what it means.** The exit hook asked `driver_heartbeat_status()` *before* clearing the heartbeat, and the PID it tested belonged to the process doing the asking, which is alive by definition. The field was a constant wearing the clothes of a measurement — the exact shape this program keeps finding (#315, #319, #320, #322, #331). It was also in the wrong place: the comment is posted *at exit*, so it can never tell a reader whether a driver is alive now. The thing that answers that is the heartbeat **file**, which works and is untouched — this lane still writes and clears it, and the reader observers actually use (`rtl_driver_heartbeat_status`) lives in `relay-turn-lib.sh`, a shared runtime dependency rather than a frozen twin. Writer here, reader there, so removing the Python-side status function cost nothing. **Nothing was lost, because nothing was ever posted:** `--log-github` was Bash-only and inert on the default lane until #322's port landed the day before, and a scan of the likely lane issues found **zero** run-log comments in existence — so no reader breaks and no history is invalidated. The half worth keeping was folded into the neighbouring line, which was already carrying the useful signal as a bare number: `- driver exit: \`3\` (no-progress escalation)`. `_exit_meaning()` is at module scope, total (an unmapped code renders `unrecognised exit code` rather than an empty parenthetical that would read like a meaning), and maps 1/2/8 defensively even though lock contention, `die()` and the lane-attempt cap all exit before the run log arms and so can never appear in one. **Python only — the Bash twin keeps the old field, on purpose.** GH-308 froze the eleven Tier-A twins and AGENTS.md directs behavior fixes to the Python twin; editing `marathon-drive.sh` would have required a `Frozen-twin-exception:` trailer, which #321 just narrowed to per-file declarations and which exists for *safety* defects (the GH-319 precedent), not cosmetic ones. Divergence in a frozen fallback slated for deletion is the intended outcome of that policy, not a new parity defect. `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh` 26/0 → **29/0**, asserting the gloss, the field's **absence** (re-adding it fails), and that the heartbeat writer survived the removal. `test/gh308-frozen-twin-guard.sh --check` confirms no frozen twin was touched. → [#333](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/333)
CHANGELOG.md-988-- **GH-322 (the port): GH-284 Phase 2 shipped in July and had never once executed — *both* halves lived only in the Bash twin.** #324 stopped `--log-github` being silently discarded; this makes it do something. `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh` `exec`s `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` at its own **line 18**, while the `EXIT` trap that runs the run log and stops the heartbeat is installed at **line 244** — so under the default lane (`XYZ_PYTHON` unset since GH-264) the process was replaced before either could ever be wired up. Every marathon since Phase 2 merged ran, exited 0, reported success, and observed nothing. **#322's own scope statement was wrong, and the correction is the substantive finding here:** it deferred only the run log on the grounds that "the driver heartbeat *is* already in the Python twin (12 references)" — those 12 matches are `xyz_marathon_heartbeat_*`, the **GH-75 `XYZ.heartbeat.json` session record**, an unrelated file and feature; `grep -c driver_heartbeat utils/py/marathon_drive.py` returned **0**. Two different features named "heartbeat" in one file, told apart only by prefix, is what let a grep agree with the wrong conclusion. Both halves are now ported: the heartbeat (write, refresh thread, clear, `RTL_DRIVER_HEARTBEAT_FILE` honored) writes a record byte-compatible with `rtl_driver_heartbeat_write` — same six fields, same atomic `mkstemp`+`os.replace` — so the Bash reader and the Python writer agree; and `--log-github` is a real flag with `run_gate_result` tracking behind it. Exit handling mirrors the Bash trap's contract exactly (code resolved first, hooks in a `finally`, original code re-exited), so reporting can never change the driven run's result. `runlog_find_comment_id` sits at **module scope**: in Bash the same parser could only be reached through a `python3` subprocess, and the invocation shape itself (SC2259) silently broke it for a release — in-process kills the failure class, and importable means the test drives the real function instead of a copy of its logic. New `test/gh322-runlog-python-lane.sh` (**5 pass / 19 fail against pre-change code, 26 / 0 after**) is the counterpart to `test/gh284-runlog-heartbeat.sh`, every driver invocation in which is pinned to `XYZ_PYTHON=0` — which is exactly why that suite could not see any of this; the new file `unset XYZ_PYTHON`s deliberately. `test/gh322-unknown-arg-rejection.sh`'s `--log-github` block was **inverted**: "refuse loudly and name the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` workaround" was an interim contract, and a lane that still refused a flag it now implements would be the bug. **Deliberately left as-is:** the run log's `driver still running` field can only ever read `running` — the hook asks for status *before* clearing the heartbeat, and the PID it checks is the process asking. The Bash twin has the identical ordering (`:238` then `:239`), so it is inherited, not introduced, and porting it faithfully beats opening a silent twin divergence — the exact disease #320 and #322 are. → [GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-284-MARATHON-CLOSEOUT-PR.md) · [#322](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/322)
CHANGELOG.md-989-- **GH-320: the executing Python lane capped turns at a third of the documented budget.** An agy review turn died with `agy -p exceeded 300s wall-clock cap` on a shim whose header *and* code both read 900. XYZ has been Python-default since GH-264, so `relay-automation/agy-turn.sh` `exec`s `utils/py/agy-turn.py` — which defaulted to **300**. Same split in `codex-turn` (900↔300) and `claude-turn` (600↔300); `aider-turn` and `pi-turn` were consistent. Because Python is the lane that runs, 300 s was the **real** ceiling for three of five turn-takers while every operator-facing document said otherwise, and the failure surfaces as `exit 7` — *turn timeout / hang* — which reads as a hung model rather than a misconfigured ceiling. The natural response to that, retrying, burns another turn at the same wrong cap. **GH-308's freeze does not cover this class:** freezing the Bash twins stops them drifting *forward* and says nothing about values that had already diverged before the banners landed; nothing in the suite compared the two numbers. Fixed by aligning the three Python defaults with their twins. New `test/gh320-twin-timeout-parity.sh` reads the default out of **both** files for all five shims and compares them — **no expected value is hardcoded**, since a third copy of the number would just be a third thing to drift — and separately asserts that each Bash header's documented `(default: N)` matches that file's own code, because the header is what misled. 10 pass / 0 fail. **Deliberately still open:** nothing establishes the turn timeout was the only constant that diverged pre-freeze; a general Bash↔Python constant-parity sweep belongs to GH-308 Phase 2. → [GH-320-TWIN-TURN-TIMEOUT-DRIFT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-320-TWIN-TURN-TIMEOUT-DRIFT.md) · [#320](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/320)
CHANGELOG.md-990-- **GH-321: the frozen-twin escape hatch was range-scoped — one trailer excused every twin edit in the PR.** The `Frozen-twin-exception:` hatch shipped in PR #318 passed the guard for **every** frozen twin touched in `BASE..HEAD` as soon as *any* commit in the range carried the trailer — including files nobody reasoned about, in commits that declared nothing, possibly by a different author. CI then printed `1 commit(s) declare Frozen-twin-exception — allowing:` and listed the **declaring** commit, so the log read like a narrow reviewed exception while the undeclared edit was **never named**. The trailer's whole value is making an exception auditable, and range scoping broke exactly that property in the case where it counts. Marathon PRs are the common case and the worst shape for it: 4+ autonomous lanes on one branch make an undeclared twin edit riding behind someone else's declared exception the expected accident, not an exotic one. Same class as #319 and #315 — *a green signal that means less than it appears, with nothing in the output revealing the gap* — and it was disclosed at merge time rather than found later. A trailer must now **name the twin(s) it covers** (`Frozen-twin-exception: relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh — <reason>`), and every changed twin in the range must be named by some trailer; failures name the uncovered file. **The rule moved out of inline `ci.yml` shell and into the guard script as `--allow-exceptions`** — inline YAML is unreachable from the suite, which is part of why the looseness shipped at all; `ci.yml` is now a single call. Per-file *across the range*, deliberately not "the trailer must be on the same commit as the edit": a later fixup correcting an earlier commit is ordinary and should not need re-declaration, and what the looseness actually cost was attribution, which naming the file recovers. A typo'd path fails loudly rather than silently covering nothing; the bare path-less form no longer covers anything (that form *is* the looseness); reason text is not scanned for paths, so a reason may cite `validate.sh` without being read as a coverage claim; strict mode (what `validate.sh` and `--staged` use) is unchanged. `test/gh308-frozen-twin-guard.sh` **15/0 → 27/0**, with a fixture built on **two** frozen twins because with one the range-scoped and file-scoped rules are indistinguishable — which is how this shipped. One case **reproduces** the defect rather than only asserting its absence: it evaluates #318's exact predicate on the same fixture and asserts it *would* have allowed the PR, so the suite says so if the fixture ever stops exercising the bug. The single historical trailer (`07ae1e7`) is the bare form and would fail this rule; it is already merged and CI only judges an open PR's own range, so no existing history is re-evaluated. → [#321](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/321)
CHANGELOG.md:991:- **PR #318 agy review: two Blockers closed, one Should implemented differently, one declined.** The review of the marathon PR was itself driven through the harness (`--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`, exit 5 = changes requested). Both Blockers were re-verified against source before being acted on. **(1)** `AGENTS.md` asserted that "CI supplies `GH308_FROZEN_TWIN_BASE`" — `grep -rn GH308_FROZEN_TWIN_BASE .github/` returned **0 matches**, so the frozen-twin guard had no enforcement anywhere. Added the `Frozen Bash twin guard (GH-308)` step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, with a `Frozen-twin-exception: <reason>` commit trailer as the documented escape hatch so a legitimate exception is auditable in `git log` rather than invisible. **(2)** The reviewer argued a silently-fake safety gate outranks the freeze policy, so `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh:493` is patched too — but the obvious shape was wrong: `printf '%q'` is eval-safe yet backslash-escapes the space rather than removing it, so the preflight regex at `:511` still captured `.../GH\` and would have `die`d "script file does not exist", trading a false pass for a hard failure. Single-quoting is eval-safe *and* regex-tractable, and is byte-identical to `shlex.quote()`'s output for the same path; the preflight regex now matches a fully quoted token. `test/gh319-gate-path-with-space.sh` drives **both** lanes — the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` cases fail against pre-fix Bash (7/2) and pass after (9/0). **(3)** The proposed fix for the GH-293 guard-marker fragility required editing `relay-drive.sh`, a frozen twin, to satisfy a `[Should]` — the wrong trade; the manifest now matches the guard's user-facing **diagnostic** (`turn cannot report: relay file`), which does not get reflowed. The underlying point was sharper than the example: `test/gh293-vendored-guard-drift.sh` was itself restating the old literal, so a manifest change would have left the test green while the guard check was dead — the fixture now **derives** the pattern from `SAFETY_GUARD_PATTERNS` and asserts it stripped something (15/0). **(4)** Declined the suggestion to isolate `test/pdda-repo-contract.sh` from `validate.sh`: CI already fails the PR on those errors, so the coupling predates the change — what changed is finding out locally in 8 minutes instead of after a push, which is precisely what GH-311 exists to fix.
CHANGELOG.md-992-- **GH-319: every marathon phase reported "gate passed" without the gate ever running — the default gate word-split on the space in the repo's own path and executed an unrelated 0-byte file.** `utils/py/marathon_drive.py` built its default gate as an unquoted string (`f"bash {root}/validate.sh"`) and handed it to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. At a clone under `.../Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm` the shell split on the space and ran `bash $HOME/Documents/GH`, passing `Repos/.../validate.sh` as a positional argument. **`$HOME/Documents/GH` exists on this machine as a 0-byte file**, so bash executed an empty script: exit 0, no output, 0.0 s. Reproduced in isolation before anything was changed. **All four lanes of the 2026-07-27 gate-and-fleet-integrity marathon were approved with no gate**, while `bash validate.sh` on that exact tree was RED with two genuine failures (`relay-pkg-freshness`, `skill-extract` — GH-308's freeze banners had drifted `relay-pkg.tar.gz`). It was caught by timing, not by any signal the harness emits: `.tick/events/` showed **6.6 s and 7.5 s** between `agy-done` and `marathon.phase.approved` against a **483 s** real suite. **GH-238's gate-runnable preflight — which exists for exactly this — did not fire**, because its `^\s*(bash|/\S*/bash)\s+(\S+)` regex captured the same wrong fragment and `os.path.isfile()` on the decoy returned `True`; the guard and the gate agreed on the wrong file, and the preflight even carried quote-stripping logic for a quoted argument the default never produced. This is the third instance of one failure class in this program, after GH-315 (a stale relay token let a build-nothing run report success) and the sandboxed-`Monitor` liveness gap folded into GH-284 Phase 2: **a broken observation layer where failure is invisible and every available signal agrees.** Fixed with `shlex.quote` on the default path and `shlex.split` in the preflight, so the runnability check inspects the file the shell would actually execute. **Regression coverage was written to demonstrate the bug, not merely assert the fix** — `test/gh319-gate-path-with-space.sh` builds its fixture at a spaced path *and plants the same 0-byte decoy at the split point*, so a regression cannot hide behind a split prefix that happens not to exist; against pre-fix code the driver prints `phase p1 complete — STATUS: Approved, gate passed` and exits 0 while the fixture's gate exits 1 (4 pass / 2 fail), and post-fix it is 6/0 with the driver exiting 5. Registered in `validate.sh`. **Deliberately not fixed:** `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh:493` has the identical construction, but GH-308 froze that file in this same PR and AGENTS.md now directs behavior fixes to the Python twin — so an `XYZ_PYTHON=0` run at a spaced path still has a fake gate until GH-308 Phase 2 retires the twin. Historical marathon runs on this machine that reported "gate passed" are retroactively unverified; no audit of them is planned. Full `./validate.sh` 131/131, 0 FAIL lines, exit 0. → [GH-319-MARATHON-GATE-PATH-WORD-SPLIT.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-319-MARATHON-GATE-PATH-WORD-SPLIT.md) · [#319](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/319)
CHANGELOG.md:993:- **MARATHON-2026-07-27 (gate + fleet integrity) fired: 4 sequential lanes, all approved, PR #318.** `gh311 → gh289 → gh293 → gh308`, builder codex / reviewer agy throughout, 2 turns per lane (4 for gh293). Each deliverable was verified by direct inspection of the diff against its brief rather than by the runner's summary line — which is how GH-319 surfaced. **GH-311** adds `test/pdda-repo-contract.sh`, running `utils/pdda/pdda.sh run` against the repo's real docs so `validate.sh` becomes a superset of tier1's PDDA contract; it immediately earned its place by catching two real errors in this changelog's own capture doc (a hardcoded `$HOME` path and a missing ROADMAP pointer). **GH-289** widens GH-245's fast-refusal from `--review-once` to every `--target-root` turn, so a BUILD turn refuses at startup instead of completing and discarding its Log; the `--review-once` diagnostic is preserved verbatim. **GH-293** adds a behavior-marker safety-guard manifest to `xyz-sync check` (a missing guard is now distinguishable from ordinary provenance drift, inspected in the installed copy rather than inferred from `source_commit`) and makes `update --all` refuse a dirty or non-canonical harness source without `XYZ_SYNC_ALLOW_UNSAFE_SOURCE=1`. **GH-308 Phase 1** stamps FROZEN banners on the 11 Tier-A Bash twins and records the policy in AGENTS.md/UPGRADE.md — no deletions, `XYZ_PYTHON=0` still reversible, with `utils/marathon-plan.sh` and `relay-turn-lib.sh` explicitly exempt. `relay-pkg.tar.gz` rebuilt (the freeze banners drift it). → [MARATHON.yaml](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-2026-07-27-GATE-AND-FLEET-INTEGRITY/MARATHON.yaml) · [#318](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/318)
CHANGELOG.md-994-- **GH-312: `xyz-sync update` / `xyz-vendor.sh` silently destroyed the target repo's live runtime state — fixed by preserving it across the vendor swap, with three more at-risk paths than the report identified.** `materialize_vendor()` builds a staged mirror of the harness and swaps it in over an unconditional `rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR"`. The stage is mirrored purely from `$HARNESS_ROOT`, so everything the *target* accumulated at runtime was deleted unread — and since `ensure_gitignore` keeps `.xyz/` out of git, nothing under it was ever hashed into a git object, leaving **no reflog, stash, or `git fsck --lost-found` recovery**. It exited 0 and printed success. A real incident on 2026-07-27 destroyed a completed two-round Codex relay thread plus its full `.tick/` event log; the findings survived only because the Codex CLI transcripts happen to live in `$TMPDIR`, outside the harness. **The intake report's requested fix was incomplete:** it named `relay-system/`, `.tick/`, and `.relay-driver.lock`, but auditing what `.xyz/` actually accumulates (repo `.gitignore` + GH-75) turned up the completion-telemetry family — `XYZ.json` (the locked record array, 1.8 MB and actively written on the reporting machine), `XYZ.json.lock/` (its `mkdir` advisory lock), and `XYZ.heartbeat.json` — with **identical exposure**: none are in `VENDOR_DIRS`, so the stage never recreated them either. Implementing the report literally would have left the bug half-fixed; the shipped preserve list carries **six** paths, and a failed copy now `die`s *before* the destructive swap rather than proceeding. Preservation was chosen over a warning or a refusal because both still depend on an operator reading output at the right moment, and the docs frame `update` as deliberate (pinned + manual) but never as destructive. **Regression coverage was written first and observed failing** — new `test/gh312-vendor-preserves-state.sh` produced 6 failures against the pre-fix code and passes 14/14 post-fix — and it pins the *other* half of the contract too: VERSION must still restamp to live HEAD and `bin/tick` must survive, so a "fix" that preserved state by skipping the update cannot pass. It also covers the direct `xyz-vendor.sh` re-run over an existing `.xyz/`, which the capture flagged as an unverified open question and which had the same destructive swap (**answered: yes**). Docs: `xyz-sync.sh`'s header and `skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md` now state what `update` does to runtime state and that a new `.xyz/` artifact must join the preserve list. Reviewed by **agy** through a driven relay (`--review-once`, `ALLOW_PATHS=""`): Approved with 4 `[Pass]` findings and no defects raised — disclosed as a clean but shallow signal, not independent corroboration. `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` rebuilt via `make-pkg.sh` (the fix touches `relay-automation/`, which drifts the vendored tarball); `relay-pkg-freshness.sh` 3/3 and full `./validate.sh` green (10 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped). **Deliberately still open:** whether durable runtime state belongs under a disposable, gitignored `.xyz/` at all — the capture's own sharper question, listed in its `non_goals`, and **not** closed by this fix. → [GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-312-XYZ-SYNC-DESTROYS-STATE.md) · [#312](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/312)
CHANGELOG.md-995-- **GH-304: relay-drive turn-taker prompt + worktree seeding used a CWD-relative relay-file path — broke same-repo vendored `.xyz/` installs for Codex.** Scaffolding/driving a relay from CWD=`.xyz` (the relay-xyz skill's documented `cd "$HARNESS"`) with a CWD-relative `--relay-file` embedded that raw string in the turn-taker's prompt and used it for worktree seeding. Since a same-repo vendored `.xyz/` has no `.git` of its own, the turn-taker's worktree roots at the *outer* repo top-level, where `relay-system/…` doesn't exist (the file is at `.xyz/relay-system/…`) — a 100% failure for Codex, masked for agy (which absolutizes the path itself). Fix: `relay-drive.sh` and `utils/py/relay_drive.py` now **absolutize `$RELAY_FILE` before exporting it** to the turn-taker (mirrors the existing `--artifact-file` handling), so it resolves identically from any CWD; `rtl_turn_prompt` (`relay-turn-lib.sh`) derives the repo-root-relative EDIT path robustly (physical-path strip, matching `rtl_init`'s allowlist normalization) so the embedded path and the seeded path stay in lockstep at the true `.xyz/relay-system/…`. **Secondary:** when the relay file is gitignored (this repo gitignores parts of `relay-system/`), `rtl_enforce`'s empty-commit case now prints a distinct "relay file is gitignored, changes are NOT git-tracked (expected, not a stall)" message instead of the ambiguous "no tracked changes (token-only move?)" that a passing and a failing run printed byte-identically. Proof: new `test/gh304-vendored-relay-path.sh` (11/11) unit-tests the allowlist normalization, prompt path, worktree seeding, and both empty-commit messages; related relay/worktree tests green locally. → [#304](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/304)
CHANGELOG.md-996-- **GH-295: PR #302 tier1 CI — two real gaps found and fixed.** `test/pi-turn.sh`'s fake `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` test fixtures ("test-key"/"test-key-not-real") were never added to `security-scan-baseline.txt`, tripping the GH-64 active gate (same pattern already baselined for `aider-turn.sh`/`deep-research.sh`). Separately, `skills/relay-automation/relay-pkg.tar.gz` had drifted from an earlier README edit on this branch and was never rebuilt, tripping `test/relay-pkg-freshness.sh`. Both fixed; `security-scan.sh`/`relay-pkg-freshness.sh` green locally.
CHANGELOG.md-997-- **GH-300: swe-diagram search input no longer touches/overflows the font-picker when typing — two distinct bugs found and fixed, same symptom family.** **(1)** `.swe-search-input` uses `type="search"` but never reset `-webkit-appearance`, so WebKit's native searchfield cancel-button decoration could override the field's explicit 180px width once it had text — the renderer already ships its own custom `.swe-search-clear` button, making the native chrome pure downside. Fixed via `-webkit-appearance: none` + explicit `::-webkit-search-cancel-button`/`::-webkit-search-decoration` resets in `utils/swe-diagram/assets/template.html`. Not independently re-verified in Safari (no automation available in this environment) — a headless-Chrome regression check confirms no change there, since Chrome doesn't exhibit the underlying bug in the first place. **(2) Found on operator re-report** (the box still visibly touched the picker on the very first keystroke, no resize needed — but resizing afterward fixed it, the key clue): `positionPicker()` only ran on page load, font-picker change, and window resize — never on the search box's own `input` event — so when the custom clear button appeared (growing the right-anchored `.swe-search` row leftward), the picker never got told to move; a resize masked the bug by incidentally recomputing from the now-grown width. Fixed by having `renderer.js`'s search `input`/clear handlers dispatch a `swe-search-resize` event on the persistent `#diagram` node, which `template.html` listens for alongside its existing triggers. **Verified quantitatively, not just visually**: headless-Chrome bounding-rect measurement showed a healthy 8px gap before typing collapsing to a -22px overlap after typing (fix 1 alone), now a constant 8px with no resize needed — and since this is plain DOM sizing/event logic rather than a WebKit quirk, the Chrome verification here is directly conclusive. `test/swe-diagram.sh` 42/42 throughout; every `ARCHITECTURE/*.html` output rebuilt after each fix. → [GH-300-SWE-DIAGRAM-SEARCH-INPUT-OVERFLOW.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-300-SWE-DIAGRAM-SEARCH-INPUT-OVERFLOW.md) · [#300](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/300)

CHANGELOG.md-1007-- **GH-280: Aider+Qwen reliability investigation concluded — root cause found and fix confirmed.** A live GH-268 Wave-1 exercise against the real production repo and the real `qwen3.8-max-preview` endpoint caught the first real failure transcript of the whole investigation: Aider auto-selects `whole` edit format for unlisted/custom model ids, but Qwen emits standard unified diffs regardless, which Aider silently discards as "no tracked changes" — the actual explanation for the historical ~86% aider-qwen failure rate, not general model unreliability. Re-running with `AIDER_FLAGS="--edit-format diff"` forced took the same task from 0/3 real edits to a 90%-complete, correct implementation landing in round 1, confirming the fix. Getting to this transcript required first closing a real observability gap: `aider-turn.sh` (and, since `XYZ_PYTHON` defaults on, the actually-executing `utils/py/aider-turn.py` and `utils/py/agy-turn.py`) were never using the GH-161 persistent-log helper, so every prior investigation round genuinely could not have captured a failure log — fixed in [#288](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/288)/[#290](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/290). Also found and fixed along the way, independent of Qwen: a fully-retired OpenRouter default model id (`openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`) that silently broke any plain `aider`/`consult` call omitting both `AIDER_MODEL` and `AIDER_OPENAI_API_BASE` — [#291](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/pull/291), no separate issue filed. **Recommendation:** codex+agy remains the default builder pairing; Aider+Qwen is usable as a fallback with `--edit-format diff` and a generous timeout set explicitly. A separate, genuinely new gap was surfaced by the same session and filed on its own: `swarm-preflight.sh`'s suggested marathon invocations never default to `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=1` — [#294](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/294) (filed, not yet fired). → [GH-280 findings](PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-280-AIDER-QWEN-VS-SONNET-INVESTIGATION.md) · [marathon plan](PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-2026-07-23-GH279-GH280-AIDER-QWEN-FOLLOWUP.md) · [#280](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/280)

Doc-only; grounded against the working tree (`ls skills/ utils/`) and the capture docs, not memory.

CHANGELOG.md-1054-### Fixed
CHANGELOG.md:1055:- **GH-241: `MARATHON.example.yaml` now states that phases run strictly one at a time and that `depends_on` is scalar-only — docs-only; the report's first claim was partially falsified before the fix was scoped.** First bug filed *through* the new `/file-xyz-bug` skill (from `rebalance-OS`, vendored `.xyz/`), and the first to exercise the "verify the report, don't apply it" gate. **Claim (1) as filed — "nothing signals sequential execution", evidenced by a 0-match grep — does not hold:** line 3 already read "runs … **in depends_on order**; the chain **HALTS** on the first phase that fails". The grep was a false negative, searching the literal `"in order"` against the string `"in depends_on order"`. The DX complaint survives in a narrower form, which is what got fixed: the line documented *ordering* but not *exclusivity*, and "in depends_on order" is precisely how a dependency-ordered **parallel** scheduler (`make -j`) describes itself — so the new text states execution is strictly one-at-a-time and that `depends_on` **constrains** ordering rather than **creating** it, since restating "runs in order" would not move a reader who read that line and still concluded concurrency. **Claim (2) reproduced exactly** against a local two-phase fixture: `depends_on: [p1]` → `depends_on unknown phase '[p1]'`, scalar parses fine; root cause is the hand-rolled YAML reader not implementing flow sequences, so `[p1]` survives as a literal scalar into the phase-id lookup (`bin/marathon-yaml:102-105`). The field table now marks the field scalar-and-single with the exact failure text, and the header recommends `--dry-run` as the standard pre-fire step. **Consistency finding the issue didn't call out:** `depends_on` (scalar, single) and `artifact` (comma-separated, multi) are adjacent rows of the same field table carrying two different multiplicity conventions — `artifact` documented its own, `depends_on` did not, leaving the reader to infer from the neighbour. **Deliberately NOT taken: suggested fix (3)**, a `^\[.*\]$` guard in `bin/marathon-yaml` — that is a code change plus a regression test, not doc-only, and stays open as defence-in-depth (the docs fix stops the author writing the list form; the guard would catch the one who writes it anyway). Verified no runtime change: `node bin/marathon-yaml relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` emits a byte-identical phase table before and after; `relay-pkg-freshness` 3/3 (the example is not a vendored path). → [#241](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/241)
CHANGELOG.md-1056-
CHANGELOG.md-1057-### Added
CHANGELOG.md-1058-- **[GH-201](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/201) — `swe-diagram` Git-history lanes (2026-07-14).** Added `layout: "git-lanes"` for vertically stacked branch rows with commits ordered left-to-right, distinct ancestry/branch-cut/merge edges, compact commit cards, current-lane emphasis, search over Git metadata, and empty long-lived lane retention. A dependency-free local generator (`utils/swe-diagram/scripts/git-history-to-json.js`) reads local and remote-tracking branch refs and emits a capped, auditable diagram spec while documenting Git's inability to recover deleted branch names or squash/rebase provenance. Added a self-contained newest-20 example at `ARCHITECTURE/git-history-diagram.json`/`.html`. Verification: focused fixtures 29/29; Node syntax and skill validation; zero dangling endpoints; headless-Chrome inspection; and an independent 7-commit forward test with two branch cuts and two non-fast-forward merges. → [GH-201-SWE-DIAGRAM-GIT-LANES.md](PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-201-SWE-DIAGRAM-GIT-LANES.md)
CHANGELOG.md-1059-- **`/file-xyz-bug` — cross-repo bug front-door into this repo's `PROJECT/1-INBOX/`, QA'd by an agy `/relay-xyz` review (Approved, r3).** Lets a Claude Code session standing in *any other repo* file a harness bug where it will actually be triaged: harvest-first intake (reconstructs the failing command, error text, and caller repo from the live transcript before asking the operator anything, capped at 3 questions), a redaction step, one preview → one confirmation, then `gh issue create` + a `GH-<n>-*.md` capture + a `ROADMAP.md` queue park. Ships `find-xyz.sh`, a device-agnostic locator with no hardcoded machine path (env override → skill's own real location via symlink resolution → relay-xyz's `find-harness.sh` → current repo); it **deliberately rejects a vendored `.xyz/` copy**, which `find-harness.sh` prefers — a vendored copy has no `PROJECT/1-INBOX`, so a report filed there is unreadable. Two guardrails carry real incident weight: it writes **nothing** into the caller's repo (no breadcrumbs, no cached absolute paths), and it **never commits or pushes** the capture, because this clone is shared with marathon/relay drivers that can leave it dirty or parked on a `marathon/*` branch. **agy review (`relay-system/2026-07-18/file-xyz-bug-qa.md`): 3 `[Blocker]` + 2 `[Should]` + 1 `[Nit]` → 5 implemented, 1 declined on evidence.** Best catch: `$XYZ_*` exports from the locator don't survive to the next Claude Code Bash call (CWD persists, shell state does not), so a later `gh issue create --repo "$XYZ_SLUG"` would have expanded empty at the one moment it mattered — fixed with an explicit callout plus scrubbing all four bare references. **Declined** agy's third Blocker (that `status: Proposed (1-INBOX — not yet active)` violates a `status: Proposed` enum) as incorrect: no such enum exists — `PROJECT/PDDA.md:230` prescribes that exact string as the minimum frontmatter for a `GH-` inbox capture, `PDDA.md:456` documents `status:` as "free-text, unvalidated by design", and `GH-226` carries the long form in-tree; applying it would have moved the doc *away* from the contract. agy verified the citation and **retracted the finding** in r3. Also fixed by smoke-testing rather than review: `install.sh` reported success when `ln -s` failed under the Bash sandbox (`~/.claude` is write-denied), leaving the skill uninstalled while claiming otherwise. Locator verified from a foreign repo, a spaces-in-path repo, a non-git dir, and a bogus `XYZ_REPO` override; slug regex verified across all six GitHub URL forms.
--
